Convolutional networks are limited in modeling long range dependencies, whereas window-based Transformers establish global interactions only progressively with increasing depth. To address these limitations, a hybrid Mamba Transformer network is proposed for fringe to height regression. The network adopts a Swin based U shaped architecture and introduces visual state space modeling at the intermediate resolution encoder stage. An axial and dilated vision state space (ADVSS) block is further developed to enhance prescan feature encoding through local, dilated, and axial depthwise convolutions while retaining four directional selective scanning. This design combines linear complexity long range modeling with direction aware preservation of local fringe structures. Experiments on a publicly available FPP dataset show that the proposed method outperforms hNet, SwinConvUNet, UHRNet, and HiDNet in mean absolute error(MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), absolute relative error, and structural similarity index measure (SSIM). Using only one deformed fringe image, the proposed method achieves an RMSE of 0.548 mm and an SSIM of 0.9985, reducing RMSE by 65.2% and 59.6% relative to UHRNet and HiDNet, respectively. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining selective state space modeling with hierarchical window based attention for accurate single-shot FPP reconstruction.

papers.title: Momentum-selective graphene spectroscopy of moir\'e excitons
papers.abstract: Far-field photoluminescence probes only the light-cone corner of an exciton's momentum content, whereas energy transfer to nearby graphene integrates in-plane momenta up to the inverse spacer thickness $1/z$. For a WSe$_2$/MoSe$_2$ heterobilayer we build the transition polarization $\bm{P}_n(\qv)$ of each localized moir\'e exciton from the registry-dependent vector dipole texture and use each $\bm{P}_n$ for both baths. The two baths rank the states differently: the graphene-rate ratios differ from the optical ones, their ordering inverts with spacer thickness, and the distance exponents at $z=10$\,nm spread by more than two units. These ratios are independent of the transition-dipole prefactor. Within the $C_3$-symmetric leading-harmonic model the chiral $p_+$ and $d_-$ states are also dark at normal incidence yet transfer to graphene at rates comparable to the bright ground state. Their graphene rate depends on the sign of the texture phase, a quantity invisible in far-field emission, which we determine from first principles. In a device this prediction requires a splitting, larger than the symmetry-breaking mixing, that protects the chiral partners. Graphene proximity thus acts as a momentum-selective near-field probe of moir\'e excitons, and we propose its use as a practical spectroscopy.

papers.title: Fine points of the moduli space of cubic rational maps
papers.abstract: A rational point of the moduli space $\mathcal{M}_3$ of cubic rational maps is fine if its conjugacy class contains a map defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, and coarse otherwise. In the invariants $\xi_0,\dots,\xi_5$ that embed $\mathcal{M}_3$ in $\mathbb{P}(2,2,3,3,4,6)$, we prove that a point with trivial automorphism group is fine if and only if the quaternion algebra $(-m_{12},-2\xi_0)_{\mathbb{Q}}$ splits, where $m_{12}=\frac{1}{3}\xi_0^2\xi_1+\xi_0\xi_4-\xi_3^2$; we give the analogous criterion on the locus $\mathcal{L}_2$ of maps with an involution and show that all other strata are fine. The proof is constructive and yields an explicit descent. We prove that the obstruction class is unramified along every divisor of the compactification, that a prime $p\ge 5$ obstructs only if the point reduces modulo $p$ into the closure of one of the two codimension-two loci $\mathcal{L}_1$, $\mathcal{L}_2$ of maps with an involution, and that $\mathcal{M}_3$ has transverse $A_1$-singularities along both, above which the class ramifies; local densities predict that $\mathcal{L}_2$ is met modulo $p$ with probability $\asymp 1/p$, so that it carries the obstruction. A census of all 214,260,288 rational points of weighted moduli height at most 7 agrees with this mechanism and supports the conjecture that the proportion of fine points tends to zero like $(\log B)^{-1/2}$.

papers.title: Properties of Oxygen-rich Asymptotic Giant Branch stars in the LMC and the Milky Way
papers.abstract: We investigate the properties of oxygen-rich asymptotic giant branch (OAGB) stars in the LMC and the Milky Way using infrared (IR) color-magnitude diagrams, two-color diagrams, spectral energy distributions (SEDs), and variability data. The observed SEDs are analyzed with radiative transfer models to constrain the properties of the central stars and their circumstellar dust shells and to estimate distances. For OAGB stars in the LMC, whose distance is well established, a set of representative OAGB models is derived by fitting theoretical SEDs to the observations. These models are subsequently applied to Galactic OAGB stars, for which Gaia DR3 parallaxes are often uncertain, to estimate distances from SED fitting. For Galactic Mira variables, distances are also determined using a period-magnitude relation calibrated with Mira stars in the LMC. We find that OAGB stars in the two galaxies exhibit broadly similar IR properties, and that the theoretical models successfully reproduce the observed IR characteristics, despite the extreme rarity of heavily obscured objects with optically thick silicate dust envelopes in the LMC. We further examine Galactic OAGB stars associated with OH, H2O, and SiO masers, including the relationship between absolute OH maser fluxes and IR colors. In addition, we investigate the IR properties of Mira-type OAGB stars and characterize their long-term variability using archival observations together with 16 years of WISE photometric data. Finally, we present a new catalog of 70,877 Galactic OAGB stars, providing a more reliable and comprehensive dataset for future studies.

papers.title: On the elliptic Hall category
papers.abstract: In this paper we study (the positive half of) the elliptic Hall category, a categorical version of the elliptic Hall algebra. Our main result is a computation of categorical versions of the generators in the coherent realization of the elliptic Hall category, i.e., via coherent sheaves on commuting stacks for $\operatorname{GL}_n\times \mathfrak{gl}_n$: we realize them as Hodge associated graded sheaves of certain twisted equivariant $D$-modules on the groups $\operatorname{GL}_n$.

papers.title: Transport by rough vector fields
papers.abstract:
The Cauchy-Lipschitz theorem guarantees that the ODE $\dot\gamma = b(t,\gamma)$ is well-posed if $b$ is Lipschitz in space, an assumption too restrictive for applications such as fluid mechanics. In 1989, DiPerna and Lions extended the theory to Sobolev vector fields with bounded divergence. Well-posedness then holds not for individual trajectories but for regular Lagrangian flows: flows that solve the ODE for almost every initial point and compress volume by at most a bounded factor. Their method rests on renormalized solutions of the associated transport equation.
  This thesis is primarily expository: it presents the DiPerna-Lions theory with detailed proofs. We treat existence, uniqueness and stability of weak and renormalized solutions of the transport equation, deduce existence (for autonomous fields) and uniqueness of regular Lagrangian flows, and discuss applications to the two-dimensional Euler equations. Three counterexamples with divergence-free fields show that uniqueness can fail without a growth condition at infinity, if $b$ has only fractional Sobolev regularity (due to DiPerna and Lions), or for $L^1$ solutions when $\nabla b \in L^r$, $r<d$ (the simplest case of a recent construction by Bru\`e, Colombo and Kumar).
  Contributions are (1) smooth approximations of $b$ with uniformly bounded divergence for the existence proof; (2) a direct proof of the known uniqueness of regular Lagrangian flows from uniqueness for the continuity equation; (3) a construction of the auxiliary cube-translating field in the example of Bru\`e, Colombo and Kumar that works for all $d \ge 2$, replacing an extension from two dimensions that is not a vector field on $\mathbb R^d$ for $d \ge 3$.

papers.title: SGL: Towards a Bridging Model for Heterogeneous Hierarchical Platforms
papers.abstract: This paper introduces the Scatter-Gather parallel-programming and parallel-execution model in the form of a simple imperative Scatter-Gather Language (SGL). Its design is based on past experience with bulk-synchronous parallel (BSP) programming and BSP language design. SGL's novel features are motivated by the last decade's move towards multi-level and heterogeneous parallel architectures involving multi-core processors, graphics accelerators and hierarchical routing networks in the largest multiprocessing systems. The design of SGL is coherent with L. Valiant's Multi-BSP while offering a programming interface that is even simpler than the primitives of Bulk-Synchronous Parallel ML (BSML). SGL appears to cover a large subset of all BSP algorithms while avoiding complex message-passing programming. Like all BSP-inspired systems, it supports predictable, portable and scalable performance. Moreover, SGL's explicit data distribution will allow automatic or programmable load-balancing.

papers.title: A variational model with finite carrying capacity for segregated multi-species populations in the whole Euclidean space
papers.abstract: We study a variational problem motivated by models of multiple segregated species in a nonhomogeneous environment. The analysis combines tools from potential theory, in particular free boundary methods. The main novelty is that we formulate the variational problem in the whole Euclidean space while imposing a finite carrying capacity constraint, which allows us to investigate saturated regions where the species attain their maximal density. In addition, we provide a modeling interpretation of the constrained energy. We show that it arises as the variational limit of energies with increasingly strong crowding and interspecific competition penalties, in the sense that, regardless of their relative rates, every sequence of minimizers of the penalized energies admits a subsequence that converges strongly to a minimizer of the constrained energy.

papers.title: Detecting and Understanding Ambiguity in Visualizations with Role-Playing Vision Language Model Interpretations
papers.abstract: Communicative visualizations can support multiple chart-grounded takeaways, including divergent or conflicting ones; we refer to this variation as interpretive ambiguity. Such ambiguity can undermine a visualization's communicative goal when the supported takeaways diverge from its intended message. Evaluating visualizations with target audiences can surface this variation, but such evaluations can be costly and difficult to scale. In this work, we explore persona-conditioned Vision Language Models (VLMs) as a complementary evaluation tool for interpretive ambiguity. For a given visualization, our pipeline uses topic-relevant personas to elicit candidate contextual takeaways supported by interpretations of perceived visual patterns, such as trends and clusters. We derive a Target--Pattern--Scope framework for comparing these interpretations, use LLM judges to assign Compatible, Disjoint, or Opposing ambiguity labels to statement pairs, and summarize their distribution in an ambiguity profile. To improve chart grounding, we benchmark candidate VLMs on chart comprehension and select the highest-performing model for each chart type. We evaluate statement-pair labeling against human-authored annotations and apply the approach to real-world, public-facing visualizations curated from established datasets. Through case studies, we examine how perceived visual patterns relate to contextual takeaways and how a visualization redesign changes the sampled interpretations. Our findings show how persona-conditioned VLMs can complement human feedback by generating candidate contextual takeaways and surfacing potential ambiguity for further inspection.

papers.title: Sharp Quantitative Weighted Estimates for Lifted Maximal Operators with Applications
papers.abstract: In this article, we establish sharp quantitative weighted estimates for the lifted Hardy--Littlewood (resp Sobolev sharp) maximal operators $\{\mathcal M_\theta\}_{\theta\in(0,\infty)}$ (resp $\{\mathcal M_\theta^\sharp\}_{\theta\in(0,\infty)}$). Specifically, for $p\in(1,\infty)$, $\gamma\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, $\upsilon\in A_p$, and $f\in L^p_\upsilon$, we prove that \begin{align*} \sup_{\theta,\lambda\in(0,\infty)}\lambda^p \underset{\mathcal M_\theta(f)(x,t)>\lambda t^\gamma} {\int_{\mathbb R^n}\int_0^\infty} t^{\gamma p-1}\,dt\,\upsilon(x)\,dx \lesssim [\upsilon]_{A_p}^{\alpha_{p,\gamma}} \|f\|_{L^p_\upsilon}^p, \end{align*} where $\alpha_{p,\gamma}:=\frac{p}{p-1}$ for $\gamma\in[-n,0)$ and $\alpha_{p,\gamma}:=1$ otherwise and where the implicit positive constant depends only on $n$, $p$, and $\gamma$. For $\mathcal M_\theta^\sharp$, the corresponding estimate holds with $\|f\|_{L^p_\upsilon}^p$ replaced by $\|\nabla f\|_{L^p_\upsilon}^p$ for any $f\in\dot W^{1,p}_\upsilon$, and with $\alpha_{p,\gamma}:=\frac{p}{p-1}$ for $\gamma\in[-1,0)$ and $\alpha_{p,\gamma}:=1$ otherwise. We show that, for an $A_1$ weight $\upsilon$, the weight constant in the above estimates becomes $[\upsilon]_{A_1}$ for the sharp ranges $p\in(1,\infty)$ and $\gamma\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, or $p=1$ and $\gamma\in\mathbb R\setminus[-n,0]$ (resp. $\gamma\in\mathbb R\setminus[-1,0]$). We also prove that $\alpha_{p,\gamma}$ is sharp, and we establish exact limiting formulae and characterize Muckenhoupt weights via weak-type bounds. As applications, we characterize the weighted Hardy(--Sobolev) space $H^1_\upsilon$ with $\upsilon\in A_1$ in terms of the truncated Riesz transforms with optimal range $\gamma\in \mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$. More applications include the sharp weighted Caffarelli--Silvestre extension and the generalization to ball Banach function spaces.

papers.title: Maximal Spaceability of the set of non-absolutely summing operators in quasi-Banach spaces
papers.abstract: For every $0<p<1$, we establish maximal spaceability of the bounded operators on $\ell_p$ which fail to be $(r,s)$-absolutely summing for all $1\le s\le r<\infty$, using the coordinate-disjointization construction and Maddox's theorem. We give detailed isometric estimates and prove a corresponding maximal spaceability theorem inside the compact operators. The compact result is based on an explicit diagonal multiplier and a single weakly $1$-summable sequence witnessing the simultaneous failure of all admissible absolute summability conditions. A diagonal characterization, a logarithmic compact example, and extensions to operators with values in quasi-Banach spaces containing a copy of $\ell_p$ are also obtained. The constructed subspaces are isomorphic to $\ell_p$ and have maximal algebraic dimension whenever the ambient operator spaces have dimension $\mathfrak c$.

papers.title: Regularity and selfless cp maps
papers.abstract: We investigate the regularity properties of C*-algebras admitting a weakly selfless unital completely positive map.

papers.title: Observational evidence of the Gaia-Enceladus-Sausage merger's influence on the opposite side of the Galactic Center
papers.abstract: The Gaia-Enceladus-Sausage (GES) merger, which occurred approximately 8-11 Gyr ago, is a key event that shaped the Galactic inner halo. Its remnants have been studied extensively and are known to dominate the halo on the Near-side of the Galactic Center (GC), i.e. the side facing the Sun, but systematic evidence for whether the Far-side (the side beyond the GC as seen from the Sun) is similarly affected has been lacking. Using 14,056 red giant stars selected from SMSS DR4 and Gaia DR3 through stringent quality cuts, we compare the metallicity distributions, velocity-space distributions, velocity dispersions, anisotropy parameters, and action-space properties of the Near- and Far-sides. We find clear observational evidence for the influence of GES on the Far-side: it hosts the same metal-rich component peaked at [Fe/H] ~ -1.4, and its metal-rich population (-1.7 < [Fe/H] <= -1.3) shows GES-typical features consistent with the Near-side, namely a "sausage"-shaped velocity distribution and a velocity anisotropy as high as beta ~ 0.8-0.9. Action-space analysis shows that 10.86% +/- 0.23% of Far-side stars carry the GES dynamical imprint, consistent with 11.56% +/- 0.16% on the Near-side. The Far-side shows a residual prograde rotation that persists under increasingly aggressive disk-removal cuts, indicating a genuine kinematic signal rather than disk contamination, and a battery of robustness tests confirms that the symmetry is not an artifact of measurement uncertainties, residual disk contamination, or incomplete Sagittarius-stream removal. These results demonstrate that GES shaped the entire inner halo (r < 28 kpc) globally and symmetrically, with its imprint clearly present on the Far-side as well as the Near-side.

papers.title: Extreme proxies for causal identification: deconfounding with outliers
papers.abstract: Causal identification under unobserved confounding typically relies on additional structure, such as a valid instrument or proxy variables. We show that heavy tailed variables offer an alternative route to identification by revealing treatment variation for which confounding becomes asymptotically negligible. Our key assumption is extreme propagation: when an unobserved confounder takes an extreme value, some observed variable in the system (called a safeguard) will become extreme with large probability. This way, selecting extreme treatment observations while safeguards remain non-extreme makes confounding asymptotically negligible relative to the treatment. We call this certification. We derive graphical conditions specifying which latent confounders must be monitored by safeguards and distributional conditions ensuring effective certification. The framework includes valid-instrument and double-proxy structures as special cases, as well as confounded instruments that are invalid in most approaches that do not exploit heavy tails. Geometrically, certification isolates the extremal ray whose slope equals the causal effect. This connects causal identification with multivariate extreme-value geometry and motivates a family of novel simple estimators. Simulations demonstrate performance gains under nonlinear confounding and heavy tails, while revealing limitations in light-tailed regimes (where cancellation can conceal extreme confounding from the safeguards). We validate our methodology in simulation studies and by recovering the ground-truth flow in a river discharge application.

papers.title: Garlic in a Box: I2P Network Emulator
papers.abstract: The Invisible Internet Project (I2P) is a peer-to-peer anonymity network whose routing and peer-selection mechanics underlie a growing family of state-sponsored covert relay architectures. Studying these mechanics demands a controlled, reproducible environment. We present Garlic-in-a-Box, an installable emulator that deploys a fully isolated network of unmodified I2P Java routers on a single host or cluster of hosts. Each router runs in its own Linux network namespace. A filesystem bootstrap removes the dependency on signed reseed servers, and synthetic geographic diversity activates the same location-aware peer-selection code paths present on the live network. A fifty-router deployment across five geographic locations stabilises in about twenty-five minutes and uses roughly 21 GB of memory. To demonstrate the platform's value, we model I2P peer selection as a two-stage process and conduct a reputation attack. Across five independent trials, the attack promotes the adversary into the victim's eligible selection set with perfect consistency, and the adversary is chosen for 1.38x more tunnels than matched controls. The platform and its measurement pipeline are released to support reproducible I2P security research and hands-on cyber-defence training.

papers.title: InferScale: Kubernetes-Native Predictive Autoscaling for SLO-Aware AI Inference
papers.abstract: Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) is widely used for inference services, but reactive scaling is often too slow when pods take tens of seconds to become ready. The problem gets worse in shared clusters, where independent HPAs compete for the same resource budget and can hurt different tenants from run to run. We present InferScale, a Kubernetes-native autoscaler that combines inference-aware signals, short-horizon demand prediction, SLO-state control, fast-path spike handling, and tenant-priority headroom without replacing the default scheduler. We evaluate InferScale on Azure Kubernetes Service in two settings. On a real ResNet-50 ONNX workload with 21-second cold start, repeated ramp-burst runs improve SLO compliance from 47.8% +/- 1.5% under a stronger external-metric HPA to 65.3% +/- 9.0% under InferScale. In repeated controlled multi-tenant contention experiments, InferScale cuts Gold-tier SLO standard deviation from 16.1 to 1.2 percentage points and makes contention outcomes follow the priority policy more closely. Repeated single-service ablations show 6-8 percentage point degradation, with an exploratory priority ablation showing a 27-point drop under contention. The main takeaway is that, in startup-sensitive inference serving, the practical value of prediction lies less in precise forecasting than in moving the controller early enough to offset cold-start delay.

papers.title: Integrable distortion II: the p-Weil-Petersson variational problem
papers.abstract:
We study the hyperbolically weighted distortion energies \[
  \mathcal{I}_p(f)=\int_\mathbb{D}
  \frac{|\mu_f|^p}{(1-|\mu_f|^2)^{\max\{2,p\}/2}}\,dA_\eta \] for finite-distortion disk homeomorphisms with prescribed boundary values, together with the associated inverse problem in the monotone Sobolev class. For $1<p\leq2$, the inverse density is polyconvex precisely when $p\geq p_{\mathrm c}=1+1/\sqrt2$. In this range, quasisymmetric data with finite-energy monotone barriers yield minimisers with holomorphic Ahlfors--Hopf differentials and strong local Sobolev convergence of minimising subsequences.
  For $p_{\mathrm c}<p<2$, a finite-energy finite-distortion barrier yields a unique absolute monotone minimiser, which is a quasiconformal diffeomorphism and is asymptotically conformal. Together with the boundary-class theorem of Part~I, this characterises the admissible boundary data as $T^p$. The proof combines a selected barrier approximation, uniform scalar gradient estimates and a weighted Reich--Strebel comparison.
  For $1<p<p_{\mathrm c}$, finite rank-one comparisons bound distortion on the positive-Jacobian set by a cutoff strictly below the ellipticity cutoff. An attained monotone minimum is either a quasiconformal diffeomorphism or has nonzero rank-one derivatives on a set of positive area. For $0<p\leq1$, minimisers with finite distortion, or homeomorphic minimisers with a locally Sobolev inverse, are M\"obius maps. We also obtain energy-dependent quasiconformal bounds for regular minimisers when $p>2$. \

papers.title: Partial Modal Tensor Regression
papers.abstract: With the rapid development of modern scientific research, tensor data have become increasingly prevalent across a wide range of fields. How to effectively characterize the relationship between tensor predictors and a response while preserving the intrinsic structure of tensor data has therefore become an important problem in high-dimensional statistical analysis. Existing tensor regression methods mainly focus on conditional means or conditional quantiles. When the response distribution is asymmetric, heavy-tailed, or contaminated by outlying observations, the conditional modal provides a robust and interpretable alternative characterization. In this paper, we propose a partial modal tensor regression (PMTR) method. The proposed method constructs the partial modal tensor covariance, which incorporates information on the conditional modal to guide tensor dimension reduction, and subsequently establishes a modal tensor regression model in the reduced tensor space. This strategy alleviates the dimensionality burden caused by direct vectorization while preserving the intrinsic structural information of tensor predictors. Under suitable regularity conditions, we establish the consistency and asymptotic properties of the proposed estimators and employ a data-driven dimension-selection procedure to determine the effective dimension along each tensor mode.

papers.title: A class of Niho type four-valued cross-correlation functions between sequences of different periods
papers.abstract: Determining the cross-correlation distributions between $m$-sequences and their decimated sequences is an important problem in sequence design. For two positive integers $n$ and $k$ with $n=2k$, this paper investigates the cross-correlation function between a binary $m$-sequence $\{u(t)\}$ of period $2^{n}-1$ and its $2^{\gcd(s,k)}+1$ short-period decimated sequences $\{u(dt+l)\}$, where the decimation $d=\frac{2^s}{2^s+1}(2^k-1)+1$ satisfies $1<s<n$ and $v_2(s)>v_2(k)$. The cross-correlation function is proved to be four-valued and its value distribution is completely determined. Several previously known binary cross-correlation functions are included in our result as special cases.

papers.title: Reversible Pseudonymisation of Documents Sent to External LLMs: an Open Bilingual Benchmark and an Engine
papers.abstract: Professionals send working documents to external large language models. A common safeguard is reversible pseudonymisation: personal data are replaced with placeholders before the request and restored locally in the answer. We present an open benchmark of five existing open tools and a regular-expression baseline on Russian and UK English, and an open engine built on the two strongest tools. The benchmark excludes each tool's own authors' dataset from its verdict, compares the engine with each tool on identical datasets for detection, reports masking precision, and tests on a held-out set of synthetic documents whose files, hashes, decision rules, run plan and stopping rule were published before any run. Two local LLMs test whether placeholders survive. All evaluation data are synthetic, and the benchmark was run by the author of the engine; code, data, predictions and raw answers are released. On external datasets no existing tool meets all predefined thresholds: in UK English the identifier and leak thresholds are not met, in Russian the identifier threshold is borderline. On the last held-out set of 1,000 documents per language, the best existing tools leave a whole value visible in 61% (Russian) and 58% (UK) of documents. On these documents, from the generator it was developed on, the engine does so in 0.3% [0.1; 0.9] and 0.2% [0.1; 0.7], leaves any part of a value visible in 0.8% and 0.2%, and meets all detection thresholds in both languages. In UK English it also restores at least 99% of its placeholders after 760 answers. In Russian it restores only 94.6% [93.6; 95.6] of name placeholders, against a 99% threshold, mainly because the inflection it borrows from pii-guard produces wrong surname forms. The engine was developed over six earlier held-out sets from the same generator; real documents were not tested.

papers.title: The Patient Is Always Right? Evaluating Sycophancy in Medical Diagnosis with Graded Patient Beliefs
papers.abstract: More people are seeking out general-purpose AI models for medical advice, including diagnosis. Yet, AI models are susceptible to sycophancy, like validating users' beliefs even when they are untrue, which could lead to false positive diagnoses. Here, we evaluate how nine AI models change their diagnostic decision when a patient presents a belief that they have a specific (but incorrect) medical condition. We vary how close the user belief is to the clinical evidence presented. Models sycophantically adopt the patient's belief on average 23.2\% of the time---sometimes even when the patient proposes a fictional, made-up condition. We also varied different personas, including a Rare Disease Claimer that got models to accept their belief 43.0\% of the time. Additional analyses find that medical fine-tuning and model scale makes models less susceptible to changing their diagnoses. Sycophantic bias in medical diagnosis raises implications for safety, especially as more people are using AI for health support.

papers.title: Two-dimensional framework for modeling load transfer in nanocomposites with thin, stiff, and prestressed reinforcements
papers.abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for simulating load-transfer mechanisms in nanocomposites reinforced by thin, stiff, and prestressed reinforcements, such as, e.g., nanosheets or nanoplatelets. The reinforcements are modeled as open material surfaces treated as membranes endowed with their own elastic properties and residual surface tension; the matrix is assumed to be isotropic elastic. In the two-dimensional plane-strain setting considered here, each material surface is represented by a sufficiently smooth curve of otherwise arbitrary shape. The theoretical part of the framework is based on the Gurtin--Murdoch theory in which the surfaces are represented by traction jumps across them. The elastic fields in the matrix are exactly expressed by the integral representations written in terms of the unknown traction jumps that are functions of the second-order derivatives of the displacements. The computational part is based on the isogeometric boundary element method (IGABEM) that utilizes non-uniform rational B-splines (NURBS). The unknown traction jumps are found from the numerical solutions of the coupled system of singular boundary integral equations, after which the elastic fields in the matrix are evaluated. The procedure of extracting the values of the stress intensity factors (SIFs) at the tips of the surfaces is described. The proposed algorithm is validated against available benchmark solutions for multiple surfaces located along either straight segments or circular arcs. Selected parametric studies are performed to examine the influence of surface curvatures, relative spacing, orientation, and interactions. An example involving a graphene nanoplatelet-reinforced epoxy is presented.

papers.title: MDS codes containing a fixed subcode over finite field extensions
papers.abstract: Let $2\le k\le n$ and let $U\le\mathbb{F}_q^n$ be a fixed $(k-1)$-dimensional linear code. We study the $[n,k]$ maximum distance separable (MDS) codes over finite extensions of $\mathbb{F}_q$ that contain the scalar extension of $U$. Our approach constructs an auxiliary linear code from \(U\). Its full-weight words characterize the desired MDS completions. We prove that \(U\) admits an \([n,k]\) MDS completion over some finite extension of \(\mathbb{F}_q\) if and only if \(d(U)\ge n-k+1\). When this condition holds, the number of these MDS codes over $\mathbb{F}_{q^m}$ is \[\#\left\{W\le\mathbb{F}_{q^m}^n:U\otimes_{\mathbb{F}_q}\mathbb{F}_{q^m}\subseteq W,\ \dim_{\mathbb{F}_{q^m}} W=k,\ W\text{ is MDS}\right\}=\frac{\chi_{\delta_GM(G)}(q^m)}{q^m-1},\] where $G$ is a generator matrix of $U$, $\delta_GM(G)$ is its represented derived matroid, and $\chi_{\delta_GM(G)}$ is its characteristic polynomial. In particular, the formula determines existence over each extension field and the least extension degree for which such an MDS code exists. Examples show that these counts may distinguish different representations of the same column matroid, while monomially inequivalent codes may have identical counts over every finite extension.

papers.title: Hyponormal and subnormal dual Toeplitz operators
papers.abstract: In this paper, we completely characterize hyponormal dual Toeplitz operators with general bounded measurable symbols by using the Douglas theorem in [R. G. Douglas, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 17 (1966), 413-415]. As an application, the hyponormality of dual Toeplitz operators with radial symbols and polynomial symbols in $z$ and $\bar{z}$ is characterized concretely. Moreover, we obtain complete characterizations for both subnormal dual Toeplitz operators with harmonic polynomial symbols and $\varTheta$-class dual Toeplitz operators with bounded harmonic symbols.

papers.title: The golden cage of science: first-last author prestige gap buys impact over disruption
papers.abstract: First and last authors make critical but distinct contributions in the majority of scientific papers. First authors tend to conduct research and analysis, whereas last authors are usually responsible for setting research directions and providing resources and supervision. The first-last author prestige gap (FL gap, $\Delta H$) is defined as the H-index difference between the last and first authors prior to the focal paper's publication. The FL gap serves as a measure of the prestige asymmetry between the two dominant collaborators. We find that larger FL gaps in either direction are associated with higher impact and lower disruption. This trade-off is robust across team sizes and intensities of prior collaboration and can not be explained by first and last authors' separate prestige effects or their academic age gap. Further analysis shows that variation in last author prestige is associated with larger differences in both the article's impact and disruption than variation in first author prestige. We refer to this coexistence of higher impact and lower disruption related to the FL gap as the ``golden cage of science'', which reflects a common collaboration structure that statistically produces highly cited but less disruptive work. These findings suggest the first-last author prestige gap as an important indicator for examining how research teams balance senior guidance with exploratory autonomy.

papers.title: Deep Scientific Reasoning under Physical Constraints: Structure-Aware Spectrum Prediction
papers.abstract: Structured scientific spectra encode rich physical information while obeying hard constraints, such as conservation laws and characteristic spectral geometry. Accurate prediction of these spectra is central to materials discovery, yet existing methods often treat them as unconstrained sequences and therefore fail to enforce the underlying physical structure. Taking electronic density of states (eDOS) as the prototypical example, we introduce DeepSciReasoner, a general paradigm for predicting scientific spectra under physical constraints. The framework combines structure-aware spectrum decoding with constraint-preserving physical reasoning, allowing predictions to capture rich spectral structure while respecting the underlying physics. We evaluate DeepSciReasoner on eDOS, phonon density of states (phDOS), X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES), and Raman spectra, where it substantially improves prediction accuracy while maintaining physical consistency. These results establish DeepSciReasoner as a reusable blueprint for structured scientific spectrum prediction under hard physical constraints.

papers.title: Derived products and completion defects of inverse limits
papers.abstract: We compute derived products and inverse limits in Grothendieck categories by exact coresolutions. For the product of $r$ doubled affine lines over $B[s]$, where $B$ is any nonzero commutative ring,the exact dimensions of products, epimorphic countable limits, and arbitrary countable limits are $r$, $r$, and $r+1$. We identify the top derived functors for every $B$-module of coefficients. Both obstruction modules contain the countable reduced product as a natural $B$-module direct summand, and a formal-series map relates them by an explicit cokernel sequence. A relative cofree coresolution gives degree shifts over an arbitrary Grothendieck category and computes the localization defect for arbitrary locally nilpotent diagrams. We also construct transfinite scalar extensions preserving a prescribed kernel and its derived limit;these give nonzero completion defects beyond any fixed ordinal.The general epimorphic top-degree vanishing question is not settled by these constructions.

papers.title: Uniqueness of radial bound states for an equation with an odd cubic-like nonlinearity
papers.abstract:
We investigate radial bound states with prescribed nodes for the odd cubic equation \[
  \Delta u+u(\abs{u}-b)(c-\abs{u})=0
  \quad\text{in }\R^n,\qquad n\ge2,\quad 0<b<c. \] Writing $a=b/c$, we prove that a radial bound state with exactly $k\ge1$ simple zeros and positive central value exists if and only if $0<a<1/2$. For each $k$, this solution is unique for all $0<a<1/2$ in dimension two, for $a\ge(7-3\sqrt5)/2$ in dimension three, and for $a\ge(43-5\sqrt{33})/32$ in dimension four. For one node, we identify exact ranges obtained from a tangent comparison and a quotient inequality in every dimension $n\ge3$; the threshold is dimension-independent for $3\le n\le23$ and is characterized implicitly for $n\ge24$. These results address the natural odd counterpart of the cubic nonlinearity highlighted in Tang's prescribed-node uniqueness conjecture [M. Tang, \emph{Invent. Math.}, 2026]. The main challenges are the second positive zero of the cubic source, the lack of a global comparison inequality, and supercritical cubic growth in higher dimensions. We overcome them by an amplitude confinement argument, controlled extensions preserving sharp comparison estimates, and a subcritical truncation for existence. A complementary small-$a$ uniqueness range in dimensions three to five follows from a recent massive double-power result.

papers.title: Designing sustainability under Earth-system rate constraints
papers.abstract: Sustainability debates are monopolized by quantities: total energy use, material stocks, or recycling volumes. These metrics are informative, but they obscure a more fundamental constraint. On a materially closed but energetically open Earth, long-term viability is governed by rates: power density, areal power density, and the rate at which dispersed materials can be repurified under dif- fuse solar fluxes. We develop a physical framework that links technological metabolism, material dilution, and recycling limits through these rate con- straints. This perspective clarifies why many contemporary technologies remain viable only through stock drawdown and high-power buffering, and why green growth strategies often shift rather than resolve the underlying mismatch between industrial activity and Earth-system dynamics. We argue that long-term sustain- ability requires both quantitative reduction in aggregate industrial throughput toward rate-bounded regimes and the development of technologies qualitatively compatible with biospheric operating conditions.

papers.title: When Does GEPA Merge Help? A Mechanism-Level Diagnostic
papers.abstract: GEPA is among the strongest reflective prompt optimizers for language-model programs, but its system-aware merge operator is unstable across models: merge improves gpt-4.1-mini on average while degrading Qwen3-8B, an asymmetry noted but left unexplained by the GEPA paper. We investigate this instability across five datasets and two models. Our nine-configuration sweep over merge timing and merge operator shows that merge can improve both models when configured appropriately. This suggests that merge instability is better explained by configuration sensitivity than by an inherent flaw in the merge operator. We then test whether prompt-level features predict GEPA's merge-accept decisions and find that they do not, ruling out static-feature gating. As a proof of concept, a behavior-based probe built from these diagnostics avoids large merge failures in our multi-seed runs by abstaining on high-risk tasks, although it does not consistently outperform NoMerge. Code is available as GEPA-MergeProbe at https://github.com/ChongZZZZ/GEPA_MERGE .

papers.title: Explaining Navigation Decisions: Stage-Aware Visual Attribution for Vision-Language Navigation
papers.abstract: As Vision-Language Models (VLMs) increasingly enable robots to follow language instructions, understanding their navigation decisions becomes important for reliable deployment. Existing explainability methods overlook a key challenge in Vision-Language Navigation (VLN): evidence for the current action may be distributed across historical and current observations and associated with different instruction stages. We identify instruction-stage insensitivity, where existing methods produce similar explanations despite changes across different navigation stages. To address this issue, we propose a stage-aware attribution framework for VLN. We first construct action-conditioned temporal instruction--visual attributions across observations. These attributions are projected into instruction space to estimate stage associations, which guide the aggregation of relevant historical evidence for refining the current explanation. An instruction-guided spatial filter further suppresses isolated responses while preserving compact, instruction-relevant regions. Experiments across multiple VLN policies and benchmarks show improved attribution quality over existing methods. We further demonstrate that our method acts as a diagnostic tool for analyzing failure cases, and validate its applicability to real-world navigation on a Unitree G1 robot.

papers.title: TCSP3.0: Template-Based Crystal Structure Prediction with Coefficient-Preserving Element Substitution and Structural Diversity
papers.abstract: Template-based crystal structure prediction (CSP) transfers a known crystal structure to a new composition by element substitution, so its accuracy depends on retrieving suitable templates, mapping elements and ranking the resulting candidates correctly. Auditing the original TCSP2.0 implementation on the T180 benchmark, we found that 469 of its 2,347 selected structures (20%) have the wrong composition, caused by element mappings that ignore stoichiometric coefficients and by sequential text substitution that cascades or corrupts element symbols. We propose TCSP3.0, which enforces coefficient-preserving mappings, substitutes species simultaneously on parsed structures and validates every candidate's composition and cell. It further adds periodic-number retrieval, soft oxidation-state evidence, radius-compatibility scoring, structural deduplication, and ORB-v3 machine-learning-potential relaxation and energy ranking of its candidates, as used by deep generative CSP baselines. TCSP3.0 achieves Top-1 and Top-20 match rates of 72.2% and 90.6% on T180, compared with 28.3% and 45.6% for TCSP2.0, and a Top-20 match rate of 74.0% on a new 800-target benchmark (T800). On T180 it also outperforms PNcsp+ and deep generative models CrystalFlow and MaskGXT (Top-1 72.2% versus at most 63.9%). Even without relaxation, TCSP3.0 reaches 67.8% at Top-1 and 90.6% at Top-20 in a median of 28 s per target on two CPU cores, about ten times faster than CrystalFlow. Paired ten-arm ablations on T180 and T800 show that most of the improvement comes from the correctness fixes; structural deduplication significantly improves the Top-5 match rate, embedding-based retrieval is required for coverage, and the remaining scoring features have small or null effects.

papers.title: Atmospheric Turbulence Profiling in the Lenghu Site Area Using MERRA-2 Data
papers.abstract: The Lenghu site, in the Saishiteng Mountains of the northern Tibetan Plateau, has been identified as an excellent astronomical site from preliminary statistics of clear nights, sky background brightness, precipitable water vapour, total seeing and weather. Since 2022, several projects with apertures larger than 4 m have started construction or are being planned. Given the use of adaptive optics (AO) on these projects, in-depth measurements and analysis of the atmospheric turbulence above the site are required: the distribution and variation of the turbulence profiles provide a large-scale, climatological basis for site planning and for comparing candidate locations, complementing rather than replacing the on-site measurements needed for instrument design and operations. Predicting the atmospheric profiles of the site and its surroundings from satellite data, combined with on-site measurements, can help to optimise the site planning. This paper uses MERRA-2 reanalysis data to study the atmospheric profiles of the site and its environment, revealing the seasonal and long-term variations of the observing conditions. The reanalysis results are cross-checked against on-site ground-level instruments serving the same purpose. MERRA-2 overestimates the median free-atmosphere seeing by +0.22 arcsec (+50 %) while keeping the night-to-night correlation weak (r ~ 0.2), and underestimates the median total seeing by -0.24 arcsec (-27 %). It captures only ~22 % of the ground-layer turbulence and little of the observed seasonal amplitude of the free atmosphere. MERRA-2 is therefore suited to relative comparisons of spatial variability between locations and to climatological characterisation, not to quantitative AO applications or night-by-night assessment of profiles.

papers.title: ElevateHead: Decide Once, Then Commit: When the Action Head Matters for Multimodal Imitation
papers.abstract: Robots that learn from people often see several valid ways to do the same task: pass an obstacle on the left or on the right, open the microwave or move the kettle first. A policy that re-decides at every step can waver between these ways mid-task. We ask when the action head (the part of a policy that turns the state into actions) matters, and how it should make this choice. On a controlled task, heads that sample one way succeed far more often than a head that averages the ways when the demonstrations contain several ways and the state gives no hint which to take (+0.72 success with two ways); this trend was not reproduced on the other tasks we ran. We then present ElevateHead, a head that decides once at a learned decision point, commits to that choice for the episode, and exposes the choice as an input a user can set. We designed it by diagnosis: each version was frozen and tested on tasks it had not seen, and the next version changed only what a measured failure pointed to; predictions were registered before each run. The first four versions each fell below BeT on at least one held-out task. The fifth completed all four subtasks of the held-out Franka Kitchen task in 45.2% of episodes against 29.3% for BeT, the strongest baseline across our tasks (+0.160, 95% CI [+0.129, +0.188]); when a mode was forced, the first completed subtask matched it in 95% of successful episodes. Diagnosis also located where commitment breaks: varied start positions (repaired on the controlled task: commitment 0.22 to 0.81, success 0.74 to 0.91) and varied object placement (partly repaired: in an exploratory variant, commitment 0.03 to 0.59 on aligning with no detectable change in success). On held-out block stacking, version 4 was comparable to BeT and did not exceed it. A real-robot test with predictions fixed in advance is planned for a follow-up version of this paper.

papers.title: Noncommutative Mean Value Theorems for Free Noncommutative Functions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study noncommutative analogues of the classical Cauchy and Lagrange mean value theorems in the setting of free noncommutative function theory. For noncommutative functions on a uniformly open noncommutative set, we prove a Cauchy-type mean value inequality involving the right noncommutative difference operator $\Delta_R$ and the G-derivative, and we establish a mean value theorem for noncommutative curves. Furthermore, we characterize uniform comparison (Lipschitz-type) inequalities at all matrix levels and prove a factorization theorem for noncommutative functions. The proofs combine the Hahn--Banach theorem, the fundamental theorem of calculus along a line segment, and the direct-sum compatibility of noncommutative functions.

papers.title: Fovea-JEPA: Overcoming Geometric Blind Spots in V-JEPA for Camera Motion Recognition
papers.abstract: Camera motion recognition requires separating viewpoint changes caused by camera translation, rotation, or zoom from object motion and scene dynamics. Video-language models often rely on semantic cues and struggle with the geometric evidence needed for this task. Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures such as V-JEPA offer strong spatio-temporal representations, but our experiments suggest that they underrepresent geometric cues in some regions. Under temporal-reversal supervision, V-JEPA improves overall but degrades on several motion families, whereas a weaker geometry-oriented VGGT predictor improves across all families. We refer to these geometrically underrepresented regions as geometric blind spots and propose Fovea-JEPA to identify and address them. Using V-JEPA as the base model and VGGT as a geometry expert, we construct intervention pseudo-labels from their prediction errors to weakly supervise a blind-spot predictor. The predictor produces token-wise response maps, which are aggregated into a clip-level intervention score to guide adaptive fusion of visual and geometric features. This selective intervention introduces complementary geometric information while preserving reliable visual predictions. Experiments on CameraMotionDataset, CameraBench, and ShotBench demonstrate the effectiveness of Fovea-JEPA, with gains of 9.67, 8.67, and 24.38 percentage points over previously reported state-of-the-art baselines, respectively. Code and models will be released upon acceptance.

papers.title: Enabling Motion-Induced WiFi-CSI Sensing in Multi-Robot Systems: A Simulation Framework
papers.abstract: WiFi Channel State Information (CSI) enables fine-grained sensing of spatial relationships between wireless devices. The WiFi Sensor for Robotics (WSR) toolbox demonstrated that WiFi-CSI measurements collected during robot motion, combined with odometry, can be used to synthesize virtual antenna arrays, enabling motion-induced bearing estimation in multi-robot experiments. However, deploying the WSR approach has remained challenging due to its limited integration with standard robotics tools and reliance on deprecated WiFi-CSI acquisition hardware. This work presents an open-source simulation framework that integrates the WSR sensing pipeline within the robotic simulator Gazebo. The framework generates synthetic WiFi-CSI measurements with realistic physical signal properties and leverages realistic robot motion required for motion-induced sensing and downstream localization. It further supports processing both simulated and real WiFi-CSI data for direct comparison and validation. Our aim is to make WSR-style sensing accessible as a modular sensing modality for robotic research. We validate our framework by comparing simulated and real-world experiments using TurtleBot3 robots, and demonstrate its use for bearing estimation and robot localization. This work lowers the barrier to entry for WiFi-CSI-based sensing in multi-robot systems and provides a foundation for integrating WiFi-CSI sensing with multi-modal perception for localization and coordination. All code and experimental details are publicly available at https://github.com/baharhaghighat/DARS_2026_Dijkstra_et_al

papers.title: Prior-Data Fitted Networks for In-Context Off-Policy Evaluation
papers.abstract: Off-policy evaluation (OPE) is essential for assessing decision policies before deployment when online experimentation is costly or unsafe. Accurate estimation remains difficult when behavior-policy data are limited and the target policy favors states and actions rarely observed in those data. We propose InCOPE, a prior-data fitted network that learns a shared policy-value prediction rule across synthetic OPE tasks. We construct an OPE task prior over Markov decision processes and behavior-target policy pairs, generating behavior-policy datasets and exact target-policy values for pretraining. For a new tabular decision problem, the pretrained network uses the behavior-policy dataset, target policy, and known task settings as context to predict the policy's expected return without task-specific parameter updates. Experiments across four tabular domains, including a semi-synthetic clinical setting, demonstrate InCOPE's effectiveness for policy-value estimation.

papers.title: A simple construction of smooth counterexamples to the Loewner and Carath\'eodory conjectures
papers.abstract: Alp\"oge recently announced smooth counterexamples to the Loewner and Carath\'eodory conjectures. We present a simpler construction based on a trigonometric function as a seed. Using this, for every positive integer $k$, we construct a smooth real-valued function on the plane, flat at the origin, whose Hessian eigenline fields have an isolated singularity of index $1+k/2$. A support-function parametrization realizes this index as an umbilic index of a non-real analytic $C^\infty$-regular surface germ in Euclidean $3$-space. The same framework, applied to a rapidly decreasing function on the whole plane, gives a strictly convex closed smooth surface with exactly one umbilic, of index $2$. This paper is self-contained with regard to the existence of an umbilic of index $2$ and the construction of a counterexample to the Carath\'eodory conjecture.

papers.title: What Sketches Tell Us about LVLMs: Conventions, Grounding, and Localisation
papers.abstract: LVLM benchmarks tell us whether a model answers correctly, but not which visual conventions it has retained, nor where those conventions live. Sketches expose this hidden structure. A sketch removes texture, lighting, and photographic context while preserving the strokes humans judged sufficient for recognition. If an LVLM can operate on that abstraction, the surviving signal is structural rather than merely photometric. We introduce a training-free sketch probe with three readouts: temporal part-construction order, spatial attention-based grounding, and the mechanistic layer/head locus of grounding. We evaluate nine LVLMs on part order and five on the attention readouts, over two part-annotated sketch datasets. Three findings emerge. First, LVLM part order tracks human convention: models reproduce canonical orderings where human drawings converge, and become correspondingly variable where human orderings vary. Controls that blank, withhold, and mismatch the sketch locate this convention in the language model. Second, part-level grounding survives the abstraction: attention heads selected from the frozen model with an existing recipe recover part and object regions on object and scene sketches, with no grounding supervision. Third, the grounding signal concentrates in a narrow mid-network band whose location follows the base language model rather than parameter count in the two families we compare, and remains stable across object and scene sketches. The result is a practical diagnostic for sketch-driven LVLMs: no fine-tuning, no auxiliary segmenter, and a layer band that doubles as a head-selection prior, matching or improving grounding mAcc@0.1 in every model and dataset we tested.

papers.title: Extremal 3-uniform hypergraphs without generalized 4-cycles
papers.abstract: Let $f_r(n)$ be the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $r$-uniform hypergraph in which all disjoint pairs of edges have distinct unions. In 1977, Erd\H{o}s posed the problem of determining $f_r(n)$ and, in particular, asked whether $f_3(n)=O(n^2)$. F\"uredi later proved that $\binom{n-1}{r-1}+\left\lfloor (n-1)/r\right\rfloor \le f_r(n)<\frac72\binom{n}{r-1}$ for $r\ge3$ and $n\ge2r$. Motivated by his constructions, he further conjectured that $f_3(n)\le\binom{n}{2}$ for all sufficiently large $n$, and that, for each fixed $r\ge4$, the lower bound is exact for all sufficiently large $n$. This is known as the Erd\H{o}s--F\"uredi conjecture. In a recent breakthrough, Huang, Ma and Yang proved the conjecture for every fixed $r\ge4$ and characterized all extremal hypergraphs. In this paper, we settle the remaining $3$-uniform case for every $n$. The bound is sharp whenever $n\ge5$ and $n\equiv1,5\pmod{20}$. Our proof uses a local weight inequality and a transfer argument.

papers.title: Uniform Continuity of Boundary Crossing for Convex Sets
papers.abstract: Let C be an inhabited, bounded, open, convex subset of a Banach space, and phi the pointwise continuous mapping taking a pair of points, one inside C and one outside, to the point where the segment joining those points meets the boundary of C. We prove constructively that phi is uniformly continuous on the Cartesian product of a set well contained in C and the metric complement of C.

papers.title: Cut a Wall, See a Wall: Identity Substitution in Occluded Point-Cloud Perception for Construction Robots
papers.abstract: Construction robots must label building elements they can only partly see. We show that when occlusion at test time removes whole regions of a scene, rather than parts of an object as in training, point-cloud segmentation networks do not simply miss the hidden elements: they relabel them, and the errors collapse onto a single sink class. With fixed synthetic layouts the column absorbs up to 70% of all test points; with randomized layouts the sink moves to the stair, predicted at 4.5-5.4x its true share across three training seeds. Baseline mIoU falls to 0.15-0.27 (fixed) and 0.36-0.72 (randomized), and up to 269 whole objects vanish in a single test set. Appending 14 hand-computed geometric features per point (GPE) restores mIoU to 0.54-0.92 and removes 64-100% of whole-object losses in every run, for PointNet++ and a PTv3-style transformer in both layout regimes; on real S3DIS scans it removes every whole-wall loss (10 to 0). In an as-built column check computed from the predictions, GPE raises the share of correctly checked views from 17-58% to 71-92%. Feature permutation on fixed, randomized and real scenes explains the pattern: each class relies on whichever cue is stable in its training data, position for height-banded slabs and beams, intrinsic shape for walls and stairs once their position varies. Occlusion augmentation is a strong alternative on mIoU, but in every setting it loses more whole objects than GPE (e.g., 25-35 vs. 0).

papers.title: T-ConSG: A LiDAR-Based Real-Time Temporal Construction Scene Graph for Dynamic and Evolving Environments
papers.abstract: Dynamic and continuously evolving environments present significant challenges for robotic mapping and scene understanding, particularly on construction sites where moving agents, temporary obstacles, and persistent structural changes coexist. While dynamic and long-term SLAM methods can detect motion and environmental changes, their outputs are predominantly metric representations that provide limited structure for higher-level spatial and temporal reasoning. This paper presents a LiDAR-based real-time temporal construction scene graph (T-ConSG) that jointly represents free-space regions, static objects, dynamic objects, and environmental events with spatial-relational and event-participation edges. The proposed framework incrementally constructs the graph from LiDAR-derived geometric evidence, maintaining persistent free-space and static-object information while tracking dynamic objects. Changes in accumulated spatial evidence are further represented as explicit installation and removal events, allowing the graph to capture both transient dynamics and persistent environmental evolution. We demonstrate the proposed representation through three complementary application studies: dynamics-aware navigation in a bricklaying testbed, construction progress monitoring on the ConSLAM dataset, and online change detection in a simulated construction environment. The results demonstrate that the proposed T-ConSG provides a unified representation for organizing spatial and temporal information and supports robotic reasoning across environments containing both short-term dynamics and persistent changes.

papers.title: Halo formation and distribution around cosmic web
papers.abstract: We use the ELUCID simulation to study how the local environment affects the formation of dark matter halos and their spatial distribution around the cosmic web. We describe the environment by local density and cosmic-web type. At fixed web type, the halo mass function (HMF) depends strongly on the local density, whereas at fixed density it depends only weakly, though significantly, on the web type; the character of both dependencies changes around the mean density. The halo formation redshift is primarily driven by local density rather than cosmic web. We then introduce the three-dimensional cosmic-web cross-correlation function (3D-WCCF), which expresses the distribution of halos around cosmic web in the local tidal eigenframe. The 3D-WCCF provides numerous anisotropic characteristics. Around all web types, halos are most strongly correlated along the axis of weakest compression, $\mathbf{e}_3$, and least along the axis of strongest compression, $\mathbf{e}_1$. Nearly all cluster-sized halos reside in knots and lie preferentially in the plane perpendicular to ${\bf e}_1$. The 3D-WCCF also provides important information on the geometry and size of filaments, sheets and voids. Moreover, early-forming halos are more strongly correlated with the web than late-forming ones, and this assembly bias is anisotropic around filaments, sheets, and voids, being strongest along $\mathbf{e}_3$, but nearly isotropic around knots.

papers.title: Toward Near-Optimal Floorplanning with Complex Design Constraints for Modern SoCs
papers.abstract: Modern system-on-chip (SoC) floorplanning is increasingly challenged by highly coupled complex design constraints. Existing methods often relax constraints into objectives via multi-objective optimization, leading to infeasible solutions or degraded quality. To address this, we formulate the problem as a constrained optimization task and propose a novel three-stage analytical framework integrating semidefinite programming (SDP), augmented Lagrangian method (ALM), and second-order cone programming (SOCP), which enforces constraints more rigorously and achieves higher-quality solutions. First, we adopt a two-step SDP formulation to obtain a robust initialization in the non-convex search space. Next, we incorporate differentiable objectives and constraints into an incremental ALM to jointly handle coupled design constraints during global floorplanning. Finally, an SOCP-based legalization strictly enforces feasibility while further reducing area. Experiments on the FloorSet benchmark show that our method satisfies all constraints with the fastest runtime. Compared with state-of-the-art methods, it reduces wirelength and area by 90\% and 16\% on average, and achieves near-optimal results, with wirelength and area being merely 2\% and 1\% larger than the ground-truth references, respectively.

papers.title: Open-source Software and Pipelines for Generalizable and Reproducible EEG Analysis: An Overview
papers.abstract: Reproducibility, replicability, robustness, and generalizability are essential but distinct requirements for reliable electroencephalography (EEG) research. Achieving these goals remains challenging because EEG datasets vary substantially across acquisition systems, file formats, experimental paradigms, participant populations, event annotations, and recording conditions. In addition, differences in preprocessing choices, software implementations, parameter settings, and computational environments can substantially influence analytical results. This overview examines the standards, open-source software, and computational pipelines that support transparent and generalizable EEG analysis. We discuss the role of the Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS), Hierarchical Event Descriptors (HED), FAIR data principles, and community reporting guidelines in improving data interoperability and reuse. We review major EEG analysis platforms, including Brainstorm, EEGLAB, FieldTrip, MNE-Python, and SPM, as well as automated preprocessing and quality-control pipelines. We also describe supporting infrastructure for dataset validation, curation, standardized event annotation, and scalable cohort-level analysis. Finally, we provide practical recommendations emphasizing standardized data organization, complete reporting of analysis parameters and software environments, code sharing, preregistration, automated quality control, and robustness analyses across plausible pipelines. Together, these practices provide a foundation for EEG findings that are more transparent, reproducible, and generalizable across datasets, laboratories, and analytical tools.

papers.title: A superprocess model for eDNA transport in random river environment
papers.abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) is increasingly used to monitor aquatic organisms in rivers, yet predicting its concentration and assessing the reliability of such predictions remain challenging because river flow fluctuates with long memory and models of eDNA dynamics are inevitably misspecified. We propose a stochastic modeling framework for eDNA concentration in rivers that addresses both issues. The eDNA concentration is described by a stochastic partial differential equation with transport, decay, source, and square-root multiplicative noise, and the flow velocity is modeled by a superposition of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-type processes with long memory. We show that the long memory of the flow velocity induces superdiffusive transport of eDNA, with the variance of the transported distance growing superlinearly in the ensemble sense. The proposed model admits a closed-form Laplace functional, based on which we prove the existence and uniqueness in law of the solution on an unbounded domain. We further evaluate the effects of model uncertainty through a robust control formulation based on the relative entropy, in which the lower and upper bounds of the expected eDNA concentration, together with the worst-case distortions, are obtained in closed form. The framework is applied to eDNA and flow velocity data collected for the upstream migration of Plecoglossus altivelis altivelis in a river in Japan. The results demonstrate that the closed-form bounds provide a computationally inexpensive tool for quantifying the range of eDNA concentrations that can be expected under model uncertainty.

papers.title: Polar-structure galaxies beyond the local Universe: first results from Euclid
papers.abstract: Galaxies hosting strongly misaligned stellar and gas structures offer a direct window into external accretion and the buildup of angular momentum through multiple spin components. Such polar-structure systems are intrinsically rare and, until now, have been identified almost entirely at low redshift. The Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1), with its uniform, space-based VIS imaging, provides an unprecedented opportunity to locate these objects over wide areas and at much greater distances. We present the first visual search for polar-structure galaxy (PSG) candidates in Euclid VIS data, spanning approximately 10% of the Q1 survey footprint. This search yields the largest high-redshift PSG candidate sample assembled to date, including roughly 100 high-confidence systems with over 50 at $z \gtrsim 0.3$, along with additional populations of face-on rings and polar tidal structures (PTS). Robust candidates are detected out to redshifts of $z\sim1$, demonstrating that polar structures can be identified well beyond the local Universe. Although the present sample is not yet sufficient for quantitative occurrence rate or evolutionary measurements, it enables initial classification and basic structural characterization of PSGs at intermediate redshift. These results lay the groundwork for future statistical studies with forthcoming Euclid data releases and illustrate Euclid's power for rare-object science across cosmic time.

papers.title: Quantitative $K$-homology of uniform Roe algebras
papers.abstract: We introduce quantitative $K$-homology for uniform Roe algebras of discrete proper metric spaces with bounded geometry, based on the controlled $KK$-theory of Willett and Yu. We construct a comparison map from Lipschitz $K$-theory and prove that, for chain geodesic spaces, it is an isomorphism in a quantitative sense; in particular, quantitative $K$-homology is isomorphic to the inverse limit of the Lipschitz $K$-theory groups as the Lipschitz constant tends to zero. We also establish a pairing between quantitative $K$-homology and quantitative $K$-theory.

papers.title: Behavior Spatial Benchmark: Evaluating Spatial Understanding for Robotics
papers.abstract: Robot tasks require grounding spatial language in physical scenes, but task success alone cannot establish whether spatial instructions are followed. We present BEHAVIOR-Spatial, a benchmark built on BEHAVIOR-1K that measures spatial question answering, point-based target grounding, and robot action to examine how VLM spatial understanding relates to VLA behavior. It comprises 3,256 spatial questions across 49 activities, 1,240 grounding queries across 14 manipulation tasks, and action evaluations covering those 14 tasks and 10 navigation tasks. Our manipulation protocol evaluates held-out configurations and instruction following when the requested target changes within a fixed training layout. The baseline achieves 41.6% on held-out configurations but only 16.1% under changed instructions. VLM adaptation and robot-data pretraining provide limited improvements, whereas oracle visual target cues raise these rates to 60.3% and 38.0%, respectively. Perception evaluations reveal policy-dependent correlations between VLM question-answering and grounding accuracy and VLA manipulation performance. Together, these findings motivate evaluating spatial instruction following alongside task completion and examining when spatial perception performance translates into robot behavior. Project website: https://arielchen07.github.io/behavior-spatial/.

papers.title: On the Chv\'atal-Gomory Closure of Integer Quadratic Programs
papers.abstract: The integer quadratic moment hull is the closed convex hull of the pairs $(z,zz^{\top})$ with $z\in\mathbb{Z}^n$. We prove that one round of Chv\'atal-Gomory (CG) cuts applied to its basic semidefinite relaxation recovers this hull exactly if and only if $n\le6$. Our approach identifies its facets with perfect Delaunay polyhedra and characterizes their recovery through depth, the gap between lattice and continuous minima of a defining quadratic after normalization. A facet inequality is valid for the rank-one CG closure exactly when its depth is less than one. We also analyze the complexity of deciding membership in the CG closure and finding violated inequalities. Every rational point outside the CG closure admits a violated CG inequality whose encoding length is polynomial in the input length. Membership is strongly coNP-complete and exact separation is strongly NP-hard. The same reduction proves strong NP-hardness of quadratic split-inequality separation, resolving a conjecture of Burer and Letchford.

papers.title: Extended LASMP: Language Aided Subset Sampling Based Motion Planner for Drone Navigation
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a command-aligned sampling distribution that incorporates navigation commands directly into the exploration process to improve the efficiency of sampling-based motion planning for quadcopters in three-dimensional environments. Inspired by the Language-Aided Subset Sampling Motion Planner, this paper extends command-aware subset sampling to aerial systems. Subset sampling is generalized to command-aligned regions, enabling structured 3D exploration while preserving probabilistic completeness. Natural language instructions are grounded into yaw-conditioned and altitude-aware geometric constraints using a prompt-based large language model for entity extraction and instruction validation. Extensive simulations in complex environments demonstrate that the proposed method generates collision-free, consistent trajectories while significantly reducing sampling effort compared to uniform RRT-based planners.

papers.title: Identification of rippling interface between laser-ablated plasma and ambient uniform plasma at rest
papers.abstract: We present laboratory experiments on the early stage of the formation process of quasi-perpendicular supercritical magnetized collisionless shocks using laser-produced plasmas in an ambient uniform nitrogen (N) gas with 1~Torr under the external magnetic field with controlled polarity. An expanding aluminum (Al) piston plasma arising from laser irradiation interacts with a magnetized ambient N plasma, producing a bright, asymmetric self-emission whose global morphology reverses with the magnetic-field polarity. Two-dimensional ideal-magnetohydrodynamics simulations reproduce the main features of the observed structures and indicate that the ripple formation is unlikely to be driven by the Kelvin--Helmholtz instability, but is instead associated with vortex formation at the rounded leading edge of the piston plasma. We show that the bright, rippling emission delineates the Al-N interface, whose intrinsic width is consistent with an electron kinetic scale, and that its upstream side is predominantly composed of N plasma. This identification allows the formation of a supercritical collisionless shock in the magnetized N plasma to be discussed with minimal Al contamination.

papers.title: Experimental Evidence for Reflected Ions and Ion Temperature Anisotropy in a Forming Supercritical Magnetized Collisionless Shock
papers.abstract: Supercritical magnetized collisionless shocks require ion reflection for dissipation, yet its role during formation remains unclear. Using high-power lasers, self-emission imaging, and collective Thomson scattering, we investigate a forming quasi-perpendicular shock. An upstream emission tail is consistent with a foot-like structure, while ion heating and temperature anisotropy extend upstream of a ramp-like region. These observations provide evidence of reflected-ion-related heating during early shock formation, although the incident and reflected ion populations are not separately resolved. Future measurements of ion distributions and plasma waves could clarify how this heating mediates shock dissipation and particle energization.

papers.title: Lightweight Change Detection for Adaptive Collective Perception in Dynamic Environments
papers.abstract: Swarm robotics enables scalable inspection through collective perception, where robots infer environmental properties from distributed observations. A common benchmark considers robots exploring black-white tiled environments and determining the majority tile type. While most work studies static environments, dynamic environments remain underexplored. We study collective perception in dynamic environments where the tile proportion and the spatial correlation of surface patterns may change over time. To enable implementation on resource-constrained robots, we integrate a lightweight change detection mechanism into a Bayesian collective decision-making framework that resets robot beliefs when distribution shifts are detected. The proposed detector requires constant memory and constant per-sample computation, unlike two recent competitive approaches that store the full sample stream, making it suitable for memory-constrained robots. We further introduce a method that detects spatially correlated sampling and adapts sampling intervals online to mitigate correlation effects. Our simulation results in Webots show competitive change detection delays, more consistent precision across communication settings, and improved decision accuracy under changing spatial correlations.

papers.title: Learning Interaction-Aware Path Corrections from Unlabeled Trajectories: A LiDAR-Based Sim-to-Real GNN Framework for Construction Robots
papers.abstract: Construction robots operating near workers require navigation that can anticipate human motion while remaining robust to dynamic and unstructured site conditions. However, existing social navigation methods depend on hand-crafted interaction rules, labeled demonstrations, or robot-specific control policies, limiting their scalability and transferability in construction environments. We propose a real-time, LiDAR-only framework that learns interaction-aware path corrections from unlabeled demonstrations. Constant-velocity extrapolation generates residual learning targets, while a GNN models relationships among the robot, pedestrians, and goal context. During deployment, an extended Kalman filter tracks LiDAR detections to construct dynamic graphs, and the GNN offsets planner-generated waypoints through a planner-agnostic interface. Within the bricklaying trial, the GNN reduced path irregularity by 39.2\% and increased minimum TTC. Across Dynablox sequences, it increased minimum TTC by 38.3\% while producing shorter, smoother paths than the baselines. Ablation studies supported a 1.0-s prediction interval and confirmed the benefits of target context, reflection augmentation, and feature normalization.

papers.title: Symplectic capacities and Weyl laws from Abelian Higgs min max theory
papers.abstract:
For a Hermitian line bundle $E\to Y$ over a Riemannian manifold $(Y^n,g)$, the self-dual Abelian--Higgs energy is defined by $
  \En^Y_{\eps,g}(u,a)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_Y
  \left(|\nabla_a u|_g^2+\eps^2|F_a|_g^2+
  \frac{(1-|u|^2)^2}{4\eps^2}\right)dV_g, $
where $u$ is a smooth section of $E$, $a$ is a unitary connection, and $F_a$ is its curvature. Pigati and Stern studied the energy as a codimension-two analogue of the Allen--Cahn energy to study minimal submanifolds in a Riemannian manifold.
  In this paper, we use this functional to define a nondecreasing sequence of symplectic capacities $\{c_k^{\AH}\}_{k\ge1}$ in dimension four by a min--max construction. In particular, we prove that $c_1^{\AH}$ is normalized on the ball and the cylinder. For the upper bound on the cylinder, we combine Gromov's theory of families of $J$-holomorphic spheres with Taubes's planar vortex. For the lower bound on the ball, we use the properties of the Abelian--Higgs theory developed by Pigati--Stern, together with a geometric estimate on smooth approximations to the double of the ball and an equivariant deformation of low energy sublevels. These estimates give the normalization without Seiberg--Witten theory.
  We then use Seiberg--Witten moduli spaces on $\CP^2$ and $S^2\times S^2$ to prove an upper bound on the higher capacities of balls and the formula $c_k^{\AH}(Z^4(a),\omega_0)=ka$. We also prove Euclidean Weyl laws for the capacity sequence and for the min--max sequence with the standard Euclidean metric. For these results, we construct AH sweepouts from moduli spaces of the solutions to the perturbed Seiberg--Witten equations.

papers.title: Stochastic quantization and Osterwalder-Schrader axioms for quantum field theory models
papers.abstract: This PhD thesis constructs the $P(\Phi)_2$ Euclidean quantum field theory on $\mathscr{S}'(\mathbb{R}^2)$.
