We study online vector balancing for independent sparse random vectors: each arrival is supported on a uniformly random set of $s$ of the $n$ coordinates, with nonzero entries equal to one (binary model) or independent random signs (signed model), and an online algorithm must sign each vector upon arrival. The prefix discrepancy is the largest $\ell_\infty$-norm of the signed sums up to the horizon $T$, the terminal discrepancy that of the sum at time $T$. For binary inputs with $2\le s\le n/2$ and $T=\Theta(n)$, Altschuler and Tikhomirov showed that both are of order $\sqrt{s}+\log\log n$; they asked how the prefix discrepancy depends on the horizon and whether a matching terminal bound holds at every prescribed time.
  Over long horizons, the two differ. For every fixed $s\ge2$ and $c>0$, every online algorithm, even a randomized one that knows the horizon, incurs with high probability prefix discrepancy $\Omega(\log\log n+(\log T/\log n)^{\alpha_s})$ for $n\le T\le e^{cn}$, where $\alpha_s=(2^{s-1}-1)/(2^s-1)$. For $s=2$, quadratic Greedy matches this bound; for fixed $s\ge3$, we give an online algorithm with prefix discrepancy $O(\log\log n+(\log T/\log n)^{1/2})$. In contrast, a deterministic algorithm that knows neither the horizon nor the failure probability keeps the terminal discrepancy $O_k(\sqrt{s}+\log\log n)$ at each prescribed time, with failure probability $n^{-k}$ for every fixed $k$, for $2\le s\le n/2$ (binary model) and $2\le s\le n$ (signed model); for $s=2$, quadratic Greedy itself does so. This answers their terminal question, and the same order is optimal for prefixes at all polynomial horizons $T\ge n$.
  The lower bound uses a finite safety game realized within the input law; the upper bounds use moments of elementary symmetric polynomials and, at terminal times, a $\cosh$ potential or a translated gauge with a Foster inequality at every state.

papers.title: Stable matching under regulation
papers.abstract: In a market in which any coalition can reach agreements, a stable outcome need not exist even when agents have substitutable preferences. We show how regulation can restore stability. If a regulator participates in every agreement, a setwise stable outcome exists when each ordinary agent's preference satisfies a condition weaker than substitutability, while the regulator's preference remains largely unrestricted. An alternative existence result allows ordinary agents to have arbitrary preferences while requiring the regulator to support each agent's profitable contract deletions. Our results apply to matching markets involving regulated activities.

papers.title: In-Context Adapter Generation for Compositional Generalization in Large Audio Language Models
papers.abstract: Large audio language models (LALMs) have achieved strong performance on standard speech and audio understanding tasks, yet their ability to systematically generalize to novel task compositions remains underexplored. Taking a meta-learning view, we extend Text-to-LoRA (T2L) to LALMs, generating instruction-conditioned LoRA adapters with a Transformer hypernetwork rather than learning a single fixed adapter shared across instructions. To exploit fine-grained task information, we introduce in-context adapter generation (ICAG), a token-level hypernetwork architecture; we call the resulting method T2L-ICAG. We evaluate this approach on two representative LALMs using SIFT-50M for supervised fine-tuning and construct a controlled compositional evaluation suite covering five task classes. Across two LALM backbones, T2L-ICAG consistently improves over static LoRA and also the global embedding-based T2L baseline. Coverage and capacity analyses further show that these gains are larger on structurally out-of-domain tasks and cannot be explained by parameter count alone. These results suggest that generating task-specific adapters from instructions is a promising direction for improving compositional generalization of LALMs.

papers.title: Spatial Audio Generation and Editing with Executable Plans and Self-Distilling Transfusion
papers.abstract: Spatial audio authoring coordinates source decisions with soundfield synthesis. For editing, plans specify what to change and retain, while reference audio supplies further acoustic detail. We present AMBIT, a unified framework for native First-Order Ambisonics (FOA) generation and editing with three connected contributions. First, a shared Transfusion backbone couples autoregressive planning with rectified-flow rendering through executable ScenePlans that specify source content, activity, and 3D trajectories. For editing, the plan describes the full target scene, including retained sources; contrastive features ground the requested change, while full reference latents supply residual acoustic detail for preservation. Second, an FOA-aware continuous VAE combines shared-decoder omnidirectional recovery, asymmetric grouped KL, and spatial covariance matching to preserve content and inter-channel structure. Third, joint Transfusion on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) refines planning on student-generated prefixes and rendering at sampling states reached under student plans, with target-conditioned teachers supervising both modes of the shared student. Evaluations across speech, music, and sound show improved generation content and spatial quality, acoustic fidelity during instruction-guided editing, and unedited-source preservation over the compared baselines. Project page: https://wjm-george.github.io/AMBIT/

papers.title: Second order N-Electron Valence state Perturbation Theory for polaritonic systems
papers.abstract: Molecules strongly coupled to optical cavities often show multi-configurational character, which the cavity can enhance by mixing electronic states. Describing them accurately requires a complete treatment of correlation between all the involved quantum particles. The available QED ab-initio methods do not treat it in its completeness except for QED-FCI. We extend second-order N-electron valence state perturbation theory (NEVPT2) to polaritonic chemistry, in its state-specific (QED-NEVPT2) and quasi degenerate (QED-QD-NEVPT2) forms. Here, the correlation due to the interaction of more degenerate configurations comes from a QED-CASSCF reference, while that associated with instantaneous interactions between the particles is added by second-order perturbation theory. Application of the methods to ammonia, ethylene and formaldimine revealed that this approach represents the perfect alternative to the well established QED-Coupled Cluster approach when the molecular system is described by more degenerate configurations. The approaches developed in this work have the potential to become state-of-the-art methodologies for the description of reactivity and photochemistry in polaritonic systems.

papers.title: Positive solutions of Yamabe-type equations with general potentials
papers.abstract: Let $(M^n,g)$ be a smooth closed connected Riemannian manifold of dimension $n\ge3$, and let $\psi\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$. We prove that the equation $$ -\frac{4(n-1)}{n-2}\Delta_g u+\psi u=u^{\frac{n+2}{n-2}} $$ has a smooth positive solution if and only if its linear part has positive first eigenvalue. In dimensions $n\ge6$, the proof combines an energy estimate under exact local mass constraints with an intersection argument for finite cycles of atomic measures; dimensions $3\le n\le5$ follow from the theorem of Bahri and Brezis.

papers.title: MulFCoder: Framework-conditioned Multi-agent for MLLM-based Multi-framework Front-end Code Generation
papers.abstract: Generating runnable front-end code from UI screenshots is a long-standing goal in automated software engineering. Existing MLLM-based methods predominantly focused on HTML/CSS, leaving multi-framework generation for React/Vue/Angular underexplored. Naively modifying prompts leads to substantial performance gaps across multi-framework and highly framework-specific error modes. To address this, we propose MulFCoder, a framework-conditioned multi-agent method that explicitly encodes framework constraints to bring multi-framework differences into a decidable rule space. MulFCoder orchestrates four agents: Grounder constructs an ElementTable, ContentTable, and macro-layout regions from detected UI elements; Planner builds a DOM-like hierarchical layout tree, produces a task schedule, and derives a framework-specific file Contract; Writer generates structured file writes or patches within a restricted edit window; Judger enforces lightweight, framework-conditioned constraints to accept or reject updates and trigger bounded repairs, preventing drift and deadlocks without expensive builds. Experiments demonstrate that MulFCoder substantially improves compilation success rate and reduces framework-specific errors, with particularly pronounced gains on Angular.

papers.title: MANTA: Unlocking DAG Flexibility in Asynchronous BFT
papers.abstract:
DAG-based BFT protocols marked a shift in consensus design by replacing single-leader proposal paths with concurrent block proposals linked through a shared graph, where references encode consensus evidence. However, under heterogeneous wide-area networks (WANs), existing designs suffer from prolonged rounds and degraded performance due to straggler effects. The root cause is rigid round advancement: replicas move in synchronized rounds, waiting for enough references from the previous round before advancing.
  We propose a flexible DAG growth framework for asynchronous BFT consensus. Our key observation is that while reference quorums are necessary for safety and liveness, they need not block every round advancement. Instead, the connectivity required for commitment can be accumulated across rounds. Within the framework, we instantiate MANTA, which combines flexible DAG growth to advance by relaxing round synchronization and flexible coin to trigger leader election and finality earlier. Experiments on heterogeneous WAN deployments show that MANTA reduces latency by approximately 30%-70% in our evaluation.

papers.title: Phase field dislocation dynamics prediction of stacking fault widths in Cu-Al Alloys using generalised stacking fault energy from DFT and interatomic potentials
papers.abstract: The equilibrium width of intrinsic stacking faults is an important material parameter affecting key deformation phenomena. Here, we perform a comparative assessment of $\gamma$-surfaces generated using MD -- with a classical embedded-atom potential (ZW) and a machine-learned Gaussian Approximation Potential (GAP) -- and density functional theory (DFT), for Cu-Al alloys of varying Al content, and incorporate them as an energy term in PFDD simulations to obtain the equilibrium SFW. All three methods reproduce the lattice parameter and elastic moduli of Cu and Cu-Al alloys in reasonable agreement with each other and with experimental measurements from literature, but the MD-derived $\gamma$-surfaces, for both ZW and GAP, deviate substantially from DFT at the seven characteristic points, with the largest discrepancies at $T$ and $T_1$. When incorporated into PFDD, the DFT-derived $\gamma$-surfaces successfully predict an equilibrium SFW that increases with Al content and agrees well with standalone MD measurements and experimental values for pure Cu, whereas the MD-derived $\gamma$-surfaces do not yield an accurate SFW within PFDD, as the altered generalized stacking fault energy landscape causes the dissociating partials to become pinned soon after separation. These results show that DFT-derived $\gamma$-surfaces remain the more reliable route to alloy SFW prediction, and interatomic potentials must capture the shear path accurately to enable robust, efficient MD-PFDD modelling of stacking faults in alloys.

papers.title: On the isomorphism of the spaces $\mathcal{k}$ and $\mathcal{K}$
papers.abstract: Let $1 \leqslant p \leqslant q < \infty$, let $\mathsf{X}$ be a separable $\mathcal{L}_p$-space and let $\mathsf{Y}$ be a separable $\mathcal{L}_q$-space. We show that the space $\mathfrak{L}(\mathsf{X},\mathsf{Y})$ of bounded linear operators from $\mathsf{X}$ into $\mathsf{Y}$ is isomorphic to $\mathfrak{L}(\ell_p,\ell_q)$ if, and only if, $\mathsf{Y}$ is complemented in its bidual. We also show that $\mathfrak{L}(\mathsf{Z},\ell_{\infty})$ is isomorphic to $\mathfrak{L}(c_0,\ell_{\infty})$ for every separable $\mathcal{L}_{\infty}$-space $\mathsf{Z}$. This extends and complements the earlier result of Arias and Farmer [On the structure of tensor products of $\ell_p$-spaces, Pacific J. Math.]. Based on this general result, we give a completely different proof of the main result of Astashkin, Le\'snik and Maligranda [Isomorphic structure of Ces\`aro and Tandori spaces, Canad. J. Math.], which states that the space $\mathcal{K}$ and its sequence counterpart $\mathcal{k}$ are isomorphic. Furthermore, we complete the picture by showing that the spaces $\mathcal{k}$ and $\mathcal{K}$, although isomorphic, are not isometric. Along the way, we show that for every infinite compact metrizable space $K$ the $\ell_{\infty}$-sum of copies of the space $\mathscr{M}(K)$ of regular Borel measures on $K$ is isomorphic to $( \bigoplus_{n=1}^{\infty} L_1[0,1])_{\ell_{\infty}} \approx \mathfrak{L}(\ell_1,L_1[0,1])$. This provides an abstract blueprint for another result of Astashkin, Le\'snik and Maligranda, namely that $\mathcal{K}$ is isomorphic to $( \bigoplus_{n=1}^{\infty} \mathscr{M}[0,1])_{\ell_{\infty}}$. Finally, we show that there are models of set theory without the Axiom of Choice in which the spaces $\mathcal{k}$ and $\mathcal{K}$ are no longer isomorphic. This last part was inspired by V\"ath's paper [The dual space of $L_{\infty}$ is $L_1$, Indag. Math. (N.S.)].

papers.title: From GPU to TPU with Coding Agents: What Works, What Fails, and What It Costs?
papers.abstract: A coding agent can migrate a machine learning workload, report success, and still change how the model trains. Rising compute costs, limited accelerator capacity, and vendor dependence are pushing organizations toward alternatives to graphics processing units (GPUs); a key question is whether agent-generated migrations to tensor processing units (TPUs) can be trusted and at what cost. We build a dataset of 148 PyTorch ML research projects and use Claude Code to migrate ten of them from NVIDIA GPUs to Google Cloud TPUs. We independently assess whether each migration runs, preserves numerical behavior, executes on the intended hardware, maintains the project's goal, and delivers acceptable performance. We also examine failures, human effort, and costs. Eight projects meet our project-goal criterion, and migrations require 2.4 human interventions on average. Of 70 execution attempts, 53 fail (76%), and 26 of these failures (49%) raise no error. The most frequent cause is repeated compilation and other execution inefficiencies, while interactions with third-party libraries can silently change the computation: in one four-chip migration, the agent reports success despite a change in gradient clipping that reduces accuracy from 86.53% to 84.89%. Execution costs vary widely: in one workload, TorchTPU, a PyTorch execution backend for TPUs, trains 1.86 times faster and 25% cheaper per run than the GPU. For practitioners, these findings motivate independent reference runs, verification under the intended hardware configuration, and workload-specific acceptance and stopping criteria that account for both computational and human costs.

papers.title: Graham's rearrangement conjecture in finite abelian groups
papers.abstract:
Graham conjectured in 1971 that every subset of the nonzero elements of a prime cyclic group admits an ordering with pairwise distinct nonempty partial sums. Recently, the work of Pham and Sauermann, together with earlier results, settled this conjecture for all sufficiently large primes. In this paper, we prove that there is an absolute integer $n_0$ such that every subset $S\subseteq G\setminus\{0\}$ of a finite abelian group with $|S|\ge n_0$ admits such an ordering, which also solves a conjecture of Alspach and Liversidge for all sufficiently large sets.
  A key ingredient of our proof is a sufficient condition via additive dimension: If $|S|=n$ and $S$ contains a dissociated subset of size at least $\Omega((\log n)^2/\log\log n)$, then $S$ has an ordering in which no proper nonempty interval of consecutive terms sums to zero. This bound is within a factor of $O(\log n/\log\log n)$ of the smallest possible additive dimension of an $n$-element set.

papers.title: A Levi-form criterion for Oka complements
papers.abstract: We prove that if $M$ is a connected Stein manifold of complex dimension at least three with the density property, then $M\setminus K$ is a connected Oka manifold for every nonempty compact $K\Subset M$ with smooth boundary whose Levi form has at least two nonnegative eigenvalues at every boundary point for local defining functions negative on $\operatorname{int}K$. For compact sets in $\mathbb{C}^n$ with smooth boundary, this settles both implications between pseudoconvexity of $\partial K$ and the Oka property of $\mathbb{C}^n\setminus K$: pseudoconvexity is sufficient but not necessary for $n\geq3$, and necessary but not sufficient for $n=2$. In dimension two, we give an explicit compact set in $\mathbb{C}^2$ with strongly pseudoconvex boundary and non-Oka complement.

papers.title: Matter that learns what matters
papers.abstract: Can a material learn what deserves its attention? We show that it can in a model optical network, in which action outcomes train a persistent record in each link. The record biases whether a source is consulted and sets how strongly it changes a stored answer, so useful sources gain attention and influence without being identified in advance. The network's experience thus shapes the information available for its future learning. Resonant readouts make this learning fragile: reinforcement can carry a record past resonance, where it persists but its influence weakens. We derive bounds within which relevant signals guide the answer, irrelevant signals are rejected and stored answers remain open to revision. These bounds guide a learning rule that limits reinforcement as records form; in simulations, it acquires useful records and keeps them functional. When relevance changes, an obsolete record can block its own replacement. A local state that strengthens negative writing after unsuccessful actions releases obsolete records and completes the learning sequence more often. How a memory is read should decide how it is written.

papers.title: Indeterminacy of period map and Griffiths heights for hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We prove that the period map $\overline {\mathcal P}$, from the GIT moduli space of degree $d$ hypersurface $X$ in $\mathbb P^n$ to the Baily-Borel compactification of the period image associated to the middle cohomology $H^{n-1}_{\rm prim}(X,\mathbb Z)$, extends regularly to $X$ if and only if $X$ has at worst nodal singularities (resp. suspensions of slc surface singularities) when $n$ is even (resp. $n$ is odd). This verifies and generalizes Laza-O'Grady's prediction on the indeterminacy locus of the period map for quartic K3s to arbitrary hypersurfaces. For Calabi-Yau hypersurfaces, we prove that the birational map from the GIT moduli space to the BBH compactification extends regularly to $X$ if and only if $X$ has semi-log canonical singularities. The results apply to distinguish the Baily-Borel and BBH compactifications. In the process, we answer two questions of Mordant on the Griffiths height for families of hypersurfaces over curves, which are crucial to the proofs of the main results.

papers.title: SymLift: Neural Semantic Lifting for Compile-Free Vulnerability Detection in Context-Incomplete Code Fragments
papers.abstract: Missing project context can prevent build-dependent analyzers from constructing program relations required for vulnerability detection, while neural predictions alone do not establish auditable derivations. We present SymLift, a compile-free framework centered on Vulnerability-Oriented Neural Semantic Lifting for context-incomplete code fragments. A fine-tuned large language model reconstructs vulnerability-relevant control-flow, data-flow, memory, and resource relations in a constrained LLVM-like intermediate representation (IR), without reconstructing the full project context or directly predicting vulnerability labels. A deterministic parser validates the IR and maps its supported operations and relations into normalized evidence facts. Explicit Datalog rules derive findings with supporting facts and derivation traces, ensuring deterministic reasoning for fixed facts and rules. We evaluate SymLift on FormAI, Juliet, and MegaVul. Reducing complete Juliet programs to function-level fragments lowers Clang compilation success from 100% to 12.00%, whereas SymLift's analysis completion rate decreases by only 1.17 percentage points. After task-specific fine-tuning, the lifter achieves a control-flow intersection over union (IoU) of 96.85% on FormAI. SymLift-Qwen-7B achieves a Target-F1 of 94.41% on FormAI and, across six vulnerability families on MegaVul, a micro-averaged precision of 98.24% and a micro-averaged Target-F1 of 91.66%. These results support accurate and auditable detection in the evaluated context-incomplete settings, even with partial program relations.

papers.title: On Detection Reliability for Small Object Segmentation
papers.abstract: This study investigates whether predicted bounding boxes are reliable for determining where small-object segmentation should be performed without risking false negatives outside those boxes. The investigation leverages adenovirus particles as small objects, YOLO26x for detection, YO-LO26x-Sem for segmentation, and Mask R-CNN for both detection and segmentation. Segmenta-tion-model predictions were matched to ground-truth adenovirus masks or reference objects using their centroids, with ground-truth mask centroids preferred over ground-truth bounding-box centroids as references for matching. Matched predicted-mask centroids were considered as inside at least one detector-predicted bounding box or outside all such boxes, while ground-truth masks without matched predictions were recorded as having no matched segmentation. For the YOLO26 models, 34 reference objects (47.89%) had matched segmentation centroids inside at least one pre-dicted box, 8 (11.27%) had centroids outside all predicted boxes, and 29 (40.85%) had no matched predicted segmentation. For the Mask R-CNN model, the corresponding counts were 69 (97.18%), 0 (0.00%), and 2 (2.82%). These preliminary experiments demonstrated that restricting segmentation to detector-predicted bounding boxes risks excluding matched segmentation predictions outside those boxes, potentially introducing false negatives.

papers.title: Non-Ergodic Markovian Mirror Descent with Unbounded Noise
papers.abstract: We analyze stochastic mirror descent for minimizing a convex objective expressed as an expectation under the stationary distribution of a Markov chain, using noisy subgradient observations along a single sample path. Through Poisson's equation, we decompose the Markovian noise and control its contribution under regularity and moment conditions that allow the stochastic subgradients and the Poisson solution to be unbounded across the state space. We establish an $O(T^{-1/2})$ bound on the expected suboptimality gap of the weighted-average iterate for an appropriately chosen step size. The analysis does not require aperiodicity or convergence of the chain's marginal distributions to stationarity. For irreducible finite-state chains, we verify the required conditions on the Poisson solution and derive explicit bounds that quantify the effect of periodicity. For irreducible countable-state chains, we verify the required regularity and moment conditions under a geometric Lyapunov drift condition and suitable growth bounds on the stochastic subgradients.

papers.title: Envy-Free Allocations for Random Non-Additive Valuations
papers.abstract:
Benade et al. (EC 2024) introduced a semi-random model for non-additive fair division in which each agent starts with an arbitrary base valuation over bundles of items and independently permutes the item names uniformly at random. While they proved that envy-free allocations exist with high probability as the number of items grows for $n = 2$ agents, they left open whether the same holds for $n > 2$ agents. We resolve this open question in the affirmative: for any fixed number of agents $n$ and any number of items $m$ divisible by $n$, an envy-free allocation exists with probability $1 - o(1)$ as $m \to \infty$.
  Our proof combines the second moment method with a connection to the (small-set) expansion of generalized Johnson graphs, which may be of independent interest.

papers.title: CyberDual: AI Attackers versus AI Code Reviewers in Real Software Maintenance
papers.abstract: Open-source projects now let AI agents review incoming code, but the code under review may itself come from an AI attacker. We present CyberDual, an arena for this dual role of AI: attacker agents hide an exploitable bug in real maintenance work on widely used open-source projects, and reviewer agents try to find and repair it. Execution decides each match: we rerun the attacker's proof of concept (PoC) on the code that comes out of review. Every attack is new, and the windows can be rebuilt each quarter from the latest upstream history. Three agentic reviewers catch 85-91% of 1,088 valid attacks from six attackers. Yet when the attacker spreads the bug over real upstream commits, about one in six attack slots still ends with a working exploit after review. The strongest attacker has open weights: GLM 5.3 almost never refuses, and its attacks make up 13 of the 28 that get past all three reviewers. When they miss, Claude reviewers mostly approve the attack, while GPT-6-Sol mostly repairs the wrong code; a reviewer from a second vendor catches about two thirds of a Claude reviewer's misses. Beyond a leaderboard, CyberDual has three uses. First, PoC execution gives both sides a reward that agent reports cannot game, so its surviving attacks can train reviewers against stronger attackers. Second, it can gate a release on both scores: Claude Sonnet 5 refuses one in five attack slots, yet attacks about as well as GPT-6-Sol, so refusal alone does not remove attack capability. Third, it can warn the teams behind a deployed reviewer when a new attacker crosses a threshold: GLM 5.3 in Claude Code already gets an exploit past Sonnet 5 in 17% of its attack slots.

papers.title: Prefix Keys and Values Matter Late: RIPE Caching for Self-Speculative Decoding in Looped Language Models
papers.abstract: A looped language model runs one block of layers $R$ times per token, so its key-value (KV) cache holds $R$ planes per recurrent layer, and self-speculative decoding (draft with a few loops, verify with all $R$) reads them all. We find that prefix keys and values matter late: at equal perturbation size, loops 25-32 are $e^{15.0}$ (Huginn-0125) and $e^{12.8}$ (Raven-Llama) times more sensitive than loops 2-9, and the planes approach the last one geometrically, at 0.88 and 0.81 per loop. Whether the deepest plane alone suffices then depends on how ripe the late planes are: on Raven, storing only it is indistinguishable from a bf16-to-fp32 change; on Huginn, 1% of positions carry 74% of its error. We turn this into RIPE, which stores the deepest plane everywhere except a window of recent positions kept at full depth. On Huginn, a 64-position window removes 89% of the tail positions at 11.9% of the full cache's memory (1024-token context), and any window at least as long as the draft block makes batched verification block-independent by construction. Nine pre-registered GPU batches back these results. Simple models of acceptance, decoding cost and memory, two of them checked on held-out measurements, account for the measured self-speculative speed-ups ($2.09\times$ with the full cache, $2.58\times$ with the deepest plane) and decompose the $2.24\times$ fixed-memory throughput gain of one shared plane.

papers.title: Comment on "Test of the Gravitational Force Law on Cosmological Scales Using the Kinematic Sunyaev--Zeldovich Effect''
papers.abstract: Gallardo et al. [Phys. Rev. Lett. \textbf{136}, 151002 (2026)] constrain the index of the force law $g\propto r^{-n}$ with pairwise kinematic Sunyaev--Zeldovich measurements, $n=2.1\pm0.3$, and exclude the deep-MOND value $n=1$ at $3.3\sigma$. The exclusion does not follow from their calculation. Their templates for $n\neq2$ [their Eq.~(8)] raise the pair-averaged Newtonian acceleration to the power $n/2$, whereas the pair average of the pointwise law [their Eq.~(30) for deep MOND] is the average of the transformed field; the step that identifies the two attributes to the three-point function a correction that is of second order and not small. In a Gaussian linear field with linearly biased tracers, Gaussian integration by parts shows that the correctly averaged template is exactly proportional to the Newtonian one, with a constant that the analysis absorbs into the mean optical depth. Gaussian realizations with peak-selected tracers find the same proportionality to within 2\% (0.5\% for the fiducial selection), and refitting the data of the Letter with the resulting template gives $\chi^2=20.1$--$20.2$, against $20.1$ for the Newtonian template and $33.8$ for Eq.~(8): in every controlled case examined the data do not discriminate between $n=1$ and $n=2$, and the $3.3\sigma$ exclusion, with the $10\sigma$ forecast that rescales it, rests on the order in which the average and the power were taken. What a self-consistent MOND cosmology predicts for this observable is a separate question, which the Letter does not address.

papers.title: On Khovanov homology of virtual links
papers.abstract: We show that the Khovanov homology of virtual knots defined by V.O. Manturov and the Khovanov homology defined by D. Tubbenhauer coincide.

papers.title: Theory of the $1/9$ Magnetization Plateau of the Spin-$1/2$ Kagome Heisenberg Antiferromagnet
papers.abstract: We investigate the $1/9$ magnetization plateau of the spin-$1/2$ kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet using infinite projected entangled-pair states and identify a spin-density-wave state with a $27$-site unit cell and a lower variational energy than previous approaches. In contrast to higher-magnetization plateaus, which are well described by localized magnons on nonoverlapping hexagons and preserve a sixfold rotational symmetry, the $1/9$ plateau only keeps a threefold rotational symmmetry and consists of a tiling by three types of $9$-site clusters related by $\pm2\pi/3$ rotations. These conclusions are supported by a complementary cluster mean-field theory which correctly preserves the symmetry of the higher plateaus but leads to the same spontaneous symmetry breaking for the $1/9$ plateau with a qualitatively similar pattern of nine different local magnetizations.

papers.title: Theoretical Pulsation Properties of RR Lyrae and Type II Cepheids in the JWST and Roman photometric systems
papers.abstract: RR Lyrae (RRL) stars and Type II Cepheids (T2Cs) are key standard candles and tracers of old stellar populations. The deep, wide-field capabilities of facilities such as the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will significantly expand their utility as a Population II alternative to Classical Cepheids for distance scale calibrations. We present theoretical pulsation properties-including light-curve morphologies, amplitudes, and multi-filter relations for RRLs (Z = 0.0001 - 0.02, M = 0.51 - 0.80, Msun) and T2Cs (Z = 0.0001 - 0.01, M = 0.495 - 0.65, Msun) to enable detailed studies of Galactic and extragalactic populations. Using alreday available non-linear convective pulsation models, we converted their predicted bolometric light curves across various chemical compositions and evolutionary stages into the JWST and Roman photometric systems. From these, we derived multi-filter Period-Amplitude and Color-Color diagrams, alongside Period-Luminosity and Period-Wesenheit relations with explicit metallicity terms. RRL relations display a significantly stronger zero-point metallicity dependence than those of T2Cs, despite sharing similar slopes. Consequently, T2Cs offer a distance scale indicator that is remarkably robust against metallicity uncertainties. As a preliminary test, we applied our metal-dependent Period-Wesenheit relations to a subset of JWST-observed RRLs in the WLM galaxy, deriving a distance modulus of mu_0 = 24.85 +/- 0.03 mag (assuming the literature average metallicity). The derived distance to WLM is consistent with most literature values, though slightly shorter than determinations based on Classical Cepheids and the Tip of the Red Giant Branch. These theoretical relations pave the way for future high-precision distance determinations and asteroseismic diagnostics with JWST and Roman.

papers.title: On maximum likelihood estimation in the $\beta$-model for random hypergraphs
papers.abstract: We study maximum likelihood estimation in the $\beta$-model for random hypergraphs, in which a group of vertices succeeds with a probability that depends on the sum of its members' parameters. The data are independent binary outcomes of experiments on groups of vertices, tested according to an arbitrary, possibly incomplete design. Suppose that every tested group has $k$ vertices and success probability in $[\epsilon,1-\epsilon]$. For complete designs in which every group is tested at least $r$ times, a unique maximum likelihood estimator (MLE) exists with high probability if $r\geq C_k\epsilon^{-1}\log n/n^{k-1}$, and for $m$ experiments on uniformly random groups, it suffices that $m\geq C_k\epsilon^{-1}n\log n$, where $C_k$ depends only on $k$. Both conditions are linear in $\epsilon^{-1}$ and, for fixed $k$, cannot be improved in general beyond the constant; they follow from finite-sample bounds for arbitrary designs. We bound the mean squared error of the MLE over a parameter box by the smallest eigenvalue of the correlation matrix of the design, and show that the rate is minimax optimal for balanced complete designs. Among $k$-uniform designs with a given number of experiments, designs in which every pair of vertices takes part together in the same number of experiments maximize this eigenvalue, and uniform random designs nearly do so with high probability. Finally, the design matrix of a uniform random design has full column rank with high probability if $m\geq\max\{n,c(n/k)\log n\}$ for fixed $c>2$ and $k=o(n/\log n)$, or $m\geq n$ when $k\geq(1+\xi)\log n$. For fixed $k$, the threshold $(n/k)\log n$ is sharp, and above it rank deficiency is asymptotically as likely as some vertex taking part in no experiment.

papers.title: Proof of the Harary--Hill conjecture: an exposition
papers.abstract: The Harary--Hill conjecture states that the crossing number of the complete graph $K_n$ is exactly $\frac{1}{4}\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor \left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rfloor \left\lfloor\frac{n-2}{2}\right\rfloor \left\lfloor\frac{n-3}{2}\right\rfloor$. We present a streamlined variant of the proof of this conjecture recently announced by OpenAI (2026). Although the original proof is relatively short, it is quite difficult to follow. We simplify several steps and provide a concise and accessible exposition of the proof. We also combine this new result with known reductions to determine the crossing numbers of several other graph families.

papers.title: Correlations between Dynamical Dark Energy and Neutrino Parameters
papers.abstract: Recent Baryon Acoustic Oscillation (BAO) data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), fitted jointly with Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) and Type Ia Supernovae (SNe) data, favor dynamical dark energy (DDE) over the standard $\Lambda$CDM model. In this work, we investigate whether the mass and degeneracy of relic neutrinos are degenerate with DDE parameters and can also account for this statistical deviation from $\Lambda$CDM. Using a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) analysis of a joint Planck CMB temperature, DESI BAO, and Pantheon+ dataset, we show a robust parameter degeneracy between the DDE equation of state and neutrino physics. We supplement this with a semi-analytical framework that recovers the numerical correlation, showing that the tight constraint on the CMB acoustic scale drives this degeneracy. Our results highlight the clear correlation between DDE and neutrino parameters, underscoring the critical need to jointly constrain the neutrino sector and the dark sector in next-generation cosmological surveys.

papers.title: An Alt-Caffarelli problem for elastic graphs
papers.abstract: We study an Alt-Caffarelli-type free boundary problem for symmetric elastic graphs with fixed boundary height. Our results concern existence of minimizers and their description in terms of regularity and shape. It turns out that the weight coefficient in front of the measure term is decisive for existence. We identify a sharp threshold for this coefficient below which existence is guaranteed. Moreover, we find that all sign-changing minimizers are described by a system of three Eulerian elasticae, none of which are lines. Another result shows non-flatness of free boundary points, a classical question in the study of Alt-Caffarelli problems. These properties lead to a better understanding of the nonexistence phenomenon above the aforementioned weight threshold.

papers.title: Slow blowup solutions for the focusing energy supercritical nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation
papers.abstract:
We consider the focusing energy supercritical nonlinear Schr"odinger equation  egin{equation*} i\partial_t\psi+\Delta\psi+|\psi|^{2p}\psi=0 \end{equation*} in dimensions $d\geq11$, with $p\in\mathbb N^\ast$, under the Joseph--Lundgren condition $2p+1>p_{JL}(d)$. For every $

Our proof combines matched asymptotic expansions across three spatial scales with modified energy estimates. The key ingredient is the systematic treatment of the singular nonlinear background and coupled oscillations generated by the slow algebraic tail of $Q$.

papers.title: Is the arXiv Apocalypse upon us? A break in preprint growth coincident with agentic AI
papers.abstract: As an experiment in agentic assisted analysis, we used an agentic AI model to analyse the effect of agentic AI on arXiv submissions; data acquisition, analysis and the first draft were carried out by the model under the author's direction. Monthly arXiv submissions have grown exponentially for three decades, at about $9\%$ per year. Fitting a piecewise log-linear trend with seasonal modulation to the full record, we find two post-pandemic breaks in growth rate. The first, in mid-2022, precedes ChatGPT and is carried by the expansion of AI research within computer science (CS); outside CS, growth from 2022 to 2025 remained at $8\%$ per year. The second, between December 2025 and February 2026, follows the release of models capable of extended autonomous work and is absent from the AI categories themselves. Since December 2025 submissions without a CS listing have run $17\%$ above trend, and in September 2026 total submissions reached a record $40\,363$. The excess is largest in mathematics, where submissions doubled within a year, and follows a gradient from formal and theoretical fields to experimental ones that is not ordered by surveyed rates of AI-tool adoption. In mathematics the increase is distributed across subfields and authors, two-thirds of it arising from a larger number of distinct authors rather than from a few prolific submitters. Across fields the clearest signature is a shift to single authorship: solo-authored papers rose by $70\%$ within a year in mathematics and condensed matter, and by $44\%$ in quantitative biology even as its total output fell, but not in experimental particle physics. The analysis is deliberately agnostic of LLM-detection methods: it uses only submission counts and metadata, with treatment timing fixed by calendar dates, and is therefore free of the outcome-triggered timing bias of author-level studies.

papers.title: EvolveMAS: A Unified Self-Evolution Framework for Decentralized Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: Decentralized multi-agent systems (MAS) enable large language model agents to interact without centralized control. Agents need to adapt to other agents at test time and reuse accumulated experience to refine their interaction strategies for future interactions across cooperative, mixed-motive, and adversarial settings. However, existing approaches often develop adaptation mechanisms for particular interaction settings. This raises a central question: how can decentralized MAS support test-time adaptation and reliable experience reuse across interaction settings? We propose EvolveMAS, a unified self-evolution framework that supports experience-driven adaptation within and across episodes. EvolveMAS pairs each main agent with a dedicated MemoryAgent for test-time memory governance, which maintains isolated Structured Memory outside the main agent's reasoning context. EvolveMAS organizes adaptation into two complementary processes: Within-Episode Online Adaptation and Cross-Episode Knowledge Evolution. During Within-Episode Online Adaptation, MemoryAgent updates episodic, semantic, and working memory from interaction evidence to inform subsequent actions. During Cross-Episode Knowledge Evolution, the main agent uses memory and episode outcomes to distill reusable interaction knowledge comprising partner profiles and interaction strategies for subsequent episodes. Across five benchmarks and six evaluation configurations spanning the three interaction settings, EvolveMAS achieves the highest normalized average score of 77.2 among the compared methods. Ablations show that test-time memory governance and cross-episode knowledge reuse both improve performance. Interaction traces further illustrate how updated memory and distilled knowledge guide subsequent interactions. These results support experience-driven adaptation in decentralized MAS without updating model parameters.

papers.title: Perceived Acceptability of Sensory Augmentation
papers.abstract: Sensory augmentation (SA) can extend how people perceive and engage with public environments through the body, offering opportunities to support shared multimodal experiences between deaf and hearing visitors. Designing such systems requires understanding which combinations of tactile stimuli and body locations users perceive as acceptable. We examined the perceived acceptability of fictitious yet feasible SA configurations in a museum use-case. Using a modified technology acceptance model, we surveyed 307 deaf and hearing participants about tactile stimulus types and body locations. The results showed significant effects of stimulus type and body location on acceptance, but no interactions with hearing status. Participants generally preferred temperature-based stimuli, subtle movement, texture, and tickling over vibration, and distal over proximal body locations. These findings suggest that tactile SA design should be guided primarily by embodied and contextual factors rather than hearing status, informing future systems for shared multimodal experience in public cultural settings.

papers.title: AuRA: From Atoms to Bits through Autonomous Robot Interaction
papers.abstract: Simulation enables robot-learning experiments at scale, but acquiring physics-informed digital twins often requires human manipulation and manual annotation of recorded interactions. To reduce this reliance on human effort, we present AuRA, a system that automates robot interaction and data preparation for digital-twin reconstruction. AuRA combines execution-aware grasp selection, gripper-motion measurements derived from robot states, and registered pre-interaction geometry and appearance priors. These choices enable autonomous collection, avoid reliance on visual gripper tracking, and recover object information obscured by the robot. Across 13 deformable objects, AuRA reduces active human labor and wall-clock collection time per successfully reconstructed asset by 88.5% and 55.4%, respectively. Relative to the human-collected PhysTwin baseline, AuRA improves seven of nine metrics for future prediction under known gripper motion, including a 28.1% reduction in one-way $L_1$ Chamfer distance. It also achieves similar mean silhouette IoU and Chamfer distance under the evaluated unseen interactions. These results highlight the potential of autonomous robot interaction to support more efficient digital-twin acquisition with comparable reconstruction quality.

papers.title: Scaling Dexterous Manipulation via Action Representation Pretraining
papers.abstract: Large-scale vision, language, and video pretraining has substantially improved the perception and generalization capabilities of robotic manipulation models, but action generation for complex dexterous manipulation remains constrained by the scarcity of robot demonstrations. Limited robot demonstrations must be used to learn both action representations and task-conditioned action distributions, making it difficult to adequately learn action representations and, in turn, limiting the ability of downstream generative models to generate complex dexterous actions. To address this limitation, we propose ARPG (Action Representation Pretraining and Generation), which explicitly separates action representation learning from action generation: we first pretrain an action representation encoder on large-scale human manipulation data. We then freeze the encoder and train a compact generative backbone (130M parameters) to learn task-conditioned action distributions in the encoder's representation space. Experimental results show that ARPG achieves state-of-the-art performance on the DexJoCo benchmark and improves the average success rate on bimanual dexterous manipulation from 10.1% for $\pi_{0.5}$ to 44.7%. Scaling experiments further show that broader coverage of human manipulation behaviors effectively improves downstream performance. These results indicate that action representation pretraining provides an independent scaling dimension for improving complex dexterous manipulation capabilities.

papers.title: Nonlinear Control of Aerial Manipulator
papers.abstract: This paper presents two controllers for a quadrotor equipped with a two-DOF robot manipulator that physically interacts with the environment. Cartesian impedance and adaptive sliding mode controllers are implemented and compared for a simple hovering task in the presence of some bounded disturbance. A full dynamic model is developed, and the two above controllers are implemented with the same initial conditions and desired position.

papers.title: The dominance of feedback mechanisms for perception in the central visual field: the flip tilt illusion by backward masking and the Feedforward-Feedback-Verify-reWeight algorithm
papers.abstract: The flip tilt illusion is the misperception of the orientation of the alignment between a pair of dots by 90 degrees. It occurs when the dot-pair contains one black dot and one white dot, is typically visible only in the peripheral visual field. It is predicted by the central-peripheral dichotomy (CPD) theory. Along the visual pathway from retina to downstream stages, our brain admits only a tiny fraction of visual input information for recognition due to a processing bottleneck that starts from the output of the primary visual cortex (V1) along the visual pathway. Accordingly, perception downstream from V1 relies on impoverished information, selected largely by gaze shifts to center the selected content at fovea and additionally by the capacity of the bottleneck even in the central visual field, likely making perceptual hypotheses about the visual scene ambiguous or illusory. To overcome, downstream areas send feedback to upstream areas such as V1 to query for additional information, thereby re-assessing the weights of the initial hypotheses. This perceptual algorithm is termed Feedforward-Feedback-Verify-reWeight (FFVW). To save resources, the feedback query is limited largely to the central visual field. The peripheral visual field is thus vulnerable to perceptual ambiguities and illusions. The CPD theory further predicts that impairing the feedback renders the flip tilt illusion visible in the central visual field. This paper reports a confirmation of the prediction. The feedback is disrupted by masking the visual inputs after a short viewing duration t. Furthermore, the FFVW algorithm is studied by a computational model of the perceptual data as a function of t. It reveals that the initial feedforward sweep of visual information explains the flip tilt illusion for t shorter than 20 ms, whereas the feedback mechanism dominates perception for longer t.

papers.title: Trajectory Generation and Control for Quadrotors
papers.abstract: In this project, I explored controller design and trajectory generation for a quadrotor. Differential flatness was used for trajectory generation based on one of the references. A minimum snap trajectory is generated from the given algorithm based on waypoint navigation, and a simple proportional plus derivative (PD) controller is used to track the trajectories. Simulation results are presented which generate smooth trajectories for position and velocity of the quadrotor.

papers.title: Toward Neuroadaptive Communication Interfaces: A Framework for Personalized Speech and Language Support
papers.abstract: Speech and language technologies have expanded access to communication, but the support they provide is often fixed. The same linguistic or visual aid may help one user and hinder another, or become less useful as task demands change. This project proposes a framework for adapting language presentation to individual abilities and ongoing interaction. It separates access to a message from the estimation of user needs and from the selection of support, including sentence segmentation, pictograms, and optional spoken output. Behavioral feedback provides the primary evidence for adaptation; electroencephalography is considered an additional, uncertainty-aware source of information rather than a direct measure of comprehension. We specify a staged evaluation comparing fixed, behavior-adaptive, and neuroadaptive interfaces. The central question is whether neural information improves comprehension and communication efficiency beyond a strong behavioral baseline.

papers.title: py-ARGOS: A Python package for automatic, statistically principled discovery of ordinary differential equations from data
papers.abstract: Recovering the governing equations of a dynamical system from data is a central problem in data-driven science, yet the available Python tooling forces a compromise among automation, statistical rigor, and reliability. We present py-ARGOS, a Python package implementing two automatic algorithms, bootstrap ARGOS and Bayesian-ARGOS, behind a uniform interface. Both are statistically principled throughout: automated model selection reduces the candidate library, each coefficient is reported with a bootstrap confidence or Bayesian credible interval that quantifies its uncertainty, and a term is retained when this interval excludes zero. Built-in diagnostics additionally flag unreliable fits. On chaotic benchmark systems, the two algorithms improve on the SINDy family's identification performance.

papers.title: The fiscal limits of efficient trade
papers.abstract: Sustaining efficient trade under private information requires external subsidies. Although a designer cannot avoid deficits on average, they can control exposure. We characterize efficient and truthful mechanisms that minimize the worst-case deficit in markets with many buyers and sellers, under interim participation. This problem is dual to maximizing expected trade surplus under correlation ambiguity, with constraints on submarkets with one agent removed. In bilateral trade, the best deficit ceiling is the competitive surplus in a benchmark continuum market, achieved by a "competitive pivot mechanism". In larger markets, optimal mechanisms are characterized in terms of worst-case residual welfare contributions, but solutions exhibit a complex combinatorial structure. We obtain explicit guarantees under natural participation charge restrictions and establish how the best deficit excess decays as market thickens. Our duality characterization is general and extends to many mechanism design environments (public goods, partnership dissolution), and alternative participation constraints.

papers.title: Task Relevance-Driven Prompt Expansion for Federated Continual Learning
papers.abstract: Federated continual learning (FCL) has attracted considerable interest by enabling local clients to continually acquire knowledge from new tasks. However, most FCL methods assume that the global server has prior knowledge of the arrival times and number of categories for new tasks, which is unrealistic in the real world. Furthermore, they neglect the importance of positive inter-task semantic relationships when learning new tasks and are significantly affected by irrelevant relationships from old tasks, thereby exacerbating catastrophic forgetting. To resolve the above challenges, we develop a novel Task Relevance-driven Prompt Expansion (TRPE) model. Specifically, to eliminate the reliance on prior knowledge of new tasks, we propose an out-of-distribution detector to identify the arrival of new tasks within local clients, along with a radius-adaptive DBSCAN to infer the quantity of categories in new tasks on the proxy server. Moreover, to explore positive inter-task relationships, we calculate the affinity between the original gradient for learning new task and its gradient orthogonal to the feature space of old tasks to evaluate semantic relevance between old and new tasks from a global perspective. Then, we use this global task relevance to determine the key-prompt pair for new tasks and identify highly related old tasks. After concatenating their prompts for training, we can leverage such positive inter-task relations to improve the continual learning of newly arriving tasks. To balance the learning of new tasks and the forgetting of old ones, a soft orthogonality constraint is applied to the local key and prompt gradients. Experiments spanning diverse datasets and backbones confirm the efficacy of our TRPE model.

papers.title: End-to-End Neural Modeling of EM Response and Design Performance for Free-Form RFIC Passives
papers.abstract: Passive matching networks are critical components in radio-frequency integrated circuits (RFICs), but their design is bottlenecked by expensive finite-difference-based electromagnetic (EM) simulation. We propose an end-to-end neural framework for free-form RFIC passives that predicts both EM response and downstream design performance under varying frequency and circuit contexts, combining a frequency-conditioned neural simulator with a circuit-conditioned neural solver. To improve design performance prediction, the simulator outputs a neural EM response consisting of both the explicit EM response and a complementary response, together with a dependence regularizer that encourages the two responses to capture orthogonal information. To evaluate the proposed framework, we construct a large-scale dataset of free-form passive layouts, synthesized from both expert-designed contours and random paths. Our 21M-parameter model achieves high accuracy across a broad frequency range, circuit contexts and passive matching settings, with $R^2>0.98$ for almost all targets, while providing orders-of-magnitude faster evaluation than traditional EM simulation. Code available at https://github.com/ETH-IDEAS/RFIC-NeuralSim.

papers.title: New results on nil rings
papers.abstract: For every field~$\Bbbk$, we construct a non-nilpotent nil algebra~$A$ whose Lie algebra $A^{(-)}$ is generated by ten elements. For $\Bbbk = \mathbb Z_p$, its adjoint group can also be generated by ten elements. Moreover, for every field $\Bbbk$ algebraic over its prime subfield, we construct a finitely presented algebra $B$ over $\Bbbk$ whose Jacobson radical is not nil. These results were found with the assistance of Aristotle (Harmonic).

papers.title: Retrospective Comparison of Radiation Oncology Patient Message Responses Generated by Epic and Institutionally Managed LLMs
papers.abstract: We retrospectively compared Epic-generated draft replies with institutionally managed hybrid GPT-4.1 and Gemini 2.5 Pro responses to 51 selected single-turn radiation oncology messages. Six clinicians, blinded to response source, rated overall quality on a five-point scale and perceived editing effort on a four-point scale. Mixed-effects models accounted for repeated ratings by message and clinician. Adjusted overall-quality means were 2.95 for Epic, 4.27 for hybrid GPT-4.1, and 4.39 for hybrid Gemini 2.5 Pro. Corresponding editing-effort means were 2.38, 1.46, and 1.41, with lower scores indicating less perceived effort. Both hybrid models received more favorable ratings than Epic for both outcomes (all Holm-adjusted P < 0.001), without a statistically significant difference between the hybrid models. These findings support prospective evaluation of clinician-supervised draft generation, though editing time and patient outcomes were not measured, and clinical safety was not established.

papers.title: Photoinduced charging and spatially selective photochemistry on ferroelectric surfaces
papers.abstract: Ferroelectric surfaces exhibit polarization-dependent photoreactivity and provide a route to program chemical patterns through local electrical control of polarization. Observations accumulated over several decades show reaction products in domain interiors, at domain boundaries, and in other selected regions, indicating that the mechanisms extend beyond a single polarization-induced band-bending picture. Here we analyze light-induced charging and interfacial reactions on uniformly polarized ferroelectrics and domain patterns, for dry surfaces and surfaces in contact with an electrochemically active solution. A common semiconductor transport and charge-conservation framework distinguishes five cases: an isolated dry ferroelectric, a dry ferroelectric connected to a carrier reservoir, a blocking ferroelectric-electrolyte junction, a reactive interface with an external carrier return, and two opposite domains coupled through the solid and electrolyte. Analytical solutions and numerical evaluations connect stationary potentials versus illumination to differential optical spectra and finite light-step responses. We further examine the doping effects on static potentials in all five cases and dynamic photovoltage in the isolated film and a fixed-polarization, bare-surface contacted-film variant. For reactive interfaces, the same framework determines reduction and oxidation rates, their spatial distributions, and accumulated reaction amount. The analysis covers surface charging and photochemical conversion beyond deposition, while retaining the electrical and chemical boundaries that distinguish finite charging from sustained turnover, and explains the observed range of photodeposition morphologies. Finally, this framework builds the theoretical foundation for the modulated photovoltage imaging methods that can readily be realized in SPM under illumination.

papers.title: IntNet: A Communication-Driven Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Cooperative Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: Achieving safety in autonomous driving through Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) is a critical yet challenging task due to non-stationarity, partial observability, and the need for effective coordination among agents. Although earlier cooperative MARL methods have aimed to improve coordination by sharing encoded state observations, we find these strategies are insufficient in safety-critical scenarios. To address this gap, we present IntNet, a novel MARL framework that enhances safety by incorporating the transmission of vehicle intent and adaptive communication scheduling into a unified end-to-end learning paradigm, jointly optimising all components for safe coordination. Central to our approach is an observation prediction module that enables agents to forecast subsequent policy outputs, which they can then share across a vehicle-to-vehicle network. Our model-free architecture employs a Graph Attention Network to process incoming messages and a scheduler component to dynamically optimise the communication graph for bandwidth efficiency. We compare IntNet against state-of-the-art communicative MARL methods in complex urban environments with both autonomous and human-operated vehicles, achieving improved coordination, lower collision rates, and reducing communication efforts by up to 60\%. Through extensive experiments, we assess the framework's learning efficiency, scalability, and the balance between information sharing and bandwidth usage for collision-free trajectories.

papers.title: DynaFlow: Learning Free-Form Multi-Agent Orchestration
papers.abstract: Multi-agent systems often rely on predefined collaboration structures, limiting their ability to adapt to diverse task requirements. We introduce DynaFlow, a framework that integrates free-form executable workflow synthesis into the action space of the main agent. The agent decides when collaboration is needed and generates task-specific programs that coordinate sub-agents through sequential or parallel execution, structured information exchange, and verification. Execution results and traces inform subsequent actions, enabling the agent to adapt collaboration as reasoning progresses. We train only the main agent through supervised fine-tuning on distilled trajectories, followed by refinement on examples filtered for unsupported premises, biased verification, and information-flow defects. All sub-agents remain fixed, separating orchestration learning from executor capability improvement. Across six benchmarks spanning mathematical reasoning, scientific question answering, and multi-hop retrieval, DynaFlow achieves 88.08% overall accuracy in Forced mode, outperforming the strongest evaluated baseline by 10.90 percentage points with the same Qwen3.5-27B backbone. Workflow analysis finds more explicit use, verification, and refinement of upstream outputs after training, highlighting cross-stage information flow as a key dimension of multi-agent orchestration.

papers.title: GNSS Anomaly Detection in Urban Canyons: A Comprehensive Survey of Multimodal Visibility Inference
papers.abstract: Reliable GNSS positioning in dense urban environments depends on assessing satellite visibility and identifying measurements degraded by non-line-of-sight (NLOS) reception and multipath. This survey organizes reception-state inference into three complementary evidence families: receiver-side signals, 3D maps and environmental models, and auxiliary sensors. Receiver-side approaches span antenna/electromagnetic, tracking/baseband, and observable-domain evidence, interpreted through rule-based, statistical, machine-learning, and deep-learning methods. Map-based approaches are examined by reviewing environmental representations and methods such as geometric screening, shadow matching, 3D ray tracing, and neural implicit visibility prediction. IMU, camera, and LiDAR measurements provide complementary kinematic, visual, and geometric evidence for online screening. Across these families, we compare accuracy, interpretability, hardware and calibration requirements, map dependence, computational cost, and suitability for real-time deployment. We identify open challenges in dataset quality and labeling, domain generalization, map freshness, and resource-efficient implementation. The resulting synthesis connects signal processing, environmental modeling, and sensor fusion to guide the design of robust urban GNSS measurement-screening systems.

papers.title: Spectra, Growth, and Localization in Half-Bounded Tensor Triangular Geometry
papers.abstract: Over a noetherian scheme, classical cohomological support determines thick tensor ideals of perfect complexes. In half-bounded derived categories, complexes with the same support can generate different radical thick tensor ideals. We study how these distinctions affect the Balmer spectrum and localization. For a commutative noetherian ring $R$, we prove that $\operatorname{Spc}(\mathbf D^-_{\mathrm{fg}}(R))$ is noetherian if and only if $R$ is artinian. For a nonempty noetherian scheme $X$, the corresponding condition is $\dim X=0$. For such a ring $R$ and a finite group $G$, $\operatorname{Spc}(\mathbf D^-_{\mathrm{fg}}(RG))$ is noetherian if and only if $R$ is artinian and $|G|$ is invertible in $R$. Using the Sanders--Zhang classification over a discrete valuation ring, we compare objects whose annihilator exponents grow at different rates in different degrees. We lift the relevant generation relations before changing coefficients and obtain spectral retractions. These comparisons persist after thick quotients and algebraic localization under explicit uniform annihilation and nonvanishing conditions. A second argument uses nonnilpotent classes of positive degree and passes from cyclic subgroups to finite groups. Applications include relative results for schemes and bounded-below spectra with degreewise finitely generated homotopy. We also describe the cohomological information shared by the resulting ideals. The localization comparisons for bounded-below complexes of finitely generated modules and for bounded-below derived objects with finitely generated cohomology are established separately.

papers.title: Symmetry-resolved quasilocal entanglement as a key to Mott and pseudogap physics in plaquette CDMFT
papers.abstract: In order to identify intrinsic quantum resources in strongly interacting fermionic systems, we introduce a symmetry resolution of the parity-superselected two-site entanglement, as measured by both the fermionic negativity and the relative entropy of entanglement. We discuss how the symmetry resolution can be extended also to the full entanglement in pure and mixed two-site states. We apply our recipe to the Hubbard model, first for a dimer, and then for a plaquette cluster dynamical mean-field theory, an established method tailored to accurately capture short-range correlations. Following the evolution of the model through the interaction- and density-driven Mott transitions at zero temperature, we highlight how the three symmetry-resolved components of the two-site entanglement probe different key aspects of Mott and pseudogap physics.

papers.title: Extrapolating learned dynamics across bifurcations based on generalized synchronization
papers.abstract: Predicting dynamics across bifurcations by extrapolating trained models is crucial in diverse fields of physics. Generalized synchronization provides a framework for understanding dynamical reconstruction by neural networks, especially in the context of reservoir computing. Building on this framework, we derive a formula combining pretrained readouts to reconstruct unseen chaotic dynamics. Using classical Lagrange interpolation theory, we derive rigorous bounds on readout errors and conjugacy residuals. Numerical examples demonstrate accurate prediction of chaotic dynamics across bifurcations.

papers.title: Reliability Assessment of FRP-RC Columns Using AK-MCS with a Piecewise Two-Branch Approach
papers.abstract: Slender concrete columns reinforced with fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) bars fail at medium to high axial load levels either by concrete crushing or by loss of stability, while the tensile strains in the reinforcement remain far below the rupture strain. Each non-linear finite element (FE) analysis yields only the capacity of the governing failure mode, and the governing mode changes over a broad zone in which both capacities are nearly equal. Both characteristics conflict with active-learning Kriging-assisted Monte Carlo simulation (AK-MCS), which assumes a single, smooth limit-state function. This paper proposes a piecewise, two-branch AK-MCS framework in which each failure mode is represented by its own Kriging model, trained only on the FE analyses in which that mode governs, and the governing prediction is the minimum of both. Safeguards against data starvation keep rarely governing branches usable. After convergence, additional FE analyses are placed based on a leave-one-out calibration check and on the width of the confidence interval on the reliability index. A design-point search on the surrogate and importance sampling at the design points provide the reliability index even where direct Monte Carlo simulation finds no failure. For an FRP-reinforced concrete column example with mixed failure, 79% and 62% of the training points lie near the mode boundary. The reliability index from the design-point search agrees with the Monte Carlo estimate to within 0.05, and an FE analysis at the design point confirms the surrogate to within 0.6%.

papers.title: PhysCreator: Creating Physically-Attributed 3D Assets at Will
papers.abstract: Significant advancements in 3D asset creation have enabled high-fidelity 3D generation from images. However, most existing representations remain inherently static, lacking the ability to model physically plausible behaviors under dynamic interactions. We present \textbf{PhysCreator}, a unified framework that directly generates simulation-ready 3D representations with spatially varying physical properties from images. Unlike prior approaches that treat physical attributes as simple post-hoc predictions or rely on expensive per-instance optimization, we reformulate physical property estimation within a unified 3D representation learning framework. We introduce a voxel-aligned latent space by lifting image observations into a spatially structured 3D representation, in which geometry, appearance, and physical properties are jointly modeled and inferred in a feed-forward manner. To enable scalable learning without densely annotated physical ground truth, we leverage vision-language distillation to transfer material-aware semantic priors from powerful vision-language models into spatially grounded voxel-level supervision. Experiments demonstrate that our method achieves superior visual quality, physical plausibility, and generalization compared to prior approaches.

papers.title: Unconditional Lower Bounds for the Fredman--Khachiyan Algorithms for Monotone Boolean Duality Testing
papers.abstract: We prove unconditional lower bounds on the number of recursive calls made by the two algorithms of Fredman and Khachiyan (1996) for monotone Boolean duality testing, as a function of the explicit input size $N$. For Algorithm A we show a lower bound of $N^{\Omega(\log N)}$ on the dual pairs $(\HH_k,\LL_k)$ obtained from the read-once family of Gurvich and Khachiyan. The proof lower-bounds the number of leaves of every binary decision tree computing the function by the modulus of its multilinear polynomial evaluated at a complex point of the unit circle. It therefore applies to every choice of branching variables and, more generally, to the class of two-child variable-restriction procedures whose terminal calls have polynomially bounded decision-tree complexity. On this family the number of calls is exactly $N^{\Theta(\log N)}$. For Algorithm B, a symmetric specialization of the polynomial padding construction of Kobayashi, Kurita, and Wasa, with full polynomial blocks, yields at least $q^{(t-1)k-t(t-1)/2}$ calls, where $k=4t^2$ and $q=\Theta(t^2)$; as a function of $N$ this is $N^{\Omega(\sqrt{\log N/\log\log N})}$ along an infinite family. In an appendix we show that applying the padding construction directly to Algorithm A gives $\Omega(2^n)$ calls on a dual pair obtained from an unsatisfiable $n$-variable formula, which is only $N^{\Omega(\sqrt{\log N/\log\log N})}$ in terms of the input size. No complexity-theoretic assumption is used. The proofs allow every branching-variable choice permitted by the respective algorithm. They concern the original recursive procedures, counting every invocation separately, without sharing calls or adding positive stopping tests.

papers.title: Nonparametric Regression on the Circle with Applications to Climate and Environmental Science
papers.abstract: Two important indicators of climate change are the decline in Arctic sea ice area and the increase in average temperatures globally. Both sea ice and temperature exhibit seasonal patterns, making circular regression a natural approach for their analysis. In this paper, we construct computationally tractable Nadaraya-Watson type kernel regression estimators on the unit circle, using rate-optimal kernel density estimators. We introduce a leave-one-out cross-validation procedure for the data-driven selection of the smoothness parameter and evaluate the performance of the proposed estimators through a simulation study covering 48 scenarios, including comparisons with existing local polynomial estimators. We then apply our methodology to historical Arctic sea ice area data and daily temperature observations in Stockholm. The fitted regression functions and their derivatives or finite differences allow us to investigate changes in both the levels and seasonal dynamics of these environmental indicators. In particular, we observe a decline in fitted sea ice area and substantial changes in its seasonal rates of growth and retreat, together with higher fitted temperatures across most of the year in Stockholm during the more recent period in comparison to historical data.

papers.title: Resolving a Clumpy Disk Wind in 4U 1957+115 with XRISM
papers.abstract: We present a high-resolution XRISM/Resolve observation of the persistent black hole candidate 4U 1957+115, revealing the first detection of an intrinsic disk wind in this source. The absorption is dominated by highly ionized Fe XXV and Fe XXVI and varies substantially throughout the observation, becoming prominent during the final $\sim40$ ks despite a modest decrease of only $\sim5$--$10\%$ in source flux. The observed evolution of the absorption cannot be explained solely by ionization changes driven by the modest continuum variability, favoring an inhomogeneous outflow with evolving line-of-sight properties. Time-resolved spectroscopy reveals substantially narrower absorption features in shorter intervals, with the inferred turbulent velocity decreasing from $\sim350~{\rm km/s}$ in the longer integration to $\lesssim70~{\rm km/s}$ in the shortest selections. This suggests that the broader absorption profiles measured over longer integrations may result, at least in part, from averaging over an evolving wind rather than from intrinsically larger turbulent velocities. Such time averaging can therefore affect the inferred physical properties of the wind and complicate efforts to identify its launching mechanism. Even though the wind carries only a small fraction of the radiative luminosity in kinetic form, its mass-loss rate may remain dynamically relevant. These results highlight the importance of time-resolved, high-resolution X-ray spectroscopy for characterizing the structure and variability of accretion disk winds.

papers.title: Space-Time Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces for Doppler-Resilient LEO Broadcasting
papers.abstract: Stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIMs) cascade programmable layers in front of a feed. In the SIM designs reported so far, including those proposed for low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites, the layer coefficients are space-only controls or are varied randomly in time to support opportunistic scheduling, so that every radiated beam carries the frequency of the feed. This paper introduces space-time SIMs (ST-SIMs), whose layers are modulated in time and use the temporal dimension of the stack deterministically: each spatial mode of the aperture is paired with its own prescribed frequency translation. The application is LEO broadcasting, where a common waveform reaches terminals with different Doppler shifts, and any common Doppler correction leaves residuals of up to half the Doppler span. We derive the harmonic-domain model of the stack, solve the minimum-energy space-frequency synthesis in closed form, and prove that full column rank of the steering matrix is necessary and sufficient for decoupling K terminal-specific translations, a result that extends to groups of terminals. We further propose a phase-only synthesis algorithm with guaranteed stationarity, together with quantization and control-rate laws. Simulations at 20 GHz over 50 random drops show that a four-layer ST-SIM with a single radio-frequency chain removes the Doppler floor of a static SIM for footprint radii above about 45 km and, under the ideal phase-only model and at equal radiated peak energy, approaches ideal digital per-terminal precompensation within 0.5 dB for resolvable terminals, whereas, in the evaluated geometries, a single time-modulated layer cannot synthesize the required modes.

papers.title: Rigorous Lower Bounds for Atomic and Ionic Ground-State Energies
papers.abstract: We establish a new iterative method for computing rigorous lower bounds for the ground-state energies of all atoms and ions. The accuracy of the resulting bounds depends on two ingredients: the quality of the initial energy estimate and the quality of the used upper bound for the maximum number of bound electrons, $N_c(Z)$, as a function of the nuclear charge $Z>0$. In particular, this new method allows us to establish the explicit lower bound $E(N,Z) \geq -0.8710\,N^{1/3}Z^2$ for the ground-state energy $E(N,Z)$ of the atom/ion with $N \in \mathbb{N}$ electrons and nuclear charge $Z \in (0,N]$, thereby considerably improving the best known constant $A=(3/2)^{1/3} \approx 1.1447$ in the estimate $E(N,Z) \geq -A\,N^{1/3}Z^2$ for $0 < Z \leq N$ and coming much closer to the best possible constant given by the Thomas-Fermi asymptotics $\lim_{N \to \infty} |E(N,N)|N^{-7/3}= -E_{\text{TF}}(1)\approx 0.7687$ derived in Adv. Math., 23(1) by Lieb and Simon. To demonstrate the potential and the limits of our method, we also compute explicit lower bounds for the ground-state energies $E(N,N)$ of all atoms with $2 \leq N \leq 86$ and we compare them with the bounds obtained in J. Chem. Phys., 62(8) by Hertel, Lieb, Thirring and the bounds obtained by Seco in his dissertation. Finally, we also provide a uniqueness result for the expectation values of the kinetic, potential and interaction energies on the ground-state space.

papers.title: A symmetric extension of Zhao's series for $\zeta(5)$
papers.abstract: We prove a four-parameter extension of Zhao's series for $\zeta(5)$. Restricting a Wilf-Zeilberger seed of Au to a hyperplane, we obtain a summand in five parameters with zero sum that is symmetric under all their permutations. Summing it from two different starting points gives two trigonometric closed forms, which we prove by Guillera's periodicity argument. The proof is self-contained, and also gives a companion series for $1/\pi^2$, which we have not found in the literature.
