We find these competences pull in opposite directions for vision-language models: closed-form questions reward precise, evidence-grounded reasoning, while open-ended answers are scored by similarity to reference text, where matching the annotation style matters as much as reasoning correctly. We present Reason-or-Recite (RoR), a two-specialist framework for the Traffic Anomaly Reasoning track of the 2026 AI City Challenge. RoR (1) rewrites the official chain-of-thought annotations into a structured, temporally grounded schema and LoRA-tunes a 9B vision-language model on the enhanced traces; (2) fine-tunes a 4-bit-quantized 27B model on answers alone, absorbing the annotation style; and (3) selects between the two candidates per question with a training-free LLM judge. RoR ranks first on the in-domain leaderboard with mean score 0.6788.

papers.title: Reinforcement learning for constrained stochastic linear--quadratic control in continuous time
papers.abstract: We study continuous-time stochastic linear--quadratic control with a scalar state and nonnegative control constraints. With quadratic running costs, randomized exploration can change the optimal mean feedback. We introduce an auxiliary problem without entropy in which the conditional policy mean is nonnegative and the covariance is prescribed in proportion to the squared state. Moment reduction and state separation yield two regional Riccati equations and characterize the finite-horizon value function and optimal conditional mean. We give a sufficient control--cost compatibility condition under which this mean coincides with the optimal feedback of the original constrained problem. For time-invariant coefficients, we characterize the undiscounted infinite-horizon optimum and establish mean square asymptotic stability under the stated assumptions. For unknown dynamics, we develop model-free actor--critic schemes for finite and infinite horizons. Numerical experiments compare the learned policies with their analytical targets and examine the effect of exploration on the optimal mean.

papers.title: Rigid Band Shift in Electron-Doped Kagome Metal
papers.abstract: We study the effects of Sn-site doping on the electronic structure of nonmagnetic kagome metal YV$_6$Sn$_{6-x}$Sb$_x$ by infrared spectroscopy and density-functional theory. The results for samples with $x$ = 0 and 1.4 demonstrate that partial substitution of Sn by Sb acts as a rigid shift of the Fermi level while leaving the band dispersion largely intact. Our findings establish Sn-site substitution in YV$_6$Sn$_6$ as a route to systematically investigate band-filling-dependent electronic properties of nonmagnetic kagome metals.

papers.title: Breakdown-Resistant Hierarchical Bayesian Calibration for Multi-Center Clinical Trials
papers.abstract: Multi-center clinical trials are threatened by systematic location shifts in biomarkers measured across devices, sites, or reagent batches. Hierarchical Bayesian models are the standard remedy, borrowing strength across centers by pooling center-specific estimates. However, we prove that the standard Gaussian hierarchical posterior has a breakdown point of zero \emph{at the level of the posterior distribution itself}: a single contaminated center drives the posterior mean of every clean center to infinity and collapses the coverage of every clean center's credible interval to zero. We introduce the Posterior-Median Hierarchical Calibration (PMHC) framework, a fully Bayesian hierarchical model that replaces the Gaussian prior on center-specific shifts with a Laplace prior. Under absolute loss, the posterior median is the natural Bayes estimator, and we prove that its breakdown point is $\lfloor (K+1)/2 \rfloor$ contaminated centers---whereas the Gaussian posterior mean has breakdown point zero for every $K$. PMHC retains a full posterior distribution, enabling meaningful credible intervals and posterior probabilities. Across $K \in \{5, 10, 20\}$ centers and $n \in \{50, 200, 1000\}$ observations per center, PMHC maintains $94$--$98\%$ coverage under contamination fraction $\epsilon = 0.60$, while Gaussian pooling collapses to $0.0\%$ coverage and its point estimate diverges by a factor of $54$. On real NHANES data ($n = 60{,}651$ across nine cycles), contamination in three cycles collapsed the Gaussian coverage to \(0.0\%\) and shifted clean cycles by \(0.41\) mg/dL, whereas PMHC maintained \(94.0\%\) coverage with a shift of \(0.008\) mg/dL. To our knowledge, this is the first explicit breakdown analysis of the \emph{posterior distribution} in hierarchical Bayesian pooling, and the first Bayesian model that is simultaneously contamination-robust and efficient in the clean-data regime.

papers.title: Aspherical Symplectic Manifolds with Positive First Chern Degree
papers.abstract: For every integer $n\ge5$, we construct a closed aspherical symplectic manifold of real dimension $2n$ with positive first Chern degree. Each example is a flat torus bundle over the same compact hyperbolic surface, with arithmetic monodromy arising from an explicit indefinite quaternion division algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$. We identify its symplectic first Chern class with the pullback of the canonical class of the base and compute its degree explicitly. Asphericity rules out nonconstant pseudoholomorphic spheres for every tame almost complex structure. Thus these examples give a negative answer to the symplectic uniruledness question of Boucksom--Demailly--P\u{a}un--Peternell in every even real dimension at least ten.

papers.title: Conformal Novelty Detection via Data-enhanced Localization
papers.abstract: Novelty detection is an important area of research in both statistics and machine learning. In this paper, we focus on the conditional novelty detection problem, where novelties arise from the relationship between different variables. We first adopt the conformal inference framework and propose a data-enhanced localized conformal p-value, constructed by recalibrating an enhanced conditional distribution estimator. This estimator efficiently captures conditional information by incorporating both calibration and test data into its kernel estimation. We show that our p-values are valid in finite samples and can improve detection efficiency. Based on this p-value, we then develop a novel conditional novelty detection algorithm, along with a data-driven bandwidth selection method that ensures finite-sample false discovery rate control while enhancing detection power. Both simulated and real data experiments demonstrate the advantages of our proposed approach.

papers.title: Genus Increase in Closed Mean Curvature Flows
papers.abstract: We construct counterexamples to Ilmanen's genus-reduction conjecture for closed mean curvature flows. We prove that a compact hypersurface with a single isolated conical singularity and a power rate of convergence to its cone admits a mean curvature flow whose forward rescaled limit is a prescribed expander smoothly asymptotic to that cone. Combining this theorem with closed mean curvature flows with prescribed tangent flows (arXiv:2405.15577, arXiv:2607.23879) and the noncompact counterexample (arXiv:2605.09657) gives the desired examples.

papers.title: More Memory, Better Videos? A Controlled Study of Visual Memory in Long-Video Generation
papers.abstract: Long-video generators increasingly retrieve past visual observations to prevent identity drift. The intuition is compelling: more access to history should make future video more consistent. But an image can be faithful to the past and wrong for the present. Does visual memory always improve the generated story? We investigate this question through VMem-Bench, a two-track diagnostic study. Track-A measures which references are selected from 92 real films (16,548 segments), before generation and without generator confounds. Track-B compares four retrieval policies with no-memory and gold-informed last-seen controls on 30 causally generated stories (2,824 segments) using a shared generator. Retrieval increases entity recall from 0.559 to 0.628-0.693 and improves similarity to past appearances, but decreases precision from 0.977 to 0.915-0.938 and forbidden-entity avoidance from 0.968 to 0.845-0.898. It can also reinforce obsolete appearances after the story changes them. Conversely, high long-gap recall can arise without memory when the prompt itself supplies the appearance; an appearance-stripping analysis exposes this confound. These results distinguish historical fidelity from current-story correctness and show why retrieval relevance or final-video consistency alone does not establish memory utility.

papers.title: DUET4D: Self-Corrective Coupled Guidance for Sparse-View 4D Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Sparse-view 4D reconstruction is highly under-constrained when only a few cameras are available. Generative priors can recover missing appearances, but video models are computationally impractical for iterative reconstruction, whereas single-view models produce temporally inconsistent pseudo-observations. Moreover, directly absorbing uncertain generative outputs into Gaussian optimization often creates redundant primitives and floating artifacts. To address these challenges, we propose DUET4D, a self-corrective coupled guidance framework for sparse-view 4D Gaussian splatting. The core of our approach is a self-corrective framework where the 4D representation guides generative prior for spatio-temporal consistent supervisions. We first construct sequential alignments from current Gaussian evidence to steer the latent restoration. Then we use Sequential Fidelity Resampling to lift generative supervisions into Gaussian space to selectively distinguish repeatedly supported primitives. The corrected representation then provides more reliable Gaussian evidence for the next restoration cycle. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DUET4D significantly improves rendering quality and rendering efficiency.

papers.title: The Choice Number of Random Graphs
papers.abstract:
In 1999, Alon, Krivelevich and Sudakov conjectured that the choice number and chromatic number of the random graph $G(n,p)$ are asymptotically equal whenever $np\to\infty$. We prove their conjecture, showing that, with high probability, $$ \operatorname{ch}(G(n,p))=(1+o(1))\chi(G(n,p)) $$ whenever $np\to\infty$. This improves the bound $\operatorname{ch}(G(n,p))\le(2+o(1))\chi(G(n,p))$ for $np\to\infty$ and $p\le0.9$ obtained by Krivelevich and Vu in 2001.
  Our proof distinguishes two cases according to the size of independent sets. When independent sets of growing size are available, we establish a sharper uniform independent-set estimate that eliminates the factor-two loss in the bound of Krivelevich and Vu. When independent sets have bounded size, we establish a deterministic result showing that, under a suitable uniform independent-set condition, a proper colouring with bounded colour-class sizes yields an asymptotically matching upper bound on the choice number.

papers.title: Follow the Regularized Leader Does Not Converge in Constrained Optimization
papers.abstract: Follow the regularized leader (FTRL) is a foundational algorithm in online learning whose regret properties have been extensively studied for decades. However, in stark contrast to mirror descent---and gradient descent in particular---the convergence of FTRL to first-order stationary points in constrained nonconvex optimization was not well understood. In this paper, we show that continuous-time FTRL can fail to converge even asymptotically in infinitely smooth constrained optimization problems: its Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) gap can remain bounded away from zero indefinitely. This is especially surprising in light of the fact that continuous-time FTRL guarantees a monotonic improvement of the objective value. As a result, we establish that non-convergent behavior of no-regret dynamics---which besets general variational inequality problems---can occur even in potential systems. From a technical standpoint, our construction relies on an infinitely differentiable function where the gradient flow dynamics exhibit decelerating oscillations without ever converging pointwise, which we in turn embed into higher-dimensional FTRL dynamics that sustain a perpetually large KKT gap. We complement our negative result by showing that FTRL with Euclidean regularization does converge when the objective function is analytic. This shows that the analytic property plays a more fundamental role for FTRL than for gradient flow: it governs not only pointwise convergence, but convergence to first-order stationarity itself.

papers.title: Shifted Window Temporal Transformer for YOLO-Guided Phase Recognition in Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy Surgery
papers.abstract: Intelligent operating rooms require accurate awareness of surgical workflow for better intra-operative decisions, teamwork, and surgical documentation. Therefore, accurately recognizing surgical phase during surgery is crucial. However, previous artificial intelligence-based methods provide fluctuating predictions for the transitions, restricting their clinical use. To address this challenge, we propose a clinically meaningful framework that integrates a Swin Transformer and Temporal Transformer Encoder (TTE) for effective surgical phase recognition and a parallel YOLOv11s network for real-time surgical instrument localization. To avoid phase flickering and to produce stable workflow predictions, a causal temporal smoothing is applied. The proposed framework is tested on the Cholec80 dataset for the simultaneous recognition of the surgical phases and instruments. The overall phase recognition accuracy of this model was 92%, and the macro average F1-score was 0.86. This performance surpasses CNN based methods such as EndoNet (81.7%) and SV-RCNet (85.3%), as well as temporal convolutional and transformer-based approaches including TeCNO (88.6%), Trans-SVNet (90.9%), and LoViT (91.5%). Besides, the module of instrument detection achieved mAP@0.5 = 0.863. The reliability of the results is confirmed, obtaining a high recognition rate of the workflows, and a high accuracy of the localization of the instruments. The proposed framework can serve as a foundation for intelligent surgical assistance, enriching situation awareness, and potential robotic surgery applications. Code will be made publicly available at: https://github.com/ac005sheekar/LapChol-Surgery-Swin-Cholec80

papers.title: Non-liftability of the field of norms of the $p$-adic false Tate curve extension
papers.abstract: Let $p\geq3$ be a prime number. We prove that the action of the Galois group on the field of norms of the $p$-adic false Tate curve extension $\mathbf{Q}_p\left(\zeta_{p^\infty},p^{1/p^\infty}\right)$ of $\mathbf{Q}_p$ is not liftable to its Cohen ring with respect to any admissible coefficient field.

papers.title: When the Persona Contradicts the Line: Diagnosing Plan-to-Synthesis Failures in Chain-of-Thought TTS
papers.abstract: Chain-of-thought TTS systems rely on language-model planners to translate persona and context into vocal delivery, but it is unclear where this intent is lost when the requested affect conflicts with lexical sentiment. We introduce a bilingual Japanese--English persona--line conflict benchmark in which each item pairs one line with congruent and conflicting personas and pre-declares the expected acoustic direction. We probe this direction in the planner-generated delivery phrase, the planner-written emotion vector, the QwenEmotion-generated vector, and the rendered waveform. Planner outputs are usually direction-correct, while downstream agreement can be substantially lower. Bypassing QwenEmotion provides only modest gains over the full planner-controlled Base. Supervising QwenEmotion raises the direction rate to 75% in Japanese and 84% in English. A learned text-to-latent interface reaches the highest English rate of 89% and the highest Japanese arousal rate of 88%. These results show that learned repair of the plan-to-synthesis interface can recover counter-textual delivery, although its effect differs across languages and acoustic axes.

papers.title: Non-Maxwellianity in Temperature Relaxation between Plasma Species
papers.abstract: Temperature relaxation between plasma species is usually described by Landau--Spitzer (LS) theory, which assumes Maxwellian distributions throughout. We show analytically that, for two Maxwellian species in homogeneous isotropic plasmas, the interspecies collisions driving relaxation generate a universal three-lobe initial distortion and that these distortions initially reduce energy exchange over a broad parameter range. Full Fokker--Planck simulations reveal substantial relaxation delays when interspecies deformation competes with self-thermalization. For post-shock deuterium--tritium plasmas relevant to inertial confinement fusion, with $T_{\mathrm{T}}/T_{\mathrm{D}}=1.5$, the relaxation time exceeds the LS prediction by 47%. The accompanying distortions lower the apparent DD/DT temperature ratio and produce positive DD and negative DT Gamow-shift residuals relative to Maxwellian predictions. These results also motivate examining non-Maxwellianity in fuel heating by fusion $\alpha$ particles.

papers.title: JevVLA: Jev-Inspired Energy-Based Adaptation for Vision-Language-Action Policies
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies can select among discrete candidates for pick-and-place manipulation or generate continuous action chunks for motion control. Improving both forms of decision making through a common mechanism while retaining the capabilities of a pretrained policy is an important adaptation problem. Inspired by Jev's structured, probabilistic decision interface, we propose JevVLA, a lightweight energy-based adaptation framework for VLA policies. JevVLA instantiates this inspiration by modeling the relative quality of action proposals: with the base policy frozen, it learns a differentiable scalar energy conditioned on observations, task context, and actions, using execution feedback, expert corrections, or demonstration-derived preferences. JevVLA uses this single learned action preference function in two ways: its values compare discrete candidates, while its action gradients correct continuous actions or guide their generation. Candidate selection and continuous control thus share one trainable decision core. Each benchmark uses independently trained weights and fixed input/output encodings, while retaining the same core network with approximately 80,000 trainable parameters. On the held-out test sets, JevVLA improves task success over the respective matched base-policy controls by 1.28, 2.31, 1.60, 1.52, and 1.28 percentage points on MetaWorld MT50, VIMA, LanguageTable, LIBERO Plus, and CLIPort, respectively. These results support the feasibility of a lightweight, Jev-inspired energy model for adapting both discrete action selection and continuous action guidance. The JevVLA implementation will be open-sourced at https://github.com/ZJU4EmbodiedAI/JevVLA.

papers.title: Inverse heat source problem from terminal data on a set of low Hausdorff dimension
papers.abstract: We study the recovery of a spatial source in the heat equation from terminal observations on a compact interior set $E$ with positive $\beta$ dimensional Hausdorff content for some $\beta>d-1$. The prescribed temporal forcing vanishes on a nontrivial interval immediately preceding the observation time. Under a spectral Sobolev prior and a quantitative noncancellation condition on the terminal spectral multipliers, we establish conditional logarithmic stability. For scattered observations on such sets, we derive a sampling inequality under a quasi uniformity assumption. Under explicit sampling and independent noise assumptions, we prove a logarithmic convergence rate in probability for the corresponding Tikhonov reconstructions with a data driven parameter choice. Two numerical experiments using a finite candidate approximation of a fixed Hausdorff set assess discrete spectral sampling stability and illustrate the effects of the waiting interval and measurement noise on reconstruction.

papers.title: An eight-dimensional nilpotent Leibniz algebra without outer derivations
papers.abstract: Jacobson's classical theorem asserts that every nilpotent Lie algebra admits a non-inner derivation. This result, however, does not extend to Leibniz algebras: there exists an eight-dimensional complex nilpotent Leibniz algebra whose every derivation is inner. In this paper, we present a systematic investigation of this algebra, with particular emphasis on the absence of outer derivations and its structural properties. We describe its lower central series, annihilators, center, and Leibniz kernel, and prove that its derivation algebra is a six-dimensional nilpotent Lie algebra isomorphic to the quotient of the algebra by its Leibniz kernel. We further show that its automorphism group is a connected six-dimensional unipotent group obtained by exponentiating inner derivations; in particular, it contains no nontrivial elements of finite order. In addition, we provide a complete classification of the quasiderivation, generalized derivation, and $\sigma$-derivation of the algebra. Finally, we show that, among the four linearly independent infinitesimal deformations, exactly one is integrable, giving rise to a one-parameter family of pairwise non-isomorphic algebras which, with a single exception, also admit only inner derivations.

papers.title: When Pointing Becomes Profiling: Social Bias and Refusal in Text-Steerable Visual Encoders
papers.abstract: Text-steerable visual encoders condition a frozen Vision Transformer on a natural-language prompt and point at the matching image region, producing prompt-conditioned heatmaps and features. We audit the released SteerViT model and find that its steering interface turns language-driven pointing into demographic profiling. On counterfactual face mosaics and real multi-person photographs, "the person" selects a man more often than the base rate, crime words select Black people more often than occupation words do, "the man" among four women selects the Black woman 75.6% of the time on SocialCounterfactuals, and "the monkey" selects Black people. None of them is in the backbone's unsteered saliency, and the crime association is not in the frozen text encoder; the race effects grow with steering strength and enter through the last two cross-attention layers: giving the prompt to those layers alone reproduces them. Four other grounding models, CLIPSeg, Grounding-DINO, SAM 3, and Qwen2.5-VL, show no crime routing and weaker race routing. The model cannot refuse. Its patch softmax must place its mass somewhere, and its heatmap separates a groundable request ("the police officer") from one that is absent ("the pizza") or that would require a stereotyped demographic inference ("the criminal") only at chance (AUROC 0.52). We introduce SafeSteer, which adds a learned abstention output and counterfactual-invariance training on the same 23M steering parameters. SafeSteer separates should-point from should-abstain prompts at AUROC 0.997, generalizes to held-out sensitive and absent words (0.998; at a 0.5 threshold it refuses 99.8% of trained and 62% of held-out sensitive words) with no over-refusal of visible people on the benchmark, and removes most race routing while keeping localization and retrieval within 1 point of the released model. Code, benchmarks, and the curated mosaic sets will be released.

papers.title: Zero-Shot Monocular Depth Estimation for Visual Perception in Lower-Limb Prostheses
papers.abstract: Monocular depth estimation has advanced rapidly with the development of foundation models that demonstrate strong zero-shot generalisation across diverse visual domains. However, the applicability of these models to visual perception for lower-limb prosthetics remains largely unexplored. Reliable depth perception is particularly important for prosthesis users, who often experience significant challenges when navigating stairs, uneven terrain, and other complex environments. To address this gap, we introduce the Lower-Limb Prosthesis (LP) dataset, a benchmark designed to evaluate depth perception from an emulated knee-level prosthetic viewpoint. Using this dataset, we evaluate four state-of-the-art monocular depth estimation foundation models. Our results provide the first systematic benchmark of monocular depth estimation performance from a prosthetic viewpoint, while highlighting both the challenges and the potential of deploying foundation models in prosthetic perception systems. The code and dataset are available at https://github.com/Ishivijay/lp_dataset.

papers.title: Optimal Rates in Local and Central Limit Theorems for the Elephant Random Walk
papers.abstract: We determine the optimal rates of convergence in the local and central limit theorems for the one-dimensional elephant random walk in the diffusive and critical regimes, $0\le p\le3/4$. For every fixed initial distribution, we treat both exact finite-time centering and standardization and the normalization $S_n/\sqrt n$ (or $S_n/\sqrt{n\log n}$ at criticality). We establish uniform Edgeworth expansions for local probabilities and distribution functions, and use these expansions to derive the optimal convergence rates, which exhibit several phase transitions depending on the symmetry of the initial distribution, the normalization, and the type of approximation. Our approach uses elephant polynomials for precise characteristic-function expansions and a random recursive tree representation for global Fourier bounds.

papers.title: Multiple harmonic star sums involving central binomial coefficients as weights
papers.abstract: We consider weighted analogues of multiple harmonic and multiple $t$-harmonic star sums, where the "star" indicates non-strict inequalities between the summation indices. In the special case where all exponents are 2, which is of particular interest also for ordinary multiple ($t$-)harmonic star sums, we obtain evaluations in terms of simple finite sums. The proofs are based on several combinatorial identities which are of interest in their own right.

papers.title: Martingality in EFM Signature Volatility Models
papers.abstract: We establish a martingality criterion for the Exponentially Fading Memory (EFM) signature volatility model, extending the recent result of Abi Jaber, Gassiat, and Sotnikov (2026). In the proposed framework, the volatility process is given by a linear functional of the EFM signature of a time-augmented Brownian motion, which yields a globally well-behaved, fully non-Markovian volatility model admitting a stationary distribution. The stationary EFM signature volatility model is also covered by allowing for a random initial value of the signature. Moreover, the volatility process can be adjusted to the initial forward variance curve. For this model, excluding trivial cases, we prove that the price process is a true martingale if and only if the truncation order is odd and a sign condition involving the correlation parameter holds.

papers.title: Automorphisms of $\mathbb{P}^1$-bundles over rational surfaces in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: We study $\mathbb{P}^1$-bundles over smooth projective rational surfaces over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, together with the actions of their neutral automorphism groups. After an equivariant square birational reduction to the projective plane or a Hirzebruch surface, we classify the possible induced actions on the base and identify the families relevant to relative maximality. For $p\geq 3$, we prove that every such $\mathbb{P}^1$-bundle is equivariantly square birational to one whose neutral automorphism group is relatively maximal, and we classify all bundles with this property. We also describe all equivariant square birational maps between these relatively maximal bundles and determine which are stiff or superstiff, the analogues of rigidity and superrigidity for $\mathbb{P}^1$-bundles.

papers.title: Comparisons of benchmark equivalence relations
papers.abstract:
We determine the Borel-reducibility comparison of each pair of $\mathbf\Pi^0_3$ benchmark equivalence relations in Gao's monograph. The additional comparisons we prove are $E_\infty\leq_B c_0$, $E_\infty
leq_B\ell_p$ for $2<p<\infty$, $\ell_p
leq_B{\equiv_m}$ for $2<p<\infty$, $c_0
leq_B{\equiv_m}$, $c_0
leq_B\ell_\infty^+$ and $\equiv_m
leq_B\ell_\infty^+$. Together with the previous positive direction, these give $\ell_p\leq_B{\equiv_m}$ if and only if $p\leq2$. These answer several questions in Gao's monograph and Kanovei' monograph. We also prove that unitary equivalence of all bounded linear operators is not Borel reducible to $\equiv_m$. This answers a question of Ding and Gao. Equivalently, unitary equivalence of arbitrary representations of $F_\infty$ is strictly more complicated than that of arbitrary representations of $\mathbb Z$. This answers a question of Thomas.

papers.title: Detection of Single Stuck-at and Bridging Faults in Cluster-based FPGA Architectures
papers.abstract: This paper presents a new technique for detecting single stuck-at and bridging faults in cluster-based FPGA architectures, using same set of test vectors generated by a test pattern generator circuitry. This technique is based on configuration of logic elements using test logic structure and the outputs of two separated logic elements are compared to detect a fault. To do this, block under test, TPG and output response analysis circuitry are generated in FPGAs. The configurations of test pattern generation, block under test and output response analysis are also discussed in this paper. The novelty lies in the fact that the same set of test vectors can detect all the stuck-at as well as bridging faults if the test vectors are applied in a particular sequence and analyzing the output results. We presented a detail analysis of results to detect faults as well.

papers.title: On almost perfect additive complements
papers.abstract: Let $A, B$ be infinite sets of non-negative integers with $n\in A+B$ for all sufficiently large integers $n$. We prove that if $A(x)B(x)-x$ does not tend to infinity, then $$\limsup_{x\to\infty}\frac{A(x)B(x)}{x}\in\Big[\frac{3}{2}, 2\Big].$$ The lower bound is sharp, and confirms a conjecture of Chen. Our proof is based on the weak limits and the convolution factorization theorem of Gabardo and Lai. A discrete proof of the same bound was also given by Zhang. Motivated by the known spectrum of perfect additive complements, we conjecture that the interval $(3/2, 8/5)$ is also excluded for almost perfect additive complements.

papers.title: Testing independence in contamination models
papers.abstract: We consider a bivariate contamination model in which the distribution of a gold standard is known, while the mixing weight and the distribution of the contaminant component are unknown, and we test whether the two coordinates of the unknown component are independent. Classical independence tests are meaningless here, since a mixture of product distributions is not a product distribution. Following the Inversion-Best Matching principle, we invert the model for every candidate weight and compare the inverted distribution of the unknown component with the product of its marginals. The weight is estimated where they are closest in a Cramer-von Mises sense, and the scaled minimal distance is the test statistic. An exact quadratic structure makes the estimator computable without numerical optimisation and yields a transparent asymptotic theory under both hypotheses. The null distribution is calibrated by a multiplier bootstrap. Simulations and applications to gene expression data and spam filtering illustrate the method.

papers.title: Synthetic Child-Adult Interactions Are Not Developmentally Plausible
papers.abstract: Synthetic data has become a common resource for training language models, and this trend has spilled over into research on developmentally plausible language modeling. However, it remains unclear whether LM-generated child-adult interactions actually resemble natural ones. We compare the synthetic TinyDialogues dataset to natural dialogue across a broad range of linguistic measures. While synthetic data matches natural data on the lexical level, it drastically underestimates the messy, fragmented nature of spoken interaction. To mitigate this, we propose instruction-tuning with data created from real dialogues, and show in a pilot study that a small model approximates the statistical tendencies of natural data after moderate parameter-efficient fine-tuning.

papers.title: Galois groups of polynomials over a fixed number field: determinant methods in general boxes, resolvents, and quantitative counting
papers.abstract:
Let $K$ be a fixed number field of degree $d$. We prove two determinant-method results for integral points over $\mathcal O_K$ in boxes whose coordinates may have different size bounds: a Bombieri-Pila type estimate for affine plane curves that retains the two separate coordinate bounds, and a Salberger-Browning covering theorem for affine surfaces. If $F\in\mathcal O_K[X_1,X_2]$ is irreducible and $T=\max B_1^{e_1}B_2^{e_2}$ over the monomials occurring in $F$, then \[
  N_K(F;B_1,B_2)\ll T^\varepsilon
  \exp\!\left(d\frac{\log B_1\log B_2}{\log T}\right). \] For an absolutely irreducible surface in three variables we obtain a covering by $O(T^\varepsilon V_{3,K})$ bounded-degree auxiliary hypersurfaces, outside $O(T^\varepsilon V_{3,K}^2)$ exceptional integral points, where \[
  V_{3,K}=\exp\!\left(d
  \left(\frac{\log B_1\log B_2\log B_3}{\log T}\right)^{1/2}\right). \] These are the number-field analogues of determinant-method estimates for unequal coordinate ranges developed in the rational setting by Browning and Heath-Brown, Salberger, Browning, and Chow-Dietmann. We then apply them to Galois resolvents of monic degree-$n$ polynomials over $K$. Independently, a large-sieve argument, in the tradition of Gallagher's probabilistic Galois theory, gives $O_{K,n}(N^{dn-d/2}\log N)$ exceptional separable polynomials, while effective Hilbert irreducibility over global fields gives subgroup-sensitive bounds with exponent $d(n-1+1/[S_n:G])$, up to logarithms. We record the interaction with the discriminant-square equation for even groups, congruence restrictions, and rectangular coefficient boxes. All determinant estimates used in the applications are proved in the paper; no conjectural global-field determinant statement is assumed.

papers.title: Quasi locally free sheaves on primitive double schemes
papers.abstract: Let $X_2$ be a complex primitive double scheme, $X=(X_2)_{red}$. The ideal sheaf of $X$ is a line bundle on $X$. Let $E$ be a coherent sheaf on $X_2$. Then there exists a nonempty open subset $U$ of $X_2$ and integers $m_1$, $m_2$, uniquely determined by $E$, such that $E_{|U}$ is locally isomorphic to $(O_X\otimes C^{m_1})\oplus(O_{X_2}\otimes C^{m_2})$. If we can take $U=X_2$, we say the $E$ is quasi locally free. If $m_1=1$ we say that $E$ is rigid. In this case, we show that deformations of $E$ are of the same type. So locally free sheaves and rigid quasi locally free sheaves on $X_2$ play the same role on $X_2$ as locally free sheaves do on smooth schemes. In this paper we study the existence and description of quasi locally free sheaves, and flat families of such sheaves.

papers.title: Supercritical Geometric Optics for multidimensional scalar conservation laws
papers.abstract: This article studies the propagation, near a smooth non-constant ground state, of monophase oscillatory wave trains with small amplitude and very high frequency for multidimensional nonlinear scalar conservation laws. These oscillations lie beyond the classical regime of uniformly bounded variation. Two scenarios may occur. Under suitable compatibility conditions, the oscillations propagate. Otherwise, they are damped through shock formation. In the baseline supercritical regime, we give an explicit criterion distinguishing these two behaviors and justify the corresponding asymptotic descriptions. At higher frequencies, the propagation mechanism becomes more restrictive and is governed by compatibility conditions involving a Lie algebra. Under a natural local constant-rank assumption, we obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of complete WKB expansions. We also prove cancellation under first-order incompatibility. Perturbing a non-constant background state limits the propagation of small scales compared with the constant-background case. Our constructions contribute to the understanding of the fractional smoothing effect conjectured by Lions, Perthame and Tadmor.

papers.title: Macro Mondrian Conformal Risk Control
papers.abstract: Conformal Risk Control (CRC) extends conformal prediction beyond the coverage setting to the control of general monotone loss functions, in a distribution-free and modelagnostic fashion. This makes it well-suited to problems with high-dimensional targets, such as the semantic segmentation task addressed in this work. However, CRC guarantees only marginal control, meaning that the risk is controlled on average over the data distribution. Under imbalanced distributions, the risk on inputs that contain rare objects may therefore remain uncontrolled, even when the marginal guarantee holds. We propose a new method that controls the risk on average over user-defined groups of the domain, drawing on Mondrian conformal prediction and macro-coverage algorithms. The method relies on a taxonomy, that is, a function that assigns a group to each data point, and reweights each point's risk by a coefficient that depends on its group probability, so that rare points contribute more than common ones. We illustrate the approach on two semantic segmentation datasets.

papers.title: Intersection multiplicity of a sparse curve and a trinomial curve
papers.abstract: Let f $\in$ C[x, y] be a trinomial and let g $\in$ C[x, y] be a sparse polynomial with N monomials (N $\ge$ 1). We address the problem of bounding the local intersection multiplicity of the bivariate polynomial system f = g = 0 at an isolated root q $\in$ (C * )^ 2 only in terms of N . Our main result establishes that the local multiplicity of the system at any isolated solution q $\in$ (C * ) ^2 is at most (N -1)(N +2)/ 2 , independently of the degrees of f and g. Furthermore, we know that this bound is sharp for N = 3.

papers.title: Revealing Imaging Characteristics of Thermal Wakes from Underwater Vehicles Without Cooling-Water Discharge
papers.abstract: Small uncrewed underwater vehicles are proliferating and threaten maritime security, yet evade sonar and magnetic sensors built for larger submarines. Infrared thermal wakes, generated by hydrodynamic displacement that modulates the cold-skin layer, offer a non-acoustic, non-magnetic alternative even without cooling-water discharge. Existing studies, however, rely on idealized simulations that fail to capture real-world backgrounds, offering limited guidance for target-background discrimination. We establish AVP-IR-Wake, the first large-scale, real-world, physically diverse benchmark of 161,485 frames collected over three years. We show that thermal wakes are extended structures of discrete vortices, violating the compactness assumption of conventional targets. We reveal local indistinguishability: individual wake vortices are statistically identical to wind-induced background vortices in temporal, frequency, and sparse domains, sharing low-frequency information and long-range correlations. This challenges the assumptions of compact, transient, high-frequency targets in conventional detection. Yet we establish global morphological separability: although locally inseparable, the wake as a whole is organized by vehicle trajectory, whereas background clutter is organized by wind-driven thermal fronts. This explains why representative detectors fail and shows that reliable detection must shift from local feature extraction to global trajectory-constrained physical modeling. Because the cold-skin layer varies globally and seasonally, forecasting wake observability will require integrating physical oceanography and atmospheric science, linking underwater surveillance to the changing ocean surface.

papers.title: Bright Compton source based on the interaction of an ultraintense laser pulse with a relativistically transparent foil and a plasma mirror
papers.abstract: We propose and numerically study an x-ray source in which a single laser pulse first accelerates electrons while passing through a relativistically transparent thin overdense foil and then, after reflection from a plasma mirror, collides head-on with them. Two-dimensional kinetic simulations show that for a laser pulse with an intensity of the order of $10^{21}$~W/cm$^2$ and optimal foil parameters, electrons are accelerated to energies of the order of 100~MeV, and the source can deliver up to $10^{7}$ photons per 0.1\% bandwidth per joule of laser energy in the 10--250~keV range, two orders of magnitude more than a similar gas-jet scheme. This also exceeds the spectral yield per joule of the best gas-target betatron sources by about an order of magnitude and is comparable to the best experimental results obtained with near-critical-density targets.

papers.title: Context-dependent Runtime Construction of Safe Regions of Attraction from Design-Time Identification for Multi-Candidate Simplex Architectures
papers.abstract: Deploying safety-critical cyber-physical systems requires control strategies that reconcile high performance and adaptability with rigorous safety guarantees. Classical control strategies offer stability proofs but are conservative, while advanced optimization- and learning-based controllers achieve high performance but lack formal verification. Runtime Assurance (RTA) architectures bridge this gap by introducing their own (dis-)advantages. Safety filters use online optimization and introduce chattering, while Simplex permissiveness is bounded by the tightness of the certified Region of Attraction (RoA) of its High-Assurance (HA) controller. Targeting this conservatism, we present a two-stage RoA certification procedure leveraging contraction-based stability to establish a target set for Taylor-model-based reachability analysis. We then treat the closed-loop system under HA control as a switched system, enabling: (a) runtime construction of context-dependent safe RoA and (b) safe switching between HA candidates to optimize recovery and maximize the operating envelope of the uncertified High-Performance (HP) controller. We validate this framework on a robotic path-tracking task using a three-stage evaluation: Ordinary Differential Equation (ODE) simulation for theoretical verification, high-fidelity Gazebo simulation under unmodeled dynamics, and experiments on physical hardware. Results show that the Simplex architecture maintains safety under fault injection and successfully shields a behavioral-cloning-trained HP controller. Crucially, the decision module introduces negligible overhead (0.028 ms average, 4.13 ms worst-case), consuming under 10 % of the control period.

papers.title: Solid-Resolving Sets on Directed Graphs
papers.abstract: A set $S \subseteq V(G)$ is a solid-resolving set of an undirected graph $G$ if each vertex can be distinguished from any vertex subset by their distances from the set $S$. Solid-resolving sets are a generalization of resolving sets, which have been studied extensively in the literature. We extend this concept to oriented graphs and directed graphs. In this setting, we first define solid-resolving sets for digraphs and then consider vertices that must be included in any solid-resolving set. We also study the solid-metric dimension, which is the minimum cardinality of a solid-resolving set of a given digraph. We determine the possible values of the solid-metric dimension for several common graph classes, including tournaments, directed trees, oriented cycles, complete bipartite graphs, as well as for Cartesian products of oriented paths and cycles. We also show via some examples that there is no trivial relation between the solid-metric dimension of a digraph and the solid-metric dimension of its underlying undirected graph. Furthermore, we show that the solid-metric dimension can increase or decrease by an arbitrary $k$ when one vertex is removed. Similarly, removing a single arc can decrease the solid-metric dimension by an arbitrary $k$; however, it can increase by at most 1. The arbitrary changes in solid-metric dimension indicate that the solid-metric dimension is a global, rather than a local, property.

papers.title: SimPOTrans: Self-Adaptation for Offline-to-Simultaneous Speech Translation via Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Simultaneous speech translation (SimulST) aims to translate ongoing speech with low latency while preserving translation quality. Recent studies have adopted large language models (LLMs) for SimulST and formulated it as a multi-turn dialogue task for efficient generation, achieving state-of-the-art performance. However, existing dialogue-style SimulST approaches typically rely on specialized training schemes to acquire simultaneous translation behavior, either using synthesized read/write trajectories, which may provide suboptimal training signals, or jointly optimizing translation quality and latency, whose competing objectives may cause optimization instability. In this paper, we introduce SimPOTrans, a reinforcement learning (RL) framework that enables offline speech translation models to self-adapt to dialogue-style SimulST. Through a simple two-stage RL post-training pipeline, SimPOTrans rewards an offline model for exhibiting translation behaviors beneficial to simultaneous scenarios when given partial speech inputs, thereby enabling offline-to-simultaneous self-adaptation without synthesized read/write trajectories or explicit latency optimization. At inference time, SimPOTrans requires no external decision policy and enables flexible quality--latency control by simply adjusting the chunk size of speech input. Experiments on the ACL 60/60 and MCIF benchmarks across three language directions (En$\rightarrow$De, En$\rightarrow$Zh, and En$\rightarrow$Ja) demonstrate that SimPOTrans outperforms several strong baselines, achieving a superior quality--latency trade-off.

papers.title: Steering for Safety, Hijacking for Profit: Trojan Threats in the LLM Activation Steering Supply Chain
papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into Web search, online recommendation, and intelligent decision-making, the third-party plugin ecosystem centered on model customization continues to grow. Among these, Steering Vectors guide model behavior by intervening in internal representations. However, the open plugin ecosystem also introduces new supply-chain security risks: malicious plugins can disguise themselves as having legitimate functionality and covertly manipulate outputs without significantly affecting model performance. Although this risk poses a real threat, the security issues of Steering plugins in the LLM supply-chain ecosystem still lack systematic research. This paper audits eight mainstream open-source Steering plugin libraries and reveals three structural vulnerabilities: insufficient distribution integrity verification, excessive plugin privileges, and missing runtime monitoring, which offers an attack surface for attackers. To investigate this threat, we propose a malicious plugin, IDH. Specifically, IDH designs a norm-gated mutually exclusive routing mechanism and proposes an information-decay inflection point localization method to automatically select the injection layer, thereby simultaneously achieving benign and malicious functions. To counter such threats, we propose a runtime defense framework, by suppressing anomalous activation interventions and orthogonalizing inter-layer trajectory. We evaluate IDH across five mainstream LLMs, using safety-refusal steering as the legitimate functionality and commercial recommendation manipulation as the hijack objective. Experiments covering six brands across three commercial domains demonstrate that IDH achieves an attack success rate (ASR) of up to 97.8% while preserving high refusal rates on harmful requests.

papers.title: DriveUniTok: A Unified Multimodal Tokenizer for Driving World-Action Models
papers.abstract: World models are emerging as a fundamental component of policy learning for real-world agents, enabling agents to predict future world states and plan actions within a learned representation of the dynamic environment. Existing approaches, however, often model appearance, metric geometry represented by projected LiDAR depth, and ego motion either partially or independently, overlooking the fact that these modalities are different projections of a shared underlying world state. This separation can lead to information loss and cross-modal inconsistency, ultimately limiting downstream performance. Motivated by this unified view of the world, we propose DriveUniTok, a unified multimodal tokenizer for driving world-action models (WAMs) that encodes these modalities in a single decodable continuous latent. We freeze DriveUniTok and adapt a pretrained diffusion model, DriveUniWAM, to predict future unified latents; the tokenizer then decodes them into future appearance, projected LiDAR depth, and ego trajectories. Experiments on NAVSIM demonstrate that our unified design achieves better future prediction and planning performance at lower downstream computational cost than separate-stream alternatives. With reinforcement learning post-training, DriveUniWAM achieves a PDMS of 91.54, reaching state-of-the-art performance among the evaluated WAM-based planners.

papers.title: CA-HNM: Constraint-Aware Hard Negative Mining for Dense Retrieval with Structured Domain Models
papers.abstract: Dense retrievers are commonly trained with hard negatives selected from lexical or dense retrieval results. Retrieval proximity, however, does not indicate whether a candidate conflicts with explicit domain structure. We introduce CA-HNM, a constraint-aware hard-negative mining framework that combines retrieval-based candidate generation with deterministic incompatibility rules derived from a structured domain model. The framework removes known positives, constructs a local typed context around the query target, records relational, scope, target, and level mismatches, and uses the resulting candidates to fine-tune a standard dual encoder. Structured information is required only during offline negative construction. We evaluate CA-HNM on MOOCCubeX and Course-Skill Atlas with two encoders, two training losses, and ten seeds. Relative to a retrieval-rank-matched control, CA-HNM-Pure has higher mean NDCG@10 in six of eight dataset--encoder--loss configurations. Four hierarchical 95% bootstrap intervals are entirely above zero, mostly under triplet loss. In a separate experiment, CA-HNM-Mixed shows slightly higher mean NDCG@10 than a matched-mixed control on both collections. Structural variants show that changes in available structure can also change candidate eligibility and negative-pool composition. The results indicate that the contribution of constraint-aware selection depends on the training objective and the composition of the negative pool.

papers.title: Calibration requirements for Epoch of Reionization 21-cm signal observations - V. Bias and variance in the cylindrical power spectrum from uGMRT Band 3 observations of the ELAIS-N1 field
papers.abstract: Detection of the redshifted 21-cm signal from neutral hydrogen requires precise control of systematic effects arising from instrumental calibration. In this work, we investigate the impact of both time- and frequency-dependent residual gain and bandpass errors on the estimation of the multifrequency angular power spectrum (MAPS) using radio interferometric observations. We discuss our previously developed analytical framework for estimating bias and excess variance in 21-cm signal MAPS in the presence of these residual errors and apply it to uGMRT Band-3 observations. The statistical properties of the residual gains are derived from the data themselves, including their temporal and spectral correlations. We introduce a robust technique for additionally flagging poor-quality data. Our results show that the excess variance induced by residual gain and bandpass errors dominates over the bias across the range of angular multipoles considered. The amplitude of this variance is comparable to the expected power spectrum upper limit at redshift $z \sim 2.2$, indicating that residual calibration errors can significantly affect the detectability of the 21-cm signal. We further transform the estimated MAPS into ($k_{\perp}, k_{ll}$) space and find the expected foreground wedge structure. Importantly, we observe a significant power leakage into the nominal EoR window, which we attribute to residual calibration systematics. This highlights that even after standard foreground mitigation, time- and frequency-correlated gain errors can introduce mode-mixing and contaminate the EoR window. Our results emphasise the necessity of improved calibration accuracy and robust characterisation of residual gain statistics for current and upcoming interferometric experiments such as the uGMRT and SKA, to enable reliable detection of the cosmological 21-cm signal.

papers.title: Fluid Antennas Enabled UAV Communication Systems: Fundamentals, Challenges, and Future Directions
papers.abstract: Low-altitude wireless networks (LAWNs) require uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) communication systems to adapt to large-scale propagation changes and fast local channel fluctuations. Fluid antennas (FAs) provide an additional degree of freedom (DoF) by reconfiguring antenna positions within a compact aperture. This article investigates FA-enabled UAV communication systems from the perspectives of fundamentals, design challenges, and future research directions. We first introduce a dual-mobility perspective, in which UAV trajectory planning provides macro-mobility for large-scale air-to-ground geometry adaptation, and FA position reconfiguration provides micro-mobility for fine-grained local channel adaptation. We then identify key design challenges arising from the high computational complexity and information uncertainty in the joint optimization of UAV trajectory, FA positions, and beamforming under mobility, energy, hardware, and security constraints. To address these challenges, we present a hybrid offline-online optimization framework, where prior information such as environment maps, user mobility patterns, and statistical channel state information (CSI) supports long-term planning, while real-time information such as instantaneous CSI and UAV state enables fast online correction. A case study on FA-enabled UAV-assisted vehicular communications demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed framework. Finally, we discuss future directions of FA-enabled UAV communication in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), secure communication, mobile edge computing (MEC), and aerial relaying.

papers.title: Explosive instability, quiet plasma: phase-space cascades, coherent vortices, and transport suppression in a dipole pair plasma
papers.abstract: Turbulence in a magnetised dipole pair plasma can transfer electrostatic energy into coherent flows while carrying entropy to small scales. This occurs via a dual cascade in a four-dimensional phase space, whereby advection by the fluctuating electric field nonlinearly phase-mixes the transit-averaged particle motion. Below a critical pressure gradient, zonal bands suppress the kinetic mode, leaving a transport floor. When the fluid mode is unstable, an explosive burst collapses into a zonal condensate on which two vortices "breathe" by reversible energy exchange, without causing net transport.

papers.title: Maximization of accelerated charge in multibunch-driven plasma wakefield accelerators
papers.abstract: Driving the plasma wakefield with a train of multiple particle bunches has the potential to significantly increase the accelerated charge, provided that the witness bunches also form a train. In this scenario, the driver bunches can replenish the wave energy after the passage of the witness bunches, yielding comparable charges in both trains. However, implementing this method at high wakefield amplitudes is complicated by the reshaping of the driver bunches as they reach radial equilibrium with the wave. The witness bunches cannot preserve their quality during this process; nevertheless, they must load the wave to prevent it from reaching the amplitude at which the wakefield period elongates and the wave destroys the driver. The proposed solution is to form an equilibrium train of initially inefficient driver bunches, which becomes efficient upon the injection of the witness bunches. This concept is demonstrated using the example of a self-modulating driver beam. Several factors favoring a high witness charge are identified: injecting additional ``phaser'' bunches at the zero-accelerating-field points, suppressing the formation of an electron halo around the plasma, and operating at the highest possible wakefield amplitudes.

papers.title: On characters of irreducible modules for Lie superalgebra q(n)
papers.abstract: Su and Zhang proved a formula for the decomposition of characters of irreducible finite dimensional modules over Lie superalgebra $\frak q(n)$ as the sum of Euler characters. They gave a combinatorial formula for the coefficients in that decomposition by generalasing of weights and caps diagrams introduced by J. Brundan and C. Ctroppel. In the present paper we give a correct version of their combinatorial formula. Our main technical tool is a family of creation operators.

papers.title: VISTA: Active Exploration for Self-Improvement in Embodied Agents
papers.abstract: Agentic embodied intelligence plays a foundational role in open-ended, dynamic physical environments. Rather than treating policy learning as an end-to-end mapping from instructions to actions, recent studies reveal that embodied systems depend not only on pre-trained foundation models, but also on harness. Prior approaches largely treat rollouts as static logs for post-hoc reflection, producing harness updates without autonomously testing and refining them through subsequent embodied interaction. To address this challenge, we propose VISTA, a meta-agent framework that transforms post-hoc rollout reflection into active self-exploration for embodied harness improvement. Specifically, VISTA maintains a harness graph that records the lineage of proposed harnesses, which enables the meta-agent to retrieve prior hypotheses, build on effective mechanisms, and avoid repeatedly exploring failed directions. Each iteration begins from a retained harness version and its execution evidence. Rather than directly committing an update from these historical trajectories, the meta-agent actively explores in the environment. It autonomously generates new rollouts, probes execution failures and recovery behaviors, and iteratively modifies the harness based on the resulting evidence. The refined harness is then evaluated afresh and added to the harness graph. We evaluate VISTA on the LIBERO-Pro, RoboCasa, and RoboTwin benchmarks. Experimental results demonstrate that VISTA progressively improves task success and is more rollout-efficient than static reflection, achieving higher success rates with fewer simulator rollouts.

papers.title: LOCUS: Locate Once, Check Until Settled. Draft-and-Verify Visual Grounding with a Box Head and Coordinate-Token Verification
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) ground a referring expression in one of two ways. They decode the box as coordinate tokens, which is precise but takes one sequential step per token, or they regress it from a hidden state with a small head, which takes one step but loses accuracy at high IoU. The two fail differently: a head usually finds the right object but places its edges loosely, while coordinate tokens place edges precisely. We therefore use the regression head as a speculative drafter for the model's own coordinate tokens. Locus writes the head's box as coordinate tokens and checks them with the same backbone by Jacobi iteration over a shared image prefix. The fixed point is the model's greedy coordinate-token answer, reached in about 5.60 sequential passes on average instead of 18.46 decoding steps; head and verifier are one set of weights, trained jointly. On the 8 RefCOCO, RefCOCO+ and RefCOCOg splits, verification raises Locus-2B's Acc@0.9 from 54.87 for its own head to 59.13, and the one-pass head is ahead at Acc@0.5 of every published model with at most 3B parameters except Florence-2-L. Against Jag, the strongest open regression-head model, at its own size and training budget, Locus ties at Acc@0.5 and, with typical acceptance, gains +4.52 points at Acc@0.9, with paired significance tests. Exact answers come 1.5x faster than vLLM greedy-decoding the same coordinate tokens with the same weights; a pure regression head remains faster still.

papers.title: From Questions to Queries to Insights: A Schema-Grounded Agentic Workflow for Natural-Language Crash Data Analysis
papers.abstract: Transportation agencies maintain extensive crash databases to identify safety priorities, evaluate countermeasures, and guide resource allocation. Making these data accessible to practitioners requires flexible ways to translate analytical questions into reliable results. Existing dashboards support predefined analyses, while additional requests often depend on specialists who understand database queries, coded fields, and agency conventions. This study presents CrashDB-QA, a fully local, schema-grounded agentic workflow that enables natural-language analysis of crash databases. Specialized components interpret questions, generate and validate read-only SQL, execute queries, and explain the results. A shared knowledge base grounds query construction in the agency's data dictionary and safety-analysis conventions, while recorded intermediate outputs support inspection and auditing. An optional extension, CrashDB-QA+, checks the alignment among the question, query, and execution result and supplies evidence for iterative repair. We evaluate the workflow on a frozen snapshot of 4.4 million Wisconsin crash records using a new benchmark of 300 questions across ten analytical categories and nine local open-weight models. Domain grounding substantially improves query accuracy, and a code-specialized 7B model provides the best accuracy-latency balance among the tested models. Compositional analyses remain more difficult than routine retrieval, particularly comparisons between groups or periods. Verification improves performance when the Judge uses authoritative field definitions and the Refiner receives execution evidence, whereas additional checking alone offers no consistent benefit. These findings demonstrate the potential of locally deployed, domain-grounded workflows to broaden access to crash analysis and identify the reasoning and verification capabilities needed for reliable use.

papers.title: Carleson duality and endpoint structure of Euclidean flag Triebel--Lizorkin spaces
papers.abstract: The main purpose of this paper is to develop the duality theory of the homogeneous Triebel--Lizorkin spaces associated with the Euclidean flag, using the discrete Littlewood--Paley--Stein analysis. After establishing bounded analysis and synthesis maps, we describe the continuous duals by Carleson conditions. In the Hardy spatial range, the representing distributions satisfy an open-set Carleson condition when the sequence exponent is greater than one and a coefficient supremum condition when the sequence exponent is at most one; in the Banach spatial range the dual is a conjugate-exponent or a supremum space. At the supremum sequence endpoint, the closure of the flag test functions is characterized by a pointwise scale tail measured in $L^p$, and a coefficient pairing decomposes every functional on the full space into a regular part and a part that annihilates the closure. By means of a fixed-envelope modulation construction we show that this closure is proper for every finite spatial exponent and that the annihilator is nonzero when the spatial exponent is at least one. The same analysis and synthesis framework also yields complex interpolation, real interpolation in the spatial exponent, the lifting property and the standard mixed-norm embeddings.

papers.title: Hallucination-Aware Multi-Agent RAG via Internal Attention Rewards
papers.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) grounds language models in retrieved evidence, but its outputs often contain claims unsupported by that evidence. Recent multi-agent RAG systems decompose the pipeline into cooperative decisions, yet they typically optimize all agents under a shared task reward such as EM or F1, which measures answer overlap rather than faithfulness to evidence. We propose a hallucination-aware multi-agent RAG framework that combines the task reward with an internal hallucination-risk signal computed from the generator's attention-head norms. Three role-specific LoRA adapters, a query planner, an evidence selector, and an answer generator, share a frozen backbone. A lightweight critic is trained once on TruthfulQA truthful/false pairs and then kept frozen, providing a complementary risk score that is added to the shared reward during cooperative PPO training. Across three backbones (Qwen3-8B, Llama3-8B, Llama2-13B) and three benchmarks (RAGTruth, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA), our method improves task performance and reduces hallucination rates over the strongest multi-agent baseline. Ablations and critic diagnostics show that the TruthfulQA-calibrated signal provides useful reward shaping that transfers across RAG tasks.

papers.title: Radial dependence of galaxy and halo properties in cosmic voids: SDSS DR7 and the ELUCID constrained simulation
papers.abstract: Cosmic voids provide a setting for examining the interplay between mass and environment in shaping galaxy and halo properties. Using the SDSS DR7 volume-limited galaxy sample and the ELUCID constrained simulation of the local large-scale structure, we investigate the radial profiles of galaxy and subhalo properties across different mass ranges, identifying voids independently in the observed galaxy and simulated subhalo distributions. Both stellar mass and subhalo mass increase from void interiors toward the void boundary, indicating that lower-mass galaxies and subhaloes preferentially reside in void interiors. The satellite fraction of subhaloes also increases systematically toward the void boundary. Galaxy colour and specific star formation rate exhibit radial variations that are weaker than their dependence on stellar mass, while the spiral fraction shows little radial dependence at fixed stellar mass. For dark-matter haloes, the apparent radial increase in size within a broad high-mass bin largely disappears when narrower mass ranges are considered. Halo concentration and spin show radial variations at fixed mass, with higher concentrations and lower spins toward void interiors, although the concentration trend is less pronounced in the extended low-mass sample. The formation redshift of low-mass subhaloes also increases toward the void boundary, whereas this dependence weakens and eventually disappears at higher masses. Overall, the radial trends in galaxy properties are generally weaker than their mass dependence, while several subhalo properties retain measurable radial variations at fixed mass.

papers.title: 3D-Force Estimation for Dual-arm Manipulation of Deformable Linear Objects via Factor Graphs
papers.abstract: Estimating forces acting on Deformable Linear Objects (DLOs) is challenging due to their underactuated nature. However, reliable contact estimation is crucial to precisely control them and enable safe manipulation tasks. Differently from the various approaches presented in the literature, this work adopts a probabilistic formulation where the DLO state and sensor data are related through conditional distributions. In particular, factor graphs are used to determine the magnitude, direction, and location of a 3D force acting on a DLO, while simultaneously reconstructing its shape. Since DLOs are not actuated and are typically thin, like cables and wires, strain gauges and actuation readings are usually impractical. Therefore, to overcome this issue, this work is tested using one type of sensing information only, thus developing a generic technique suited for a wider variety of tasks. Realistic tests are performed by introducing noise into the measurements while the DLO follows a prescribed path in the presence of external forces that are accurately estimated.

papers.title: Mustafin degenerations of six points in the projective plane and self-duality
papers.abstract: Mustafin varieties provide a framework for degenerating the projective plane together with marked points, governed by the combinatorics of Bruhat-Tits buildings. Such limit objects are parametrized by the boundary points of a projective compactification of the moduli space of $n$ points in $\mathbb{P}^2$ constructed by Schaffler-Tevelev. In this paper, we study the locus of this compactification generically parametrizing self-dual configurations, or equivalently, six points lying on a conic. We prove that this locus is a tropical compactification of the moduli space of self-dual configurations, with associated fan a refinement of the self-dual tropical Grassmannian introduced by Geiger-Hashimoto-Sturmfels-Vlad. We show that this compactification is a blow up of $\overline{\mathrm{M}}_{0,6}$ and we classify the objects it parametrizes: degenerations of $\mathbb{P}^2$ equipped with a stable $6$-pointed rational curve that records the limiting conic.

papers.title: Stochastic analysis of an emergency department with two levels sharing the servers
papers.abstract: In this paper, a stochastic model of an overcrwoded emergency department (ED) with two levels is analysed. A patient care pathway consists of a first consultation, followed by diagnostic tests and then a discharge consultation. The first level includes the patients before or during the first consultation. The second level applies to patients currently undergoing diagnostic tests, and patients waiting for or attending a second consultation. Each level has limited capacity; thus, when the second level is full, patients must remain at the first level. One of the key features of this model is the fact that first and second consultations are handled by the same pool of emergency physicians, which means that their decision to prioritize level 1 or level 2 affects the behavior of the system. Under a scaling assumption, the evolution of the number of patients in each step of the pathway is investigated. It is shown that, depending on the parameters, there is a phase transition between two different regimes: a regime limited by the number of emergency physicians and a regime limited by the second level capacity. Stochastic calculus gives the convergence of the state Markov process to a deterministic solution of a differential inclusion, which is proved to be unique and is explicitly characterized. The equilibrium points of the solution are determined depending on the service policies. It allows to compute the exit rate of the ED and the average length of stay, and find the policies that optimize them.

papers.title: PushAround: Collaborative Path Clearing via Physics-Informed Hybrid Search
papers.abstract: Large vehicles in cluttered environments are often blocked by movable obstacles, motivating mobile robot teams to clear traversable corridors. Navigation Among Movable Obstacles (NAMO) approaches often abstract obstacle displacements while neglecting robot dimensions, obstacle mass, contact geometry and forces, yielding physically infeasible plans. PushAround is a physics-informed hybrid search that couples geometric connectivity reasoning with short-horizon simulation to construct executable clearing plans. Repeated W-clearance connectivity graph (WCCG) queries expose frontier gaps requiring widening and rank them by estimated downstream costs. The search generates direct or recursive pushing candidates, selecting obstacles, directions, contacts and forces, and admits physics-evaluated candidates. Numerical experiments validate WCCG against standard connectivity checks and demonstrate scaling to denser clutter and teams of up to four robots, with robustness to simulated execution-side physical-parameter mismatch.

papers.title: A Bang-Jensen-Gutin-Li type condition for pancyclicity in digraphs
papers.abstract: Bang-Jensen-Gutin-Li type conditions are degree conditions for the existence of hamiltonian cycles in digraphs, which impose degree restrictions on nonadjacent vertices which have a common in-neighbor or a common out-neighbor. They can be viewed as directed analogues of both Fan-type conditions and heavy subgraph conditions in undirected graphs, and they also generalized the classes of locally semicomplete digrahs, loclaly in-semicomplete digraphs, and locally out-semicomplete digraphs. In this paper, we prove what is, to our knowledge, the first Bang-Jensen-Gutin-Li type condition for pancyclicity in digraphs. More precisely, let $D$ be a strong digraph with order $n\ge 3$. We show that, if for every $u\in V(D)$ belonging to a dominated nonadjacent pair or a dominating nonadjacent pair, we have $d(u)\ge n$, then $D$ is pancyclic, unless $D$ belongs to one of two well-characterized classes of exceptional digraphs.

papers.title: Type-II Singularities of Immersed Locally Convex Curves Evolving under Generalized Anisotropic Gage Area-Preserving Flows with Slow Curvature Speeds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the singularity behavior of immersed locally convex closed plane curves evolving under generalized anisotropic Gage area-preserving flows with slow curvature speeds of the form $\kappa_\sigma^\alpha$, where $0<\alpha\le 1$. Here $\kappa_\sigma$ denotes the anisotropic curvature associated with a prescribed anisotropy function $\sigma$. We prove that every finite-time blow-up is of Type-II provided that the Euclidean length of the evolving curve remains uniformly bounded away from zero. This result holds without any symmetry assumptions on either the initial curve or the anisotropy. When the initial signed area is nonzero, this length lower bound is automatically satisfied, and thus any finite-time singularity is necessarily of Type-II. By means of Hamilton's rescaling method combined with a differential Harnack estimate, we show that along a suitable blow-up subsequence, the rescaled curves at the selected times converge locally to the profile of a translating solution of the corresponding anisotropic curvature flow $V=\kappa_\sigma^\alpha$. We also establish sufficient conditions for finite-time singularity formation in terms of the initial signed area and anisotropic length. Moreover, we construct locally convex initial curves arbitrarily close to the Wulff curve for which a finite-time Type-II singularity occurs.

papers.title: Kronecker-Structured Video Completion with Cross-Fitted Self-Supervised Residual Learning
papers.abstract: Tube-wise video completion reconstructs temporal trajectories at spatial locations unobserved in every frame. We propose a two-stage framework combining regularized masked Kronecker product decomposition (KPD) with cross-fitted self-supervised residual learning. First, we estimate a compact structural backbone directly from observed entries using cyclic component-wise least-squares updates, spatial and temporal factor regularization, and regularizer-optimal scale balancing. The exact updates yield a nonincreasing objective. Second, we address the mismatch between in-sample fitting errors and the prediction errors encountered at missing tubes. We partition observed tubes into folds and construct residual targets using backbone models fitted without the corresponding target tubes. A lightweight 3-D convolutional neural network then predicts corrections from the backbone, visible residual context, observation mask, and local detail features. Exact data consistency preserves observed measurements. Experiments include ablations, sensitivity analysis, grayscale and RGB video completion, and structured missing patterns. Our method achieves the highest mean PSNR and SSIM at the higher tested sampling rates on the grayscale benchmark. On eight selected DAVIS RGB sequences, it achieves the highest mean missing-region PSNR and full-frame SSIM and the lowest mean missing-tube temporal-gradient MAE at every evaluated sampling rate.

papers.title: MemVLN: Streaming Episodic Memory for Vision-Language Navigation
papers.abstract: Vision-language navigation (VLN) requires an embodied agent to follow language instructions through 3D environments. Maintaining persistent episodic memory remains a challenge for VLM-based streaming agents in long-horizon navigation. We present MEMVLN, a streaming episodic memory framework that maintains a bounded bank of compressed perceptual features annotated with timesteps and action-derived relative poses, and produces compact memory tokens via cross-attention. We pair the proposed memory with a frozen pretrained geometry encoder. To learn the memory module, we design a masking-based trajectory summarization task with multi-granularity sub-trajectory decomposition, encouraging route reconstruction exclusively from episodic memory. Under navigation training restricted to the official R2R/RxR trajectories, MEMVLN achieves state-of-the-art performance on most reported metrics on standard VLN-CE benchmarks. Long-horizon analyses further characterize when episodic memory is useful. For physical evaluation, we collect 30 instruction-conditioned episodes in one physical scene, use 24 as demonstrations for post-training, and hold out six for testing. On the held-out episodes, MEMVLN improves success over the VLM baseline from 17% to 40%, and post-training further raises it to 47%.

papers.title: Two families of Young tableaux with periodic walls: Counting formulas and differential transcendence
papers.abstract: Banderier, Marchal, and Wallner studied the enumeration problem for Young tableaux with walls. These are similar to standard Young tableaux, except that local decreases are allowed at some walls. In 2021, Banderier and Wallner counted Young tableaux with periodic walls, in which the elementary blocks are Young diagrams of shape $(2,2)$. They obtained exact counting formulas for $30$ of the $32$ classes up to symmetry. In this paper, we first derive recurrences for counting the remaining two classes of Young tableaux with periodic walls. We then prove that their counting exponential generating functions are differentially transcendental. Consequently, they are neither D-algebraic nor D-finite. This disproves a conjecture of Banderier and Wallner.

papers.title: Quantitative Persistence and Regularity of Invariant Graphs for Dissipative Twist Maps
