First, there exists a compactly supported continuous function which is the divergence of a bounded Lipschitz vector field but not of any continuously differentiable vector field. Second, every continuous function whose distributional partial derivatives are locally $m$-integrable (the critical exponent for Sobolev embedding) is the divergence of a continuously differentiable vector field.

papers.title: Pulsed Laser Deposition of Ferroelectric SrTiO3 Shells Enables Polarization-Controlled Charge Separation in TiO2 Photoanode
papers.abstract: Ferroelectric polarization offers a powerful route to govern the interfacial charge separation in photoelectrodes; however, chemically converted ferroelectric shells lack sub-nanometer thickness control, coherent strain retention, and chemically clean interfaces. Here, we use pulsed laser deposition to fabricate stoichiometric SrTiO3 shells on hydrothermally grown TiO2 nanorod arrays, achieving atomically defined core-shell architectures while preserving the one-dimensional transport geometry. The photocurrent density followed a volcano-shaped dependence on shell thickness and reached 1.9 mA cm-2 at 1.23 V versus RHE under AM 1.5G illumination for the optimized 15-mins sample, exceeding the established hydrothermal benchmark. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy revealed a tetragonally distorted, oxygen-stoichiometric shell, identifying coherent interfacial strain rather than defect dipoles as the origin of the ferroelectric order. Kelvin probe force microscopy directly imaged a polarization-induced built-in electric field whose magnitude scaled with charge-transfer efficiency and photocurrent density. Together, these complementary structural, chemical, electrostatic, and device-level measurements established a quantitative strain-polarization-built-in field-charge separation relationship. This work transforms ferroelectric photoanode engineering from empirical optimization into an atomically controllable and predictive materials strategy for high-efficiency solar water-splitting devices. This approach is readily extendable to visible-light absorbers and complex ferroelectric heterostructures.

papers.title: Kinetic modifications to parallel transport in a low-recycling scrape-off layer: A one dimensional gyrokinetic study
papers.abstract: A liquid lithium boundary offers a route to improved energy confinement via reduced recycling, but the resulting low-density, high-temperature edge can become sufficiently collisionless such that standard fluid models are no longer applicable. Experimental measurements of scrape-off-layer (SOL) parameters, including density decay length ($\lambda_n$) estimates presented here can be used for simple analytic estimates of kinetic effects, but need more complete kinetic treatment. We present gyrokinetic simulations, with one configuration-space dimension and two velocity-space dimensions, of low and higher-recycling LTX-$\beta$ SOL conditions using Gkeyll, an open-source continuum gyrokinetic code. The simulations follow a single open field line, self-consistently evolving kinetic ion and electron distribution functions, electrostatic potential, collisions, sources, and sheath losses constrained by experimental midplane measurements. The hotter low-recycling case develops a larger parallel potential variation, and a density response not captured by an adiabatic Boltzmann-electron closure of the field equations, demonstrating the importance of kinetic electrons and the ambipolar potential in reducing electron end losses. Collisionality scans show that, as ion neoclassical collisionality falls below unity, the ion distribution develops pronounced non-Maxwellian features. The corresponding SOL particle and energy confinement times increase at low collisionality, particularly for low recycling, because ions become mirror-trapped and electron losses are throttled by the ambipolar potential. These results indicate that low-recycling lithium boundaries in LTX-$\beta$ access a regime where mirror trapping and electrostatic confinement fundamentally alter parallel residence times relative to conventional fluid expectations, an effect expected to be more pronounced in larger devices.

papers.title: RoKON: Efficient and Adaptive Data-Enabled Predictive Control for Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Data-enabled predictive control has recently emerged as a promising control paradigm, enabling a transparent optimal-control formulation without the need to learn an explicit dynamics model. This paper presents a number of extensions paving the path towards its use in real-time robotics tasks. Following recent work, we utilize a nonlinear predictor based on Gaussian kernels to represent the relationship between input and output data. We propose a damped Gauss-Newton method that enables real-time control by efficiently exploiting the least-squares structure of the control problem. In addition, we introduce a hybrid buffer management strategy that incorporates informative online data while retaining relevant offline data, allowing the predictor to account for changes in the dynamics. We demonstrate the tracking performance and computational suitability of the proposed method in MuJoCo using a Franka Research 3 arm pushing a block across surface, without prior knowledge of its changing friction values.

papers.title: The Formal Critical Coupling of the Four-Dimensional Anderson Model
papers.abstract:
In this work we present a formal renormalization-group (RG) calculation for the weakly coupled four-dimensional elliptic Anderson model. Under a scale-independent bare-coupling convention, and with the normalization $\lambda_{\varepsilon}$, the bubble-chain resummation yields the geometric series $\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{formal}}(\lambda)$, with a formal pole at $\lambda_c$. We stress that this pole is a feature of the formal bare bubble series. The argument combines Bogoliubov-Parasiuk-Hepp-Zimmermann (BPHZ) renormalization, a Hepp-sector motivated restriction to the bubble-chain subclass for explicit resummation, and an explicit summation of the resulting geometric series.
  Numerically, we illustrate the analytic building blocks of the formal expansion: the massive Green function, the bubble integral, the geometric resummation, the extraction of the formal pole from synthetic noisy data, a kurtosis diagnostic, and a phase diagram of the formal variance. These computations visualize the deterministic kernels and the formal resummation used above. Using spectral methods and nonlinear least-squares fitting, we verify the short-distance asymptotic behaviour of the massive Green function for $G=(1-\Delta)^{-1}\delta_0$, reproduce the logarithmic divergence of the bubble integral in four dimensions, compute the formal effective variance $\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{formal}}(\lambda)$ arising from the bubble-chain resummation, locate the formal pole at $\lambda_c$, and draw a schematic phase diagram of the formal variance in the $(\lambda,\log\varepsilon)$ plane. The kurtosis diagnostic uses a synthetic proxy for the non-Gaussian regime; the sharp change is imposed by construction. Nonlinear fitting of synthetic data recovers the formal pole within the statistical uncertainty of the synthetic noise. Our results illustrate the analytic formulas and the fitting procedure.

papers.title: Periodic data conjugacy for diffeomorphism cocycles
papers.abstract: We consider H\"older continuous cocycles over a hyperbolic dynamical system with values in the group of diffeomorphisms of a compact manifold. We focus on establishing conjugacy between two cocycles from conjugacy of their periodic data. We obtain such a result under bunching, or domination, assumption on the cocycles and a mild regularity assumption in $C^0$ topology on the maps conjugating the periodic data. We also obtain conjugacy to a constant cocycle assuming boundedness in $C^1$ or pre-compactness in $C^0$ for the constant cocycle and the conjugating maps.

papers.title: A Contextual Measure of Ambiguity in Prescriptive Text
papers.abstract: Ambiguity in prescriptive text such as laws, contracts, rules, policies, or recommendations can be both desirable (e.g., if it enables a law to adapt to changing context, such as new technologies) and undesirable (e.g., if it leads to arbitrary discretion or conflict over the law's interpretation). To help navigate these trade-offs, it would be valuable to have methods for quantifying ambiguity that are predictive of such outcomes, but existing measures capture how text is perceived in isolation rather than how it is interpreted in context. In this paper, we propose quantifying ambiguity as the degree of disagreement among a set of stakeholders ("raters") on how alternative prescriptive texts ("policies") apply in each of a set of relevant scenarios ("cases"). Using two policy domains, we present preliminary analysis suggesting that, even when using simulated raters, this approach (i) correlates with real human disagreement, and (ii) is robust to spurious text features. We then apply the measure to existing deliberation datasets to describe the association between policy ambiguity and support for those policies.

papers.title: DEX-PHD: A Dexterous Portable Handheld Device for Multimodal Data Collection
papers.abstract: Existing manipulation data collection methods typically offer either accurate robot-state acquisition through kinematic-chain-based teleoperation or convenient, portable operation through vision-based approaches. We present DEX-PHD, a portable handheld device that combines these advantages for dexterous manipulation by integrating a dexterous robot hand, continuous per-finger control, and multimodal logging. The system records proprioceptive information, fingertip contact data, and wrist-camera video, while the operator directly controls the robot hand through joint-level mapping. Its untethered design enables data collection across diverse environments. We demonstrate DEX-PHD on contact-rich tasks requiring coordinated multi-finger manipulation and deploy the collected demonstrations through open-loop replay on a physical humanoid robot. The results show that open-loop replay preserves the main temporal patterns of finger motion and task-relevant contact. Therefore, DEX-PHD provides a practical platform for portable, multimodal dexterous manipulation data collection.

papers.title: Poisson closures and Poisson $A$-algebras
papers.abstract: We study the interaction between the Lie and Poisson subalgebras of a Poisson algebra. Given a Lie subalgebra $U$ of the underlying Lie algebra $\mathcal P_L$, we consider the Poisson subalgebra generated by $U$, called its {Poisson closure}, and investigate when Lie-theoretic properties such as nilpotency and solvability are preserved under this construction. We also study the stability under Poisson closure of several distinguished Lie subalgebras, including maximal nilpotent and solvable subalgebras, Engel and Cartan subalgebras and the derived algebra. As an application, we investigate Poisson $A$-algebras, defined by the condition that every nilpotent subalgebra is a zero algebra. In the finite-dimensional case, we obtain structural results relating Poisson $A$-algebras to Lie $A$-algebras and to the associative structure of the algebra.

papers.title: The Schur positivity of Lucas binomial differences
papers.abstract: For positive integers $a\le b\le c\le d$ with $ad=bc$, we prove that the Lucas binomial coefficients satisfy $(-1)^{a+1}(L_{b,c}[X]-L_{a,d}[X])\in\mathbb{N}[e_1[X],e_2[X],h_2[X]]$, resolving Bergeron's conjecture on Schur positivity in two variables. We also prove the same positivity for $L_{u,v}[X]-e_1[X]^{uv-rs}L_{r,s}[X]$ when $rs<uv$. Using Lucas atoms, we establish $e$-positivity for degree-adjusted Lucas multinomial differences under dominance order.

papers.title: Finite determinacy and rigidity of quiver potentials
papers.abstract: We prove that a quiver potential over a field of characteristic zero is finitely determined if and only if the trace space of its Jacobian algebra is finite dimensional. In particular, Jacobi-finite potentials are finitely determined. We further prove that rigid potentials are finitely determined and, over an algebraically closed field, unique up to right equivalence on a fixed quiver. For finitely determined weighted-homogeneous potentials, we give an explicit bound on the jet order sufficient for finite determinacy in terms of the arrow weights, the weight of the potential, and the highest nonzero weight of the trace space of its Jacobian algebra. We also establish new invariance results for weighted-homogeneous potentials under right equivalence.

papers.title: XL MIMO Extreme Learning Machines: Wave-Domain Inference with Stacked Metasurfaces
papers.abstract: The recently envisioned goal-oriented communications paradigm requires machine learning inference to be performed directly on wirelessly transferred data, by splitting neural network computations between the transmitter, the Receiver (RX), and the wireless channel. Such approaches aim to offload large portions of the computation onto the channel itself, which is often controlled by reconfigurable MetaSurfaces (MSs). Typical MS-parametrized systems, however, enable only limited computation offloading in the wave domain, usually corresponding to a single neural network layer, due to adverse channel fading effects and the almost linear operation of the channel and conventional MS models. In this paper, we demonstrate that an eXtremely Large (XL) Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) system equipped with Stacked Intelligent MSs (SIM) at the RX side, together with a single antenna and its accompanying radio-frequency chain, may act as a two-layer neural network operating exclusively over the air. The first (uncontrollable) network layer corresponds to the transformations offered by wireless fading, while the second (controllable) layer is implemented via SIM operations. In particular, only the first, front-end MS layer needs to exhibit nonlinear response to serve as an activation function. Leveraging the Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) framework, the proposed XL MIMO system architecture is shown to be a universal approximator, and the optimal linear-SIM-based combining is derived in closed form, allowing for fast training even and partial signal observability. Numerical evaluations across diverse datasets showcase that the proposed XL-MIMO-ELM framework achieves classification accuracy comparable to idealized digital models, thereby, proving the viability of low complexity, wave-domain neural computations.

papers.title: An Interactive Evolutionary Multiobjective Optimization Algorithm Based on Interpretable Active Preference Learning
papers.abstract: Many decision-making tasks are inherently multi-objective. Interactive evolutionary multi-objective optimization algorithms (iEMOAs) are particularly well-suited to help the decision-maker find their most preferred solution. However, many of these algorithms employ black-box preference models. For high-stakes decision-making tasks, like healthcare and defense, a high level of transparency is needed, for instance to support accountability. We propose an interpretable iEMOA which uses active learning to efficiently learn a tree-based preference model directly from pairwise comparisons. The survival operator of NSGA-II and NSGA-III is extended with the learned preference model to guide the algorithm towards the region of interest. An extensive experimental study compares the proposed method to a state-of-the-art black-box model and a state-of-the-art interpretable model. Results indicate that our proposed model outperforms the alternatives in terms of finding the most preferred solution at the cost of a slightly worse average final population. Finally, a case study on a real-life engineering problem illustrates how inspecting the learned model reveals which objectives drive the decision-maker's preferences.

papers.title: Extremal Trudinger-Moser inequality associated with many point vortices with multi-intensities
papers.abstract: We study the boundedness of extremal 2D Trudinger-Moser inequality associated with many point vortices with multi-intensities. Sufficient conditions for continuously-distributed measures are given in one-sided and two-sided cases.

papers.title: Hierarchical Bayesian Joint Modeling of Athlete Performance Trajectories and Latent Peak Ages
papers.abstract: Determining when athletes reach peak performance is a central question in sports science, with implications for talent identification, training design, and cross-discipline comparisons. Statistical inference is challenging because peak age is not directly observed: competition records are noisy and selective measurements of underlying performance capacity and are often limited to incomplete observation windows. We develop a hierarchical Bayesian joint modeling framework that links a longitudinal model for athlete-specific performance trajectories to a regression submodel for latent peak age. The longitudinal component models observed competition performances as noisy measurements of athlete-specific performance trajectories over age. The peak-age component then treats the maximizer of each trajectory as a latent response in a parametric accelerated failure time (AFT) model, allowing athlete-level covariates to explain earlier or later peak age. The hierarchical structure borrows information across athletes, while joint posterior inference propagates uncertainty from trajectory reconstruction to both individual peak-age estimates and population-level covariate effects. Simulation studies show that, as observation windows become less informative, the joint model preserves substantially smaller regression bias and reflects the information loss through wider uncertainty, whereas pseudo-peak and two-stage alternatives exhibit larger bias. An application to World Athletics ranking data illustrates how the joint model estimates discipline-specific peak-age patterns and covariate effects under incomplete and irregular observation windows. Beyond sports, the proposed framework applies broadly to problems that couple longitudinal trajectories with function-derived latent features.

papers.title: Acceleration of the BSS Algorithm
papers.abstract: Bartel, Sch\"{a}fer and Ullrich investigated the BSS subsampling algorithm, which is based on the work by Batson, Spielman and Srivastava. While this algorithm works well, the bottleneck is its complexity of $\mathcal{O}(\sigma^2nm^3)$ for a frame of $n$ vectors of dimension $m$ and oversampling $\sigma^2$. We continue their work by showing that the algorithm can be implemented in $\mathcal{O}(\sigma^2nm^{2.5})$. Moreover, for some special cases, an even faster implementation is possible. In particular, BSS subsampling of Fourier-type frames on a full frequency cube can be implemented in essentially $\mathcal{O}(\sigma^2m^2(n+m^{1.5}))$.}

papers.title: MANTIS: Multi-Axis News Transformations for Instance-Wise Stress Testing and Worst-Case Training in Fake News Detection
papers.abstract: Automated fake news detection is vital on social media, where fake news is easily rewritten to fool detectors. However, existing approaches typically rely on superficial writing cues or single-style text rewrites, resulting in poor robustness under diverse cosmetic modifications. We construct MANTIS-Bench, a multi-axis presentation-attack benchmark that pairs original news with rewritten views across writing style, emotional expression, and dissemination framing. We further propose MANTIS, an instance-adaptive adversarial framework enabling dynamic worst-case training tailored to each news article with zero inference-time overhead. This reframes fake news defense from heuristic format smoothing into targeted, fact-invariant credibility assessment. Experiments on MANTIS-Bench show that MANTIS reduces the Union Attack Success Rate (UASR) by 3.55 percentage points relative to SheepDog on GossipCop and consistently outperforms prior single-axis defenses on Macro-F1 while maintaining competitive clean accuracy, demonstrating the effectiveness of multi-axis and instance-adaptive worst-case training.

papers.title: Differentiability and Convexity of the Solution Maps for Fully Non-linear Parabolic HJB Equations
papers.abstract: We study the dependence on the terminal condition of solutions to a fully nonlinear parabolic Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) equation, when the terminal condition varies along a finite-dimensional family. This problem is motivated by a dual formulation of semimartingale optimal transport. The equation is posed as a terminal-value Cauchy problem on an unbounded spatial domain. Under structural ellipticity and regularity assumptions on the nonlinear operator, we recall local parabolic H\"older estimates and stability results for bounded uniformly continuous terminal data. We then establish continuous directional differentiability of the solution map with respect to the finite-dimensional parameter, and identify its derivative through the corresponding linearized Cauchy problem. Under an additional convexity assumption on the Hamiltonian and a non-degeneracy condition on the terminal data, we prove local strong convexity of the point-evaluated solution map. The analysis relies on Evans--Krylov theory for fully nonlinear parabolic equations and combines PDE arguments with probabilistic representations. Finally, we extend the differentiability and convexity results to cascades of Cauchy problems in which successive equations are coupled through terminal conditions at several prescribed times. This structure is motivated, for instance, by optimal transport problems with marginal constraints imposed at several maturities.

papers.title: Making Small Code LLMs More Efficient for Secure Code Review with Neuro-Symbolic Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: As AI coding assistants generate more code, the need to review it for security flaws grows. Existing approaches leave a gap: static analyzers identify program sites but offer little explanation, while language-model explanations can be difficult to verify. Small open-weight code models could make security review available without sending proprietary code to a hosted service. We study whether fine-tuning helps these models turn security evidence into explanations that developers and tools can check. We present secSemScan, which pairs a static analyzer with a locally deployable model that writes a schema-constrained security monologue naming program sites, assigning a CWE, and giving a machine-parseable verdict. We also introduce OGSM (Oracle-Grounded Security Monologue), a dataset of 1,993 C/C\texttt{++} functions covering 22 CWEs in the taint and lifetime families. Each record pairs a function with analyzer-derived or fix-diff-derived evidence and a monologue. We fine-tune three open-weight code models in two stages, first on the output format and then on the monologue content. Because evaluation prompts supply the verdict and evidence, our results measure how well models use that information, not whether they detect vulnerabilities independently. On 355 test records, fine-tuning raised Qwen2.5-Coder-7B's verdict accuracy from 4.8\% to 96.6\%; DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B reached 78.9\%, and StarCoder2-7B reached 43.7\%. Qwen2.5-Coder-7B cited 87.5\% of Tier~1 oracle sites, and every line it cited belonged to the oracle evidence. The results suggest that fine-tuning helps small models produce more structured, evidence-linked security reasoning.

papers.title: Routing Around the Queue: An Evaluation of Eco-Routing Protocol on different Traffic Scenarios
papers.abstract: We evaluate ErouVe, a vehicular eco-routing protocol in which roadside units (RSUs) collect per-segment travel-time and CO2 reports from passing vehicles and answer route requests with the lowest-cost alternative, across a range of road architectures and traffic scenarios. We conduct the evaluation with a working implementation of the protocol inside Veins, adapted to drive SUMO's own router rather than a hand-rolled shortest-path search, on a network offering a short, signal-controlled route and a longer, signal-free bypass, under two traffic scenarios. This evaluation reveals clear strengths and weaknesses of the protocol. Under light, uncongested traffic, ErouVe's fleet-wide effect is light. Under traffic dense enough to stress the signalized route's throughput and produce a real, growing queue, the same protocol succeeds a medium fleet-wide CO2 reduction, with diverted vehicles individually saving even more fuels. We use these findings to propose three targeted corrective methods; a knowledge-gated cost-acceptance rule, a diversion-locking rule, and a distance-normalized CO2 cost function, that respectively address a cold-start knowledge asymmetry, decision flapping under noisy crowd-sourced data, and a per-second CO2 metric that rewards idling. Each of these weaknesses are generic pitfalls for any crowd-sourced routing signal and all proposed methods measurably restore protocol effectiveness.

papers.title: Thermosolutal Marangoni instabilities in a weakly viscoelastic falling film with soluble surfactant
papers.abstract: We examine the linear stability and nonlinear evolution of a heated falling film containing a soluble surfactant and a weakly viscoelastic liquid. The stress response is described by the short-memory Walters model, while surface tension depends on temperature and surface concentration. An Orr--Sommerfeld analysis and its long-wave limit determine how elastic memory and the two Marangoni stresses enter the instability threshold. A five-field weighted-residual model is then derived to describe finite-amplitude disturbances. The bulk and surface transport equations are written with compatible fluxes, which conserve their combined projected surfactant inventory in a periodic domain. The numerical examples show that solutal Marangoni stress suppresses disturbance growth and reduces the amplitude of the nonlinear waves. Thermal Marangoni stress increases the maximum growth rate, although its effect on the width of the unstable wavenumber band is different. Elastic memory changes both the onset and the finite-wavelength response. The nonlinear profiles develop a main hump and capillary ripples, accompanied by variations in bulk concentration, surface concentration, and interfacial temperature. These results describe the competition between thermocapillary forcing, surfactant redistribution and elastic stress within the retained long-wave model. The larger elastic parameters are interpreted as formal predictions of the truncated constitutive equations, rather than as a controlled extension to strongly elastic flow.

papers.title: Beyond Words Alone: Disentangling Distributed Evidence for Visually Grounded Cultural Translation
papers.abstract: Social media enables cross-lingual communication, yet the meaning of user-generated content (UGC) is often distributed across text, images, and cultural knowledge, making translation challenging. Existing evaluations typically treat images as optional and assume textual information is sufficient, obscuring whether errors stem from missing visual evidence or inadequate cultural adaptation. We introduce \textbf{Culture-MMT}, a diagnostic benchmark for \textbf{distributed-evidence pragmatic reconstruction} in social-media translation. It contains 498 curated, de-identified UGC instances across 20 domains, categorized into Symbol, Visual, and Hybrid by their required evidence. We also develop a human-aligned domain-specific judge, Judger, and a controlled evaluation framework that systematically varies the evidence available to translators. Across 17 model configurations, real images improve performance by +0.280 on Visual and +0.197 on Hybrid, but only +0.050 on Symbol, while random images provide no comparable gains. Human-authored descriptions further show that jointly dependent cases remain more challenging even when visual facts are explicit. These results characterize culturally effective social-media translation as {meaning reconstruction from distributed evidence}, highlighting visual grounding and cultural-pragmatic adaptation as distinct model bottlenecks.

papers.title: Visible Reasoning: User-Facing Decision Transparency for Generative AI Systems
papers.abstract:
Across multiple waves of computing, public trust in new technology has followed the emergence of governance mechanisms that made dominant risks legible and manageable. Generative AI shifts this pattern: these systems synthesize across heterogeneous sources, and users increasingly experience them as reasoning systems. The central question changes from "did it perform correctly?" to "can we trust how it arrived at its conclusion?"
  This paper introduces Filtered Decision Logs (FDLs), a user-facing transparency mechanism that makes decision formation visible without exposing raw chain-of-thought. FDLs pair each response with (i) a concise decision rationale, (ii) influence-ordered supporting data points derived from tool outputs, and (iii) relevance indicators showing which sources most shaped the conclusion. To operationalize evidence selection, we propose a trace-based method that reconstructs observability telemetry into a provenance tree and ranks evidence using four deterministic semantic and structural signals - Final Answer Similarity, Average Relevancy, Persistence, and Structural Proximity - combined via adaptive weighted scoring. We demonstrate FDLs across three domains: career advising (5 tools), investment analysis (4 tools), and travel planning (4 tools). In a formative evaluation with 50 participants (25 students, 25 working professionals in AI development), 92% rated the influence-ranked evidence as helpful for understanding and trusting the system's recommendation. Counterfactual tool-removal experiments confirm that removing the top-ranked source changes the answer more than removing a low-ranked source, validating that the ranking tracks decision dependence. We conclude that evidence-ranked transparency helps users identify misleading signals and missing context, enabling more confident acceptance, correction, or re-run of system decisions.

papers.title: Understanding Python Linters through a Comprehensive and Systematic Empirical Study
papers.abstract: Code linters, tools that automatically detect code issues, help developers accelerate development and improve code quality by identifying errors early. Unlike previous studies that focused mainly on single linters or informal comparisons, this paper presents the first large-scale empirical study of five widely used Python linters: Ruff, Pylint, Flake8, Mypy and Black, through four key user concerns: linting rule checks, speed, configuration methods, and linter preferences. We analyze 1,551 linting rules, categorize them into five types, and construct rule mappings, finding that more than 40% are shared between multiple linters, with Ruff and Pylint together covering over 80% of all rules. Pylint has the most rules in the first two categories, and Ruff leads in the last three. Next, we measure their running times on 1,000 GitHub projects under three setups (single-rule, default, all-rules), finding a consistent speed ranking from fastest to slowest: Ruff, Mypy, Flake8, Black, and Pylint. Ruff is extremely fast, with runtimes typically within one second. Then, we summarize four configuration methods and four types of configuration options from 443 available options across the five linters. While all linters support the four configuration methods, they differ in project configuration formats and flexibility in their configuration options. Finally, an analysis of 3,094 GitHub projects using the five linters reveals that over 50% use multiple linters, share strong consensus on option selections and rule suppressions, but exhibit project-specific variations in enabled-rule configurations. Our findings provide actionable insights for linter users and establish a benchmark dataset and taxonomy to support future research, such as cross-linter rule mapping, performance modeling, and automated configuration.

papers.title: A Mathematical Murmuration
papers.abstract: We give a summary of a large group activity presented to primary school children as part of a STEAM (STEM plus The Arts) event. We describe the routine we demonstrated, this was based upon the tutting dance form, and the murmuration of starlings. Indeed, this demonstrates movement/dance as both a viable and engaging form of teaching mathematics.

papers.title: FeatureLoop: Benchmarking Coding Agents under Evolving Requirements
papers.abstract: Software development with coding agents often begins with a rough request that users refine after trying the implementation. Final correctness alone does not capture the repeated guidance this process requires. We introduce FeatureLoop, a benchmark of 61 human-reviewed tasks from 34 repositories across five primary programming languages and seven software forms. Each task follows one development goal in a persistent workspace through evolution feedback, which adds or clarifies requirements, and completion feedback, which reports failures of stated requirements. Cumulative executable checks track new behavior, repair, and preservation of earlier functionality. We evaluate 12 frontier models and find that the strongest completes 72.1% of tasks with both feedback types. Across models, however, only 15.4% of observed failed stages recover within two corrective revisions. Further analysis reveals incomplete repairs, regressions, and model-specific differences in feedback use and token efficiency, identifying obstacles to reliable, low-intervention development.

papers.title: TP-JSCC: Efficient Token Pruning and Joint Source-Channel Coding for LVLMs-based 3D-VQA in Cloud-Edge Collaboration
papers.abstract: Deploying large vision-language models (LVLMs) on resource-constrained embodied agents for 3D visual question answering necessitates cloud-edge collaboration. However, offloading massive visual data to the cloud over bandwidth-limited and noisy channels introduces severe latency and transmission distortion. To address this, we propose TP-JSCC, an efficient token pruning and joint source-channel coding method for LVLMs-based 3D-VQA in Cloud-Edge Collaboration. First, we develop a Local and Global Semantics-based Hybrid Token Pruning (LGS-HTP) module to significantly reduce the visual token count. By decoupling foreground-background tokens and jointly selecting local and global semantics, LGS-HTP effectively reduces redundancy while preserving reasoning-critical tokens. Second, we introduce a lightweight Token Joint Source-Channel Coding (T-JSCC) module to further compress the pruned tokens and ensure their robust transmission over error-prone channels. By employing lightweight cascaded linear layers and Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR)-adaptive mechanism, this module adapts to fluctuating channel conditions while maintaining minimal computational overhead. Extensive experiments on ScanQA and SQA3D datasets indicate the exceptional efficiency and robustness of our approach. Specifically, on ScanQA validation set, the LGS-HTP module could achieve 90% pruning ratio while incurring less than a 1% CIDEr loss. Building on this, the T-JSCC further compresses the tokens by 18 times, resulting in an overall 180 times data volume reduction for robust transmission, while saving 90% in computational complexity for LVLM deployment. Our code is available at https://github.com/yuanhui0325/TP-JSCC.

papers.title: Minimax Rates for Conditional Generative Learning under Wasserstein Loss
papers.abstract: We study minimax rates for conditional generative learning under integrated Wasserstein loss, with H\"older continuous conditional laws and an unrestricted covariate distribution. We evaluate unrestricted generators through their conditional output distributions. For expected Wasserstein loss, the minimax rate agrees with the rate under uniform covariates and follows from balancing localization bias against unconditional distribution estimation error. Higher moments of the loss can instead be dominated by unobserved covariate regions, which force an additional risk contribution of order $n^{-1}$, where $n$ is the sample size. An adaptive localization argument gives matching upper bounds. The results cover unrestricted response laws and possibly vanishing Besov densities for $W_1$, and extend to higher Wasserstein orders under uniform response density bounds and integrability conditions. A multiscale lower bound closes the logarithmic gap in unconditional $W_1$ minimax rates in dimension two for both unrestricted distributions and Besov density classes. We also establish minimax rates for conditional Brenier maps under density, integrability, and uniform curvature conditions.

papers.title: S$^2$-RL: Sample-Set Dual Reinforcement Learning for Generative Semantic Segmentation Dataset Distillation
papers.abstract: While dataset distillation has witnessed significant advances in image classification, its extension to dense prediction tasks such as semantic segmentation is plagued by two core bottlenecks: bi-level optimization-based approaches suffer from prohibitive computational costs stemming from pixel-wise gradient unrolling, whereas proxy-based generative methods merely infuse visual textures into fixed semantic masks derived from real data, thus failing to condense rich semantic knowledge into a compact set of informative, novel scene generations. To address both bottlenecks simultaneously, we propose a novel Sample-Set Reinforcement Learning (S$^2$-RL) framework for generative semantic segmentation dataset distillation (SSDD). Specifically, S$^2$-RL formulates SSDD as a diffusion model based text-to-image generation paradigm, enabling flexible generation of images with informative, novel semantic distributions via a concise text prompt. Furthermore, we fine-tune a diffusion policy via Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), leveraging a sample-set dual reward paradigm: for individual samples, it enforces semantic alignment with input text prompts and intra-class feature diversity; for sample sets, it maximizes inter-sample semantic distribution diversity by solving a contextual multi-armed bandit problem. These design choices enable S$^2$-RL to distill large-scale semantic segmentation datasets into a compact set of generated samples that encapsulate diverse, informative semantic knowledge without the need of pixel-wise gradient unrolling. Extensive experiments on the ADE20K and COCO datasets demonstrate that S$^2$-RL achieves substantial and consistent improvements over state-of-the-art baselines, establishing a new benchmark for SSDD.

papers.title: Uniform large-genus asymptotics of Weil-Petersson volumes
papers.abstract: Let $V_{g,n}$ denote the Weil--Petersson volume of the moduli space of genus-$g$ hyperbolic surfaces with $n$ cusps. We obtain an asymptotic expansion in inverse powers of the genus as $g\to\infty$, uniformly for all $n\ge0$. This includes cusp counts of order $\sqrt g$ and larger, where the fixed-$n$ expansion of Mirzakhani and Zograf no longer gives a uniform approximation. The leading term is explicit and has relative error $O(g^{-1})$. Truncating the expansion at a suitably chosen order proportional to $\sqrt g$ gives relative error $O(\exp(-a\sqrt g))$ for some $a>0$, with no restriction on the growth of $n$. For fixed $n$, the leading term identifies the universal constant in the Mirzakhani--Zograf asymptotics as $1/\sqrt\pi$, as conjectured by Zograf. We also answer two questions of Mirzakhani: we determine explicit asymptotic profiles for volume ratios uniformly in the number of cusps, and for adjacent coefficient ratios of the one-boundary volume polynomial uniformly over all degrees. The proof uses a positive recursion for mixed $\kappa_1$--$\psi$ intersection numbers, with the absolute normalization determined by comparison with the known asymptotics of pure $\psi$ intersection numbers.

papers.title: Enhancing Deep Reinforcement Learning for Robotic Motion Planning via Task Decomposition
papers.abstract: Training robotic manipulation policies in simulation is widely adopted due to safety and cost efficiency; however, tasks involving obstacles remain under-performing and often converge slowly under Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL). To address this challenge, we propose a task decomposition framework for DRL that integrates Transfer Learning (TL) with Reward Redesign (RR) to improve learning efficiency and robustness in obstacle environments. The TL strategy selectively transfers only the first-layer critic parameters across structurally related tasks, since that layer captures general state--action representations while deeper layers encode reward- and obstacle-specific value geometry; RR decomposes tasks into staged sub-objectives to provide denser optimization signals. Experiments on the PyBullet Panda platform show consistent gains in obstacle settings. On Push with obstacle, our method achieves $0.83 \pm 0.05$, outperforming the strongest baseline (Truncated Quantile Critics (TQC), $0.77 \pm 0.06$) by approximately $7.8\%$. On Slide with obstacle, performance reaches $0.95 \pm 0.02$, exceeding Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) ($0.84 \pm 0.06$) by about $11\%$ success rates. In addition to higher final performance, forward transfer reduces convergence time by up to $70\%$ in obstacle tasks, and RR shortens sparse-reward Pick-and-Place training from roughly $0.75$M to $0.20$M steps ($\approx73\%$ reduction). The best policy is deployed on a real Franka Emika FR3 robot as a qualitative feasibility demonstration.

papers.title: Query Complexity of Learning Axis-Aligned Partitions
papers.abstract: This work establishes the query complexity of learning high-dimensional boxes in the exact query learning setting. Let $X \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a set of $n$ points, labeled by a collection of $k$ boxes: the label of each point in $X$ is determined by the unique box containing it. A learner aims to exactly recover the labels for every point in $X$ given access to a label oracle. We consider three increasingly-structured settings. In the most general setting, there are no conditions on the boxes, and they may overlap. We show that CAL (Cohn-Atlas-Ladner 1994), a classical active learning algorithm, is minimax-optimal with query complexity $\Theta(kd \log (n/kd))$. When the boxes are disjoint, we examine two regimes. In the large-$k$ regime, CAL remains minimax-optimal. For the constant-$k$ regime, an optimized variant of the Halving algorithm (Heged\"{u}s 1995) can beat CAL by a $\log(d)$ factor. Finally, in the most-structured settings, the boxes correspond to the leaves of a constant-sized decision tree. We prove a tight query complexity of $\Theta(d + \log n)$ that is additive in $d$ and $\log n$, generalizing a recent result (Black-Larsen-Mazumdar-Saha-So 2026) that establishes the query complexity of learning decision stumps.

papers.title: The Hidden Costs of Forgetting: A Study of Trajectory Deletion in Software Engineering Agents
papers.abstract: Software engineering agents resend their entire trajectory to an LLM at every turn, motivating online trajectory reduction. Prior work shows that randomly deleting 75% of tokens in old turns may preserve agent effectiveness, but it remains unclear why, how agents compensate for missing content, and whether it actually reduces costs. This paper presents an empirical study of 42 trajectory-reduction configurations, focusing on effectiveness, agent behavior, and cost. We systematically explore deleting content from old turns by varying the scope, granularity, amount, and timing of deletion across 9,400 runs with two state-of-the-art agents on SWE-bench Verified. We find deleting large amounts of trajectory content (e.g., up to 100% of reasoning text) can preserve overall effectiveness. Importantly, such deletion must be applied with a delay, as immediate deletion tends to significantly degrade effectiveness. Agents often compensate for deleted content by re-fetching it, increasing both the number of turns taken and the input/output tokens. Whether trajectory reduction reduces costs depends on the pricing model: Under a flat pricing model, estimated costs fall in 26 of 42 evaluations. Surprisingly, under a caching-aware pricing model, zero evaluations yield lower costs, since reducing the trajectory breaks the cached prefix billed at a lower rate. Our findings have three implications: First, token counts alone are misleading; trajectory reduction techniques must consider overall costs under a realistic pricing model. Second, analyzing trajectories is crucial to understand agent behavior, as end-to-end effectiveness hides differences such as excessive re-fetching. Finally, these results highlight the need for future work on memory management to reduce costs without sacrificing effectiveness.

papers.title: Beyond "[at]": A Large-Scale Measurement of Email Address Presentation on Computer Science Scholars' Homepages
papers.abstract: Publishing an email address makes a scholar reachable, but also exposes it to automated collection. Yet how email addresses are presented on the Web has not been measured systematically across their content, form, and location. We measure it across 32,413 homepage records of computer-science scholars listed in CSRankings with MailScope, which preserves raw and rendered HTML, extracts addresses with a three-stage cascade (rules, then large language models, then a crawling agent), and labels each address. Among 19,517 reachable homepages, we find an address for 17,712 scholars (90.8%). Our measurement yields four main findings. (i) Presentation is diverse: only 53.8% publish plain content, the others spread over 23 subtypes of symbol substitution, code, and semantic description, and 5.5% of scholars' addresses appear only after rendering. (ii) Presentation follows hosts rather than individuals: scholars on one host share a content class in 67.9% of pairs, compared with 38.8% across hosts of one institution, whereas research output and institution rank are barely related to presentation. (iii) Content and form are coupled through code-based links, and 6.2% of scholars with non-plain selected presentations have plain-text copies of the same address elsewhere. (iv) Plain addresses are more common behind passed bot challenges, and 36.1% of redirecting homepages no longer lead to scholars. Human assessment yields 94.4% weighted exact-set agreement on 143 judgeable pages, complemented by three 500-page review rounds with human verification. Presentation is diverse but clusters by shared host, and by our label-based estimate plain-string matching misses nearly half of the addresses.

papers.title: Learning Scene Coordinate Reconstruction from Unposed Images via Pose Graph Optimization
papers.abstract: Learning-based structure-from-motion methods such as ACE-Zero have demonstrated strong performance in estimating cameraposes and scene coordinates from unordered image collections without requiring ground truth supervision. However, the lack of global and multi-view consistency constraints in ACE-Zero can lead to pose drift and misalignment, particularly in complex or ambiguous scenes. In this work, we propose a hybrid framework that integrates pose graph optimization (PGO) into ACE-Zero to refine camera poses and suppress incorrect refinements. We construct pose graphs directly from ACE-Zero outputs by extracting relative pose constraints from predicted scene coordinates. Furthermore, we introduce an uncertainty-aware optimization strategy by estimating confidence scores using geometric priors, including epipolar and optical flow consistencies across views. Our approach improves the robustness and accuracy of pose estimation, demonstrating that global geometric reasoning can effectively complement learning-based inference in structure-from-motion.

papers.title: Survey on Favard length and rectifiability
papers.abstract: We overview recent results quantifying the Besicovitch projection theorem, focusing on the theory of quantitative rectifiability and connection to Vitushkin's conjecture.

papers.title: Model-independent calibration of gamma-ray bursts with Bayesian neural networks
papers.abstract:
Context. Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) extend cosmological distance measurements beyond the range densely sampled by Type Ia supernovae, but their standardization requires reliable calibration and uncertainty estimates.
  Aims. We calibrate the Amati correlation without assuming a background cosmological model, assess its stability, and examine the cosmological reach of current and future GRB Hubble diagrams.
  Methods. We train a Bayesian neural network on Pantheon+ supernovae, assess and recalibrate its predictive uncertainties, and calibrate the correlation for GRBs at $z \leq 1.5$ using the D'Agostini and Reichart likelihoods. We combine the GRB Hubble diagram with supernovae, Hubble-parameter measurements, and DESI baryon acoustic oscillations. Local-regression, covariance, leave-three-out, redshift-evolution, and Efron-Petrosian diagnostics test the standardization assumptions. We also analyse idealized future catalogues of 1500 standardized GRBs.
  Results. The diagram reaches $z \simeq 9.4$. Covariance and leave-three-out diagnostics produce small changes in the cosmological constraints. A parametric evolution coefficient is consistent with zero, whereas the truncation-corrected diagnostic indicates marginal isotropic-energy evolution that can occur along the Amati relation. Dark-energy extensions improve the phenomenological fit relative to flat $\Lambda$CDM: AIC favours the Chevallier-Polarski-Linder parametrization, while BIC favours constant-$w$ dark energy. Forecasts show strong conditional model-discrimination power under the adopted uncertainty model.
  Conclusions. GRBs provide a complementary high-redshift extension of the supernova distance ladder. Present results do not establish an evolving dark-energy equation of state. Larger homogeneous samples are promising, but realistic selection functions and calibration systematics remain essential.

papers.title: Constraint Learning by Optimizing over Trained Neural Networks: A Pragmatic Tutorial
papers.abstract: Constraint learning is an emerging paradigm of modeling optimization problems with the help of machine learning. In this paradigm, trained machine learning models are embedded into the optimization model. For example, we can learn constraints empirically from available data, or we can avoid using a nonlinear objective function by learning a simpler approximation for it. Neural networks become a compelling option if the machine learning models must capture more elaborate and nuanced relationships. However, optimization models embedding neural networks may become too large or too slow to solve. In this tutorial, we present practical considerations for an effective and efficient use of constraint learning with neural networks and validate it with a case study highlighting the benefit of smaller and sparser networks.

papers.title: A living catalog of stream interaction regions in the Parker Solar Probe era
papers.abstract: Stream interaction regions (SIRs) and corotating interaction regions (CIRs) are important phenomena in heliospheric physics. These large-scale structures vary temporally and spatially, both in latitude and with radial distance. The additions of Parker Solar Probe (PSP) and Solar Orbiter have allowed for investigations into the radial evolution of these structures over a wide range of heliocentric distances for the first time since the Helios era. To better enable investigations of SIRs and CIRs within the inner heliosphere, we have developed a living catalog of SIR and CIR observations by Parker Solar Probe with corresponding observations by STEREO-A as well as ACE and Wind at 1 au. The methodology used for the identification of events and the generation of this catalog, the initial catalog of PSP observations spanning orbits one through five along with corresponding 1 au observations, and information on accessing the living catalog for future studies is described. This list of SIR and CIR events from PSP and corresponding observations from other heliophysics missions will enable case studies utilizing unique orbital arrangements, as well as aid in future statistical studies to further understand the properties and evolution of these structures.

papers.title: Maximization of nuclear fusion reactivity via optimal energy distributions
papers.abstract: We investigate the optimization of nuclear fusion reactivity relative to the choice of energy probability distribution. A single Maxwell-Boltzmann (MB) distribution is found to be optimal in the region where reactivity is a concave function of the average available kinetic energy, specifically near the reactivity peak. Conversely, in regions where the reactivity curve is convex, optimization is achieved through a bimodal MB distribution. We then discuss our results in the context of three classes of generalized energy distributions (superstatistics), which are modeled as a continuum of MB distributions. As expected, in all cases examined, the reactivity gains provided by superstatistics are bounded by the proposed optimal distribution. Finally, we apply these findings to deuterium-deuterium and deuterium-tritium fusion processes using empirical parametrizations of their respective cross sections. For both reactions, employing optimal bimodal MB distributions at low average energies-of particular interest for magnetically confined plasmas-yields a reactivity enhancement of approximately a factor of 2.

papers.title: Escaping cells dilute CRISPR screen responses unequally across cell types
papers.abstract: Single-cell CRISPR screens run in many cell types are used to compare how cell types respond to perturbation, to train models that transfer effects between them and to score such models. These uses assume that cells carrying a guide RNA had their target knocked down. Yet cells grow for days before sequencing: when an essential gene is knocked down, knocked-down cells are depleted or stop dividing while cells that escaped knockdown keep growing, and the measured response, an average over all cells carrying the guide, is diluted. We define the escape fraction of a perturbation as the share of its measured cells whose target was not effectively knocked down, and estimate it from each cell's counts of the targeted gene with a two-group mixture that recovers known fractions in simulated mixtures. In most cell types the escape fraction rises with how essential the gene is, it is higher in a later screen of the same cells, and it reaches about half of the measured cells in human embryonic stem cells (hESCs). It predicts how much each response is diluted: the response size falls to (1 - e)^2 of that of the knocked-down cells. Because the escape fraction differs between cell types, it changes all three uses: hESCs respond like K562 cells unless knockdown depletes them, the coefficient a simple transfer model learns is lowered by the dilution of the cell type it predicts, and a benchmark scored on all cells rewards predictions shrunk towards no change, partly because that ground truth is itself diluted. Where cells stop dividing instead, the response also contains expression differences between cell-cycle stages. Response sizes should be compared on knocked-down cells or corrected for the escape fraction.

papers.title: Governing Enterprise AI Traffic at Scale: Design and Operation of a Policy-Driven, Multi-Vendor LLM Gateway on Envoy
papers.abstract: Large organizations consume large language models (LLMs) from several vendors at once, each with its own API dialect, credential model, streaming protocol and pricing. Integrated directly, this heterogeneity yields credential sprawl, format lock-in, unbounded spend and inconsistent governance. We present the design and production operation of the Cosmos LLM Gateway, the governed entry point for enterprise LLM traffic at PayPal. Built on Envoy, it splits work by latency profile: I/O-bound control decisions (authentication, credential brokering, policy and budget evaluation) run in an out-of-process external-processing service, while wire-format translation, token metering and prompt-cache shaping run in-proxy as a Rust WebAssembly filter, so that, by default, streamed response body chunks never wait on an out-of-process call. Models, providers and prices are largely validated data rather than code. Governance is declarative policy evaluated by Open Policy Agent and managed through a control plane with role-scoped authoring, approvals, pilots, shadow-mode rollout, usage notifications and versioned policy bundles. For use cases that require it, a data-loss-prevention layer can block, redact or pseudonymize detected sensitive content before it reaches a provider. Spend scopes are views over per-model usage counters, so a new budget applies to spend already recorded in its window without migration. As of September 2026, the gateway serves more than 12,000 developers and hundreds of business use cases, handling roughly 200 billion tokens per day across more than 100 models at 99.999% availability to business. In a benchmark of the core request path against a synthetic upstream, it adds a median of 4 ms and a p99 of 11 ms of overhead at more than 2,200 requests per second on two 4-vCPU instances. We report the architecture, policy model, evaluation and lessons learned.

papers.title: Symplectic singularity as hyperK\"ahler cone
papers.abstract: We prove that any symplectic singularity has a structure of hyperK\"ahler cone. In particular, it is equivalent to the vertex of a conical symplectic variety, and it is automatically K-polystable.

papers.title: Extremal Perfect Monotone Equilibria in Bayesian Games with Strategic Complementarities
papers.abstract: We study sharp bounds on equilibrium behavior in Bayesian games when players may make mistakes. Under strategic complementarities, the set of behavioral perfect equilibria has a largest and a smallest element, both in pure strategies. We ask when these bounds are monotone and how they depend on the way mistakes are made. For monotone supermodular games, we consider limits of equilibria under increasing perturbations, in the sense that conditional tremble distributions have full support and increase stochastically with type. We show that the largest and smallest perfect equilibria exist, which are pure and monotone. Under the general perfection notion, the extremal perfect equilibria continue to be monotone in the setting with finite actions. With infinite actions, the extremal perfect equilibria can be nonmonotone, and the set of perfect monotone equilibria can even lack extrema.

papers.title: MATCHA: A Chinese Multi-Disorder Mental Health Dataset with Cross-Lingual Analyses on Social Media
papers.abstract: Mental health research on social media has been dominated by English-language datasets and DSM-5-centered resources, limiting cross-lingual and cross-cultural understanding of online mental health expression. We introduce MATCHA, the first Chinese multi-disorder mental health dataset that links disorder-specific Weibo Super-Topic communities with users' broader public timelines. MATCHA covers seven DSM-5 disorders and a control group, comprising 46,025 cohort-level users and 1.8 million posts. The dataset distinguishes users with explicit self-disclosure evidence from broader disorder-related participants through an LLM-assisted annotation pipeline, and is released in a rigorously de-identified, controlled-access format. Using MATCHA, we analyze behavioral, linguistic, symptom-related, and life-event-related patterns across disorders, and conduct cross-lingual comparisons with Twitter-STMHD. Our analyses show that Weibo Super-Topics function as concentrated spaces for affective and health-related expression, while cross-platform differences between Weibo and Twitter often exceed cross-disorder variation. MATCHA provides a new resource for community-aware and cross-lingual mental health NLP research.

papers.title: Depth Improves Training-Time Scaling for Difficult Tasks in Deep Linear Networks
papers.abstract: Neural scaling laws describe the predictable power-law dependence of model performance on training time, dataset size, and model scale, with the exponents quantifying how performance changes with resources. Recent theory has shown how scaling exponents are shaped by the data distribution and the structure of the learning task, but whether network depth can improve training-time scaling has remained unsettled. Through a refined analysis of deep linear networks, we clarify that the task spectrum determines when increasing network depth improves training-time scaling. For spectrally difficult tasks, increasing depth improves the asymptotic training-time scaling exponent, whereas for easy tasks, the exponent remains independent of depth, with depth affecting only a logarithmic correction at the boundary between these regimes. Remarkably, we find that a reparameterization of time governed by the predictor norm provides a unified description of the dynamics across task difficulties. Under this reparameterization, the loss follows a common scaling law whose exponent is independent of depth. Numerical experiments on a task derived from benchmark image data and with nonlinear networks exhibit qualitatively consistent task-dependent effects of depth on training-time scaling. Our findings advance the theoretical understanding of how task structure shapes the effects of network architecture on learning and offer a basis for studying scaling behavior across broader classes of neural networks.

papers.title: HiFiPix: Bringing High-Fidelity Real-World Super-Resolution Back to Pixel Space
papers.abstract: Diffusion-based real-world image super-resolution suffers from limited reconstruction fidelity due to information loss in VAE-based latent representations. Recently, pixel-space diffusion models offer a promising high-faithfulness alternative by avoiding latent compression, but adapting them to Real-ISR remains challenging due to inherent patch boundary artifacts and degraded generative capability. To address the issues and maximize the potential of pretrained pixel-space diffusion models, we propose HiFiPix, a pixel-space Real-ISR framework capable of ultra high-fidelity reconstruction and fine-grained visual generation effects. To suppress patch boundary artifacts, we penalize unrealistic high-frequency periodic components with a Cross-Scale Wavelet Discriminator (CWSD) for image-level supervision, and Mixup Contrastive Self-Distillation (MixCSD) for intermediate representation regularization. Furthermore, we uncover a heterogeneous generation-fidelity trade-off across low-rank adapters (LoRA) and propose Selective LoRA Pruning (LoRA-SP) to adaptively prune LoRA layers, enhancing generative capability with minimal deterioration of reconstruction fidelity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that HiFiPix consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art latent space methods in terms of both restoration accuracy and perceptual quality by a large margin. Code and models will be released.

papers.title: Learning High-Quality Pseudo-Labels for Point-Supervised Temporal Action Localization
papers.abstract: Point-supervised temporal action localization (PTAL) aims to recognize and localize action instances in untrimmed videos using only point-level annotations. Existing pseudo-label-based methods have made substantial progress in PTAL. However, confidence-based initialization can overlook well-localized proposals. Meanwhile, existing methods either keep pseudo-labels fixed during detector training or update them without fully exploiting alternative boundary evidence from the original proposal pool. These limitations constrain supervision quality, thereby hindering detection performance. To learn high-quality pseudo-labels, we propose a framework that integrates prior-guided initialization with consensus-guided refinement during detector training. Our framework comprises two modules: Prior-Guided Initialization (PGI) and Consensus-Guided Refinement (CGR). PGI combines proposal confidence with point-derived priors to establish instance-specific reliability for initial pseudo-label selection and candidate retention. CGR continually uses the retained original candidates to construct boundary targets, combining their consensus with evolving detector predictions to refine pseudo-labels throughout training. Experiments on four benchmarks demonstrate that our method achieves competitive detection performance compared with existing methods. In particular, our method achieves 68.5\% average mAP over tIoU thresholds 0.1--0.7 on THUMOS14, surpassing PseR by 3.7 percentage points. Code is available at https://github.com/zhenyingfang/LHQP

papers.title: Existence of a weak solution to the Navier-Stokes equations enjoying the energy equality
papers.abstract: To date, a Leray's weak solution to the Navier-Stokes equations enjoys an energy inequality. We prove the existence of a weak solution that enjoys the energy equality. The existence of the weak solution is achieved as limit of solutions to the mollified Navier-Stokes system (Leray's approach). Since no uniqueness result is known for weak solutions we are not able to claim that any weak solution in the sense of Leray-Hopf enjoys the energy equality.

papers.title: Periodic measures for time-inhomogeneous stochastic differential equations driven by multiplicative $\alpha$-stable processes: Existence, uniqueness and numerical approximation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the periodic measures within the context of time-inhomogeneous Markov processes. By extending the Hairer--Mattingly method to the time-inhomogeneous case, we first establish the existence, uniqueness and exponential ergodicity of periodic measures for general time-periodic Markov processes. These results are subsequently applied to time-inhomogeneous stochastic differential equations under the assumption that the drift is weakly dissipative and locally Lipschitz. We further employ the truncated Euler--Maruyama scheme to study numerical approximations of the periodic measures and derive the convergence rate between the exact and discrete periodic measures. These numerical results are new even in the time-homogeneous case under the assumptions considered in this paper.

papers.title: Delayed maximum energy solar energetic particle events: Statistical analysis from Solar Orbiter
papers.abstract: Investigations of solar energetic particles (SEPs) have long utilized the dispersive nature of onset times, as in, the earlier arrival of higher-energy particles compared to lower-energy particles, to infer information such as the path length to the acceleration site at the time of initial particle release. However, recent observations by Solar Orbiter and Parker Solar Probe have begun to characterize SEP events with an apparent delay in arrival times of the higher energy portion of the particle distribution, above a critical energy separating the delayed particles from that of the typical velocity dispersion signature at lower energies. Features of these delayed maximum energy (DME) SEP events, sometimes referred to as "inverse velocity dispersion" events, could provide new insight into the impacts of magnetic connectivity to locations along an expanding coronal mass ejection-driven (CME-driven) shock wave, variations of acceleration along the shock surface, and transport effects in the inner heliosphere. This study focuses on the occurrence rate and characteristics of DME events observed by Solar Orbiter relative to their footpoint locations with respect to the initial flare site. These DME events show a bias in occurrence rate towards events when the observer's footpoints were westward of the associated flare location. Additionally, estimated locations at which the highest-energy particles of DME events are released into the flux tube suggest continued release of increasingly higher-energy particles from the CME-driven shock into the connected flux tube well into the inner heliosphere. This indicates that DME events could be attributed to inner heliospheric effects and are not actually coronal in origin. This finding is consistent with previous observations and interpretations of SEP events connected westward of the associated flare.

papers.title: PRISMA: Differentially Private Synthetic In-Car Telemetry via Differentiable Simulation
papers.abstract: Differentially private synthesis of in-car energy consumption data is challenging because the output is high-dimensional, and known lower bounds show that the privacy-utility trade-off degrades with the square root of the number of output dimensions. However, we observe that the intrinsic dimensionality of in-car energy consumption is much lower than that of the raw trace: given a small set of contextual personal variables-such as start point, end point, the car model, and the driving behavior-the consumption profile can be largely explained by publicly available map data (including elevation) combined with a physical model of vehicle energy use. We exploit this low intrinsic dimensionality in PRISMA, a Privacy-preserving In-car Synthesis and Modelling Algorithm. PRISMA involves three stages: (i) energy consumption traces are encoded into a low-dimensional latent space; (ii) the distribution of latent vectors is synthesized using the differentially private tabular data synthesis algorithm AIM, and (iii) samples drawn from this distribution are decoded back into full energy consumption traces via a differentiable physics-based simulation, a step that consumes no additional privacy budget since it uses only public information. By using a compact, physically-grounded latent representation of the traces, PRISMA significantly reduces the effective output dimension. Our experimental results show that PRISMA achieves for a competitive $\varepsilon = 0.5$ a better data synthesis performance than prior tabular and marginal-based DP synthesis baselines by preserving the diversity of the original power consumption profiles without collapsing to a small set of modes.

papers.title: Generative Structure from Motion with Native 3D Diffusion
papers.abstract: Recovering an object's 3D structure and camera motion from a few uncalibrated views is a fundamental problem in computer vision. Classical structure from motion methods recover 3D geometry consistent with the input images but cannot recover unseen regions; native generation methods produce plausible 3D objects which are related but not necessarily faithful to the input images. Methods simply concatenating reconstruction and generation allow error to cascade across the two stages, instead of producing a 3D object consistent with both the distribution and the input. We propose GenSfM, which integrates image-based 3D reconstruction with a native 3D diffusion model. In particular, we use a multi-modal diffusion transformer to jointly denoise the shape latent and per-view pose latents under shared self-attention, grounding generated geometry in the observed views while using object-level priors to infer unobserved regions. A compact 3D-native UV-volume tokenization keeps the joint sequence small as views are added, and a pose-aware stage refines geometry and texture by sampling per-voxel image features at the recovered camera poses. On Toys4k and GSO, for $4$ uncalibrated views, GenSfM improves novel-view PSNR by $3.2$-$4.5$ dB and reduces median Chamfer distance by $2.8$-$3.8\times$ over a strong native-3D generation baseline, while recovering input-view poses over $96\%$ Acc@$5^\circ$ without any external pose-estimation backbone, post-hoc optimization, or known intrinsics. Project page: https://dotb1ue.github.io/GenSfm/.

papers.title: Ranking Function Generation with LLMs for Termination
papers.abstract: Ranking functions are a fundamental technique for proving loop termination, but constructing them manually is challenging and requires substantial expertise. We propose RAINFALL, a neuro-symbolic framework which follows the generate-verify-refine paradigm and tightly integrates LLMs with symbolic verification. RAINFALL formulates ranking function synthesis as a code-completion task by inserting placeholders into the input program and constraining the LLM to fill four predefined slots for each loop. The completed program is then checked by a symbolic verifier. If verification succeeds, a valid ranking function is obtained; otherwise, the verifier's diagnostics are translated into natural-language feedback that guides iterative refinement of the LLM's output. We evaluate RAINFALL on two public benchmark suites comprising 358 terminating C programs. Using MiniMax V2.7, RAINFALL synthesizes verifiable ranking functions for 323 programs (90.22%), outperforming all promising baselines. In particular, it solves 12 more programs than PROTON 2.1, the best-performing baseline and winner of the SV-COMP 2026 Termination category. Furthermore, combining RAINFALL with PROTON 2.1 increases the success rate to 96.65% (346/358 programs). We also conduct ablation study confirming individual contributions of placeholder contracts, few-shot examples, symbolic verification, and diagnostic information feedback. Experiments across LLMs further confirm the effectiveness of RAINFALL. Our results suggest a generic, sound framework for ranking-function synthesis and, beyond termination, LLM-assisted synthesis of formally checkable liveness certificates, both of which represent new directions of software engineering research.

papers.title: Physical assumptions versus nature: the shape of the heliosphere
papers.abstract: Context. The Interstellar Probe study describes a mission concept with a launch window beginning in 2036, aiming to reach several hundred astronomical units beyond the heliopause within a time frame of at least 50 years. One of the fundamental questions related to this mission is where the boundaries of the heliosphere are and how thick they are. To answer it we need to know the shape of the heliosphere. Over the past 60 years numerous models of the heliosphere have been developed. For a long time these models depicted a heliosphere resembling a comet. Since around 2015 models have been presented that differ significantly from the shape of a comet. Aims. The aim of this paper is to emphasize that the obtained image of the heliosphere depends on the model assumptions contained in these articles. Methods. We review numerous publications examining the shape of the heliosphere. All of these articles use a magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) model of the heliosphere together with various assumptions that simplify the physics of the interaction of the solar wind flowing from the Sun with the surrounding interstellar medium. Results. The result of all these studies is a shape of the heliosphere described as either croissant-like or cometary-like, depending on the assumptions made. Conclusions. We are still uncertain which model represents the real heliosphere. Nature requires a theoretical model that is more accurate. In our opinion the interaction of the solar wind with the interstellar medium must be described by the Boltzmann system of equations using artificial intelligence. In the context of the planned space mission this conclusion is crucial.

papers.title: On generators and relations for $O_n^\circ(V)$ in higher-level Zhu algebras, Part II
papers.abstract:
We study circle relations in the higher-level Zhu algebra of a vertex operator algebra $V$. For regular vacuum words in homogeneous letters, we prove the termwise correction-residue conjecture of Part I: every correction in the one-sided iterate expansion belongs separately to the finite-length plus subspace. The first correction formed with the left truncated field vanishes identically. Multiplying the diagonal commutator kernel by a power of $1+x$ turns it into a Laurent polynomial. This proves the vanishing and writes every other correction as a finite combination of product residues with fewer $Y_L$ factors, coming from the word obtained by replacing one negative mode by a nonnegative one. These results hold at all levels $n\ge0$, without an auxiliary-degree hypothesis.
  For $n\ge1$ and a homogeneous ordered pair $(u,v)$, two explicit triangular families span the quadratic residue operators modulo the length-one and singular-iterate relations, giving $\dim\mathcal{Q}_n((u,v))\le n(n+1)$. The universal product-coefficient arrays have dimension exactly $n(n+1)$ and three natural bases; restriction to the regular mode square is an isomorphism. This proves operator spanning and gives invertible matrices for two complementary diagonal eliminations. For equal inputs, mode interchange reduces the families to their odd-indexed members, giving $\dim\mathcal{Q}_n((u,u))\le 2\lfloor (n+1)^2/4\rfloor$. The pairwise estimates give an explicit global quadratic bound for any finite homogeneous strong generating set. Heisenberg, Virasoro, and affine $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ examples illustrate equality and strict inequality in the operator bounds.

papers.title: Local Algebraic Stability of Wasserstein Gradient Descent-Ascent and Mean Field Langevin Dynamics without Spectral Gap
papers.abstract: We study the local stability of Wasserstein gradient descent-ascent (GDA) for entropy regularized two-player zero-sum games on noncompact domains. When one or both equilibrium measures fail to satisfy a Poincar\'e inequality, the spectral gap arguments underlying local exponential convergence are unavailable. we show that Wasserstein GDA converges algebraically to the mixed Nash equilibrium in chi-squared divergence, provided the initial relative density is a small perturbation in $L^2$ with bounded algebraic moments. The proof has two main ingredients: a cancellation in a negative Sobolev energy estimate, and a bootstrap argument that keeps the moments bounded uniformly in time. For polynomial-tailed equilibria, we construct perturbations supported far out in the tails that survive over diffusive time scales, which gives algebraic lower bounds on the worst-case relaxation rate. We also establish analogous local algebraic stability and lower bound results for mean-field Langevin dynamics, when the equilibrium fails to satisfy a spectral gap.

papers.title: WorldPager: Zero-Stall Tiered Memory for Long-Horizon World Models on a Single Consumer GPU
papers.abstract: Interactive world models keep the KV of past chunks as retrieval memory so that revisited places stay consistent. On a single consumer machine (one RTX 4090, 32 GiB of host memory, one NVMe SSD), long sessions with such memory hit two walls. The first is capacity: the KV of Matrix-Game 2.0 exhausts host memory after 45 seconds of video in bf16 and after 2.8 minutes in int4. The second is the model's positional horizon of 4.3 minutes. We show that this memory is capacity-bound rather than bandwidth-bound and that its access set is known before compute, because the camera pose is an input. An analytical model built on these observations predicts spill points to within one chunk and classifies zero versus non-zero stalls correctly on held-out configurations.
